column1: #mapping_set_title: HEMO cross-ontology relationships and mappings to HEO, QUDT and SBO

#mapping_set_description: Two tiers. Primary rows (mapping_tier primary) are exactly the cross-ontology annotation assertions of hemo.ttl and hemo-formulae.ttl, each reified there as an axiom with its linking kind and reason. Their predicates are HEMO annotation properties, hemo:9000001 formalises, hemo:9000026 takes input of type, hemo:9000002 is executed by task, hemo:9000007 is on measurement scale type, hemo:9000012 carries causal claim held by and hemo:9000013 takes weight of type, with predicate_type owl annotation property. Secondary rows are in this file only. They map HEMO terms and records to HEO 1.3.0 concepts, and HEMO units and quantity kinds to QUDT, with SKOS predicates read from the HEMO subject. A broad match says the object is broader than the HEMO subject and a narrow match that it is narrower, and the build checks each reason states the same direction. No row states identity and none uses skos:exactMatch. Every row carries one of the five linking kinds as the CURIE of a HEAO 0.2.0 individual, heao:4000001 definitional, heao:4000002 representational, heao:4000003 computational, heao:4000004 causal and heao:4000005 valuational. Convention. A relationship from a formula to a process, record, estimate or HEAO valuation term whose value it computes is computational, and so is one to a record type that supplies an input. One to a statistical measure whose definition it states is definitional. A HETO task executing a formula is computational. A variable's link to the RHEO record that holds its causal claim, and to the HEAO weight that supplies its value, is representational, because both ends are records and nothing is caused or valued by the link. The causal and valuational kinds are not used in this release. Mappings to HEO, QUDT and SBO describe meaning and are definitional.

#comment: Written by src/build_hemo.py and drafted by Michelle Ashley with Claude. Every row is proposed and unreviewed, so mapping_justification is semapv:UnspecifiedMatching. It becomes semapv:ManualMappingCuration with reviewer_id when a named curator signs a row off, and rejected rows are removed. Confidence is a house scale fixed by predicate, 0.9 for a primary row or a close match, 0.8 for a broad or narrow match, 0.7 for a related match, not a measured confidence. Each reason states why the row holds and then quotes both definitions, or says the object has only a label, as for QUDT units and HETO steps. Quoted HEO definitions and module descriptions are verbatim and may contain colons. object_source_version is empty for QUDT, STATO and SBO, which publish no release IRI HEMO could cite. QUDT was read from the qudt-public-repo main branch on 18 October 2026, STATO and SBO through OLS on 18 and 19 October 2026.

column2: QALYs from periods of constant utility

The module describes Option-level net monetary benefit as "Calculates the net monetary benefit of a single option at threshold lambda from that option's own expected effect and expected cost."; HEAO defines net benefit method as "A valuation method in which health and costs are placed on one scale by valuing health at a stated money value of health, or costs at the health they would buy, so that options are compared by net benefit.".

column2: Option-level net monetary benefit
column10: Calculate incremental cost-effectiveness ratios or net monetary benefit
column24: Calculating net monetary benefit applies this formula. The module describes Option-level net monetary benefit as "Calculates the net monetary benefit of a single option at threshold lambda from that option's own expected effect and expected cost."; HETO names the step Calculate incremental cost-effectiveness ratios or net monetary benefit and gives it no definition.

column2: Incremental net monetary benefit
column24: The incremental net monetary benefit values the QALY gain at lambda and subtracts the cost (HEMO-HOOK-11). The module describes Incremental net monetary benefit as "Calculates the difference in net monetary benefit between an intervention and its comparator at threshold lambda. A positive value favours the intervention in every quadrant of the cost-effectiveness plane."; HEAO defines health-money exchange as "A valuation in which health is converted into money, or money into health, by applying a monetary value of health, as in the health term of net monetary benefit or the cost term of net health benefit.".

column2: Incremental net monetary benefit
column24: A RHEO decision threshold specification states the lambda this formula takes as an input. The module describes Incremental net monetary benefit as "Calculates the difference in net monetary benefit between an intervention and its comparator at threshold lambda. A positive value favours the intervention in every quadrant of the cost-effectiveness plane."; RHEO defines decision threshold specification as "A directive information entity stating a value against which a decision maker compares the results of an economic evaluation, such as a cost-effectiveness threshold per QALY gained.".

column2: Incremental net monetary benefit
column10: Calculate incremental cost-effectiveness ratios or net monetary benefit
column24: Calculating net monetary benefit applies this formula. The module describes Incremental net monetary benefit as "Calculates the difference in net monetary benefit between an intervention and its comparator at threshold lambda. A positive value favours the intervention in every quadrant of the cost-effectiveness plane."; HETO names the step Calculate incremental cost-effectiveness ratios or net monetary benefit and gives it no definition.

column2: Pairwise dominance rule including ties
column10: Rank the options by cost and remove dominated and extendedly dominated options
column24: Removing dominated options applies this rule. The module describes Pairwise dominance rule including ties as "Classifies whether an intervention dominates its comparator: it costs no more, produces no less health and is strictly better on at least one of the two. The intervention is dominated when the same rule holds with the comparison reversed."; HETO names the step Rank the options by cost and remove dominated and extendedly dominated options and gives it no definition.

column2: Per-person EVPI from probabilistic draws
column24: The expected value of perfect information per person is the output of this formula (HEMO-HOOK-17). The module describes Per-person EVPI from probabilistic draws as "Averages, over S equally weighted draws, the highest net benefit available in each draw, the value of choosing with perfect information, and subtracts the highest expected net benefit among the options, the value of the decision made on current information. The result is the expected opportunity loss of the current decision per person and an upper bound on the value of research for that person."; HEAO defines EVPI estimate as "A value of information estimate of the expected gain in net benefit per person from resolving all uncertainty in the parameters of a decision model before choosing, equal to the expected value of the maximum net benefit across options minus the maximum of the expected net benefits.".

column2: Per-person EVPI from probabilistic draws
column24: A value of information analysis computes this expected maximum less the maximum expected net benefit. The module describes Per-person EVPI from probabilistic draws as "Averages, over S equally weighted draws, the highest net benefit available in each draw, the value of choosing with perfect information, and subtracts the highest expected net benefit among the options, the value of the decision made on current information. The result is the expected opportunity loss of the current decision per person and an upper bound on the value of research for that person."; HEAO defines value of information analysis as "A valuation in which the expected value of reducing decision uncertainty is assigned, as the expected gain in net benefit from deciding with more information, calculated from a probabilistic analysis at a stated money value of health.".

column2: Population EVPI over the decision's lifetime
column24: The population EVPI is the per-person EVPI times the discounted affected population (HEMO-HOOK-20). The module describes Population EVPI over the decision's lifetime as "Multiplies per-person EVPI by the discounted number of people expected to face the decision in each period while it remains relevant. The result is compared with the cost of research: when it is below the cost of any feasible study, further research is not worthwhile on these grounds."; HEAO defines population EVPI estimate as "A value of information estimate equal to the EVPI per person multiplied by the discounted number of people expected to be affected by the decision over its expected lifetime, which bounds the value of further research on that decision.".

column2: Incremental net health benefit at threshold k
column24: Dividing an incremental cost by a money value of a QALY gives the health forgone, a health opportunity cost valuation (HEMO-HOOK-12). The module describes Incremental net health benefit at threshold k as "Converts the incremental cost of an intervention into the health expected to be displaced elsewhere, Delta_C divided by k, and subtracts it from the incremental health gain. A positive value means population health increases overall; a negative value means the health gained does not offset the health lost from care not funded elsewhere. It gives the same decision as incremental net monetary benefit at the same threshold."; HEAO defines health opportunity cost valuation as "A health-money exchange in which a cost falling on a constrained health budget is converted into the health expected to be forgone elsewhere in that system, by dividing it by a money value of a QALY taken to reflect the marginal productivity of the budget, either an estimated supply-side threshold value or a value a decision-making body has adopted for that purpose.".

column2: Incremental net health benefit at threshold k
column24: A RHEO opportunity cost record holds the health forgone H_d. The module describes Incremental net health benefit at threshold k as "Converts the incremental cost of an intervention into the health expected to be displaced elsewhere, Delta_C divided by k, and subtracts it from the incremental health gain. A positive value means population health increases overall; a negative value means the health gained does not offset the health lost from care not funded elsewhere. It gives the same decision as incremental net monetary benefit at the same threshold."; RHEO defines opportunity cost record as "A cost record recording the value of the best alternative use forgone when a resource is used in a stated way, in money or in health (such as QALYs forgone), which names that forgone alternative as an intervention or a kind of care process.".

column2: Transition probability from a constant rate
column24: A RHEO probability estimate over one cycle is the output of this formula. The module describes Transition probability from a constant rate as "Converts a constant event rate into the probability that the event occurs within an interval of length Delta, among people at risk at the start of the interval. The function exp is the exponential function."; RHEO defines probability estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the probability that a kind of clinical event occurs, either within a stated time interval or per event, in a stated population.".

column2: Transition probability from a constant rate
column24: A RHEO event rate estimate supplies the rate h that this formula converts. The module describes Transition probability from a constant rate as "Converts a constant event rate into the probability that the event occurs within an interval of length Delta, among people at risk at the start of the interval. The function exp is the exponential function."; RHEO defines event rate estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the number of clinical events of a kind per unit of person-time in a stated population.".

column2: Transition probability from a constant rate
column10: Convert rates or survival data into transition probabilities for the model cycle
column24: Converting rates into transition probabilities for the model cycle applies this formula. The module describes Transition probability from a constant rate as "Converts a constant event rate into the probability that the event occurs within an interval of length Delta, among people at risk at the start of the interval. The function exp is the exponential function."; HETO names the step Convert rates or survival data into transition probabilities for the model cycle and gives it no definition.

column2: Constant rate from a transition probability
column10: Convert rates or survival data into transition probabilities for the model cycle
column24: Recovering a constant rate from a probability lets it be rescaled to another cycle length. The module describes Constant rate from a transition probability as "Recovers the constant rate implied by a probability observed over an interval of length Delta. The function log is the natural logarithm. The rate can then be rescaled to any cycle length or combined with a hazard ratio."; HETO names the step Convert rates or survival data into transition probabilities for the model cycle and gives it no definition.

column2: Transition probability rescaled to a new cycle length
column24: A RHEO probability estimate over one interval is rescaled to a model cycle by this formula. The module describes Transition probability rescaled to a new cycle length as "Converts a probability observed over one interval into the probability for a model cycle of a different length, under a constant hazard. It combines the two conversions above without computing the rate explicitly."; RHEO defines probability estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the probability that a kind of clinical event occurs, either within a stated time interval or per event, in a stated population.".

column2: Transition probability rescaled to a new cycle length
column10: Convert rates or survival data into transition probabilities for the model cycle
column24: Rescaling a probability to the model cycle length applies this formula. The module describes Transition probability rescaled to a new cycle length as "Converts a probability observed over one interval into the probability for a model cycle of a different length, under a constant hazard. It combines the two conversions above without computing the rate explicitly."; HETO names the step Convert rates or survival data into transition probabilities for the model cycle and gives it no definition.

column2: Absolute and relative risk reduction from a relative risk and baseline risk
column24: The relative risk RR of this formula is the STATO relative risk measure. The module describes Absolute and relative risk reduction from a relative risk and baseline risk as "Applies a relative risk, for example a pooled estimate from a meta-analysis, to an assumed comparator risk for the population of interest. The intervention risk is p_C times RR, so the ARR is p_C times the relative risk reduction 1 minus RR. For a fixed relative risk, the ARR rises in direct proportion to baseline risk: at a relative risk of 0.75 a baseline risk of 0.04 gives an ARR of 0.01, a fifth of the value at 0.20."; STATO defines relative risk as "Relative risk is a measurement datum which denotes the risk of an 'event' relative to an 'exposure'. Relative risk is calculated by forming the ratio of the probability of the event occurring in the exposed group versus the probability of this event occurring in the non-exposed group.".

column2: Relative risk of intervention to comparator
column24: A relative risk applied to a baseline probability carries the causal claim that the intervention changes the risk. RHEO holds that claim as a relative effect estimate. The module describes Relative risk of intervention to comparator as "Ratio of the intervention risk to the comparator risk."; RHEO defines relative effect estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the effect of an intervention relative to a comparator, expressed as a ratio or a difference, such as a hazard ratio or a relative risk.".

column2: Absolute and proportional QALY shortfall
column24: An OHEO absolute QALY shortfall estimate is AS. The module describes Absolute and proportional QALY shortfall as "Absolute shortfall subtracts the expected remaining QALYs of people with the condition under current care from those of the matched general population. Proportional shortfall divides the same difference by the general-population QALYs. Both look forward from the point at which the technology would be used, so health already lost does not count, and both are discounted at the reference-case rate."; OHEO defines absolute QALY shortfall estimate as "A QALY shortfall estimate expressed as the number of future QALYs lost.".

column2: Absolute and proportional QALY shortfall
column24: An OHEO proportional QALY shortfall estimate is PS. The module describes Absolute and proportional QALY shortfall as "Absolute shortfall subtracts the expected remaining QALYs of people with the condition under current care from those of the matched general population. Proportional shortfall divides the same difference by the general-population QALYs. Both look forward from the point at which the technology would be used, so health already lost does not count, and both are discounted at the reference-case rate."; OHEO defines proportional QALY shortfall estimate as "A QALY shortfall estimate expressed as the proportion of expected future QALYs lost.".

column2: Severity QALY weight from the shortfall bands
column24: The rule selects 1, 1.2 or 1.7 by whichever shortfall implies the greater severity, a value on a cut-off taking the higher level, as NICE PMG36 table 6.1 states (HEMO-HOOK-14). The module describes Severity QALY weight from the shortfall bands as "Returns the NICE severity weight from absolute and proportional shortfall. The weight is 1.7 if absolute shortfall is at least 18 or proportional shortfall at least 0.95, 1.2 if absolute shortfall is at least 12 or proportional shortfall at least 0.85, and 1 otherwise. The measure implying greater severity decides, and a value on a cut-off takes the higher band. Each comparison returns 1 when true and 0 when false."; HEAO defines severity weighting rule as "An equity weighting rule that sets the weight given to QALYs by bands of absolute and proportional QALY shortfall, applying whichever implies the greater severity.".

column2: Severity QALY weight from the shortfall bands
column24: The output w is the HEAO severity weight. The module describes Severity QALY weight from the shortfall bands as "Returns the NICE severity weight from absolute and proportional shortfall. The weight is 1.7 if absolute shortfall is at least 18 or proportional shortfall at least 0.95, 1.2 if absolute shortfall is at least 12 or proportional shortfall at least 0.85, and 1 otherwise. The measure implying greater severity decides, and a value on a cut-off takes the higher band. Each comparison returns 1 when true and 0 when false."; HEAO defines severity weight as "An equity weight applied to QALYs according to the severity of the condition, as measured by absolute or proportional QALY shortfall, such as the QALY weights of 1.2 and 1.7 in table 6.1 of the NICE manual.".

column2: Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs
column24: Multiplying each resource quantity by its unit cost and adding is resource valuation (HEMO-HOOK-08). The module describes Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs as "Multiplies the quantity of each resource used by its unit cost and adds the products over all resource types. Keeping quantities and unit costs separate shows whether a cost difference comes from different resource use or from different prices, and lets an analyst in another setting substitute local unit costs. The same sum over options gives the cost terms C_j used in the ICER and net monetary benefit."; HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method.".

column2: Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs
column24: A RHEO unit cost valuation process computes each term q_i p_i. The module describes Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs as "Multiplies the quantity of each resource used by its unit cost and adds the products over all resource types. Keeping quantities and unit costs separate shows whether a cost difference comes from different resource use or from different prices, and lets an analyst in another setting substitute local unit costs. The same sum over options gives the cost terms C_j used in the ICER and net monetary benefit."; RHEO defines unit cost valuation process as "A costing process in which the quantity of each recorded resource use, or of a recorded absence from work, is multiplied by a stated unit cost, producing one cost record for each record valued.".

column2: Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs
column24: A RHEO cost aggregation process computes the sum. The module describes Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs as "Multiplies the quantity of each resource used by its unit cost and adds the products over all resource types. Keeping quantities and unit costs separate shows whether a cost difference comes from different resource use or from different prices, and lets an analyst in another setting substitute local unit costs. The same sum over options gives the cost terms C_j used in the ICER and net monetary benefit."; RHEO defines cost aggregation process as "A costing process in which cost records are added together into a total, such as the cost of a care episode, a patient's annual cost or the cost of a programme.".

column2: Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs
column10: Multiply each resource use estimate by the unit cost of that resource
column24: Multiplying each resource use estimate by its unit cost gives the terms. The module describes Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs as "Multiplies the quantity of each resource used by its unit cost and adds the products over all resource types. Keeping quantities and unit costs separate shows whether a cost difference comes from different resource use or from different prices, and lets an analyst in another setting substitute local unit costs. The same sum over options gives the cost terms C_j used in the ICER and net monetary benefit."; HETO names the step Multiply each resource use estimate by the unit cost of that resource and gives it no definition.

column2: Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs
column10: Add the costs for each option or health state
column24: Adding the costs gives the total. The module describes Total cost from resource quantities and unit costs as "Multiplies the quantity of each resource used by its unit cost and adds the products over all resource types. Keeping quantities and unit costs separate shows whether a cost difference comes from different resource use or from different prices, and lets an analyst in another setting substitute local unit costs. The same sum over options gives the cost terms C_j used in the ICER and net monetary benefit."; HETO names the step Add the costs for each option or health state and gives it no definition.

column2: Price-year adjustment of a cost with an inflation index
column24: Revaluing a cost by the ratio of two price index values is a price year adjustment (HEMO-HOOK-09). The module describes Price-year adjustment of a cost with an inflation index as "Moves a cost observed in price year a to price year b by multiplying it by the ratio of an appropriate price index in the two years. When the index is published as annual percentage increases, as the NHS Cost Inflation Index is, the index is built by chaining: each year's value is the previous value multiplied by one plus that year's increase. The NICE manual names the NHS Cost Inflation Index and the PSS Pay and Prices Index, both reported in the Unit Costs of Health and Social Care manual, or the ONS consumer price index."; HEAO defines price year adjustment as "A monetary revaluation in which an amount of money is moved from one price year to another by applying a price index ratio, as in inflating past unit costs to the price year of an analysis.".

column2: Price-year adjustment of a cost with an inflation index
column24: A RHEO cost adjustment process that inflates a cost applies this formula. The module describes Price-year adjustment of a cost with an inflation index as "Moves a cost observed in price year a to price year b by multiplying it by the ratio of an appropriate price index in the two years. When the index is published as annual percentage increases, as the NHS Cost Inflation Index is, the index is built by chaining: each year's value is the previous value multiplied by one plus that year's increase. The NICE manual names the NHS Cost Inflation Index and the PSS Pay and Prices Index, both reported in the Unit Costs of Health and Social Care manual, or the ONS consumer price index."; RHEO defines cost adjustment process as "A costing process in which a cost record is converted to another currency, inflated or deflated to another price year, or discounted to a base year, using a stated factor.".

column2: Price-year adjustment of a cost with an inflation index
column10: Choose a unit cost for each resource and adjust it to the price year of the analysis where needed
column24: Adjusting a unit cost to the price year of the analysis applies this formula. The module describes Price-year adjustment of a cost with an inflation index as "Moves a cost observed in price year a to price year b by multiplying it by the ratio of an appropriate price index in the two years. When the index is published as annual percentage increases, as the NHS Cost Inflation Index is, the index is built by chaining: each year's value is the previous value multiplied by one plus that year's increase. The NICE manual names the NHS Cost Inflation Index and the PSS Pay and Prices Index, both reported in the Unit Costs of Health and Social Care manual, or the ONS consumer price index."; HETO names the step Choose a unit cost for each resource and adjust it to the price year of the analysis where needed and gives it no definition.

column2: Absence cost by the human capital approach
column24: Valuing all time lost at the wage rate is the human capital method (HEMO-HOOK-16). The module describes Absence cost by the human capital approach as "Values every hour of absence at the value of an hour of work. D_a counts calendar days absent, so D_a divided by 7 gives weeks absent, and multiplying by the usual weekly hours and the hourly value gives the cost. The human capital approach usually values time at gross earnings including employer-paid costs such as payroll taxes and benefits, the full cost of employee compensation."; HEAO defines human capital method as "A valuation method in which productive time lost to ill health or premature death is valued at the earnings that would have been received over the whole period lost.".

column2: Absence cost by the human capital approach
column24: The result is a productivity cost. The module describes Absence cost by the human capital approach as "Values every hour of absence at the value of an hour of work. D_a counts calendar days absent, so D_a divided by 7 gives weeks absent, and multiplying by the usual weekly hours and the hourly value gives the cost. The human capital approach usually values time at gross earnings including employer-paid costs such as payroll taxes and benefits, the full cost of employee compensation."; HEAO defines productivity cost valuation as "A resource valuation in which time lost from paid or unpaid productive activity, or reduced output at work, because of ill health or premature death is converted into money, by the human capital method or the friction cost method.".

column2: Absence cost by the friction cost method
column24: Valuing time lost only within the friction period, with an elasticity of production, is the friction cost method (HEMO-HOOK-16). The module describes Absence cost by the friction cost method as "Counts absence only up to the friction period, the time an employer needs to restore production, usually by replacing the worker, and multiplies the counted hours by the value of an hour and by the elasticity of production with respect to working time. Absences shorter than the friction period count in full. When the hourly value already allows for the elasticity, as the Dutch reference price does, e is set to 1."; HEAO defines friction cost method as "A valuation method in which productive time lost to ill health is valued only over the friction period needed to replace the absent worker and restore production.".

column2: Atkinson equally distributed equivalent health for epsilon other than 1
column24: The parameter epsilon of the Atkinson equally distributed equivalent is the HEAO relative inequality aversion parameter (HEMO-HOOK-15). The module describes Atkinson equally distributed equivalent health for epsilon other than 1 as "Gives the equally distributed equivalent health as the power mean of the n health values with exponent one minus epsilon. At epsilon of 0 it equals the arithmetic mean, so only total health counts; at epsilon of 2 it is the harmonic mean; and as epsilon rises it moves towards the health of the worst-off person, the maximin rule. Each h_i is the health of one person, or of one of n groups of equal size."; HEAO defines relative inequality aversion parameter as "An inequality aversion parameter of a relative, Atkinson, social welfare function, in which concern about inequality depends on proportional differences in health between people.".

column2: Atkinson equally distributed equivalent health for epsilon other than 1
column24: The equally distributed equivalent is the equity-weighted value of a distribution of health that the hook asks for (HEMO-HOOK-15). The module describes Atkinson equally distributed equivalent health for epsilon other than 1 as "Gives the equally distributed equivalent health as the power mean of the n health values with exponent one minus epsilon. At epsilon of 0 it equals the arithmetic mean, so only total health counts; at epsilon of 2 it is the harmonic mean; and as epsilon rises it moves towards the health of the worst-off person, the maximin rule. Each h_i is the health of one person, or of one of n groups of equal size."; HEAO defines equity weighting as "A decision modifier weighting in which health or money already valued is weighted by an equity weight, or aggregated with an inequality aversion parameter, to express a social value judgement about whose gains or losses count for more.".

column2: Atkinson inequality aversion parameter epsilon
column24: A HEAO relative inequality aversion parameter supplies epsilon. The module describes Atkinson inequality aversion parameter epsilon as "Inequality aversion parameter, zero or above and not equal to 1 in this formula. Higher values give more weight to gains at the lower end of the distribution. It is a social value judgement, not estimated from the health data; the median elicited from the public in England was 10.95."; HEAO defines relative inequality aversion parameter as "An inequality aversion parameter of a relative, Atkinson, social welfare function, in which concern about inequality depends on proportional differences in health between people.".

column2: Atkinson equally distributed equivalent health at epsilon of 1
column24: The geometric mean is the equally distributed equivalent at an inequality aversion of 1, an equity-weighted value of the distribution (HEMO-HOOK-15). The module describes Atkinson equally distributed equivalent health at epsilon of 1 as "Gives the equally distributed equivalent health when epsilon equals 1, where the general formula HE-FM-ATK-002 is undefined. The EDE is then the geometric mean of the n health values, the nth root of their product, written here as the exponential of the mean natural logarithm. The function log is the natural logarithm. It corresponds to Atkinson's logarithmic welfare function and is the limit of the general formula as epsilon tends to 1."; HEAO defines equity weighting as "A decision modifier weighting in which health or money already valued is weighted by an equity weight, or aggregated with an inequality aversion parameter, to express a social value judgement about whose gains or losses count for more.".

column2: Years lived with disability from prevalent cases and a disability weight
column24: The disability weight DW is the HEAO disability weight applied to the person-time lived with the sequela (HEMO-HOOK-05). The module describes Years lived with disability from prevalent cases and a disability weight as "Multiplies the number of people living with a sequela over one year by its disability weight, the GBD 2010 prevalence method, without age weighting or discounting. A weight of 0.05 means that 20 years lived in the state count as one year of healthy life lost. YLDs for a disease are the sum over its sequelae."; HEAO defines disability weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the loss of health in a health state on a scale on which 0 is full health and 1 is equivalent to death, used to weight time lived with disability in DALYs.".

column2: Years lived with disability from prevalent cases and a disability weight
column24: Weighting person-time with a sequela by its disability weight gives healthy years lost, a health-adjusted time valuation (HEMO-HOOK-05). The module describes Years lived with disability from prevalent cases and a disability weight as "Multiplies the number of people living with a sequela over one year by its disability weight, the GBD 2010 prevalence method, without age weighting or discounting. A weight of 0.05 means that 20 years lived in the state count as one year of healthy life lost. YLDs for a disease are the sum over its sequelae."; HEAO defines health-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which time lived, or time spent in a health state, is converted into health-adjusted time on a health value scale, such as QALYs or DALYs, by applying a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight to each period.".

column2: Disability weight of the health state
column24: A HEAO disability weight supplies DW. The module describes Disability weight of the health state as "Severity of the state on a scale from 0 (equivalent to full health) to 1 (equivalent to death)."; HEAO defines disability weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the loss of health in a health state on a scale on which 0 is full health and 1 is equivalent to death, used to weight time lived with disability in DALYs.".

column2: Disutility as a utility decrement from a stated baseline and its QALY loss over the harm's duration
column24: The decrement d is the HEAO utility decrement, subtracted from a baseline utility for the duration of the event (HEMO-HOOK-26). The module describes Disutility as a utility decrement from a stated baseline and its QALY loss over the harm's duration as "A disutility is the baseline utility without the harm minus the utility with it, both from the same instrument and value set, and the QALY loss is the decrement times the time the harm lasts. Some studies report decrements as negative numbers; here a loss is positive."; HEAO defines utility decrement as "A valuation weight that is a reduction in preference-based utility associated with an event, a treatment or a health state, applied by subtraction from a baseline utility.".

column2: Incidence-based years lived with disability for one sequela without discounting
column24: The disability weight DW is the HEAO disability weight applied to the time lived with the condition. The module describes Incidence-based years lived with disability for one sequela without discounting as "Counts the new cases of a sequela in the reference year and multiplies them by the disability weight and by the average duration of a case until remission or death, so all of each case's future health loss is assigned to the year, and the age, in which it begins. This is the form used by the GBD 1990 study and WHO's updates before 2010, here without their discounting and age weighting."; HEAO defines disability weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the loss of health in a health state on a scale on which 0 is full health and 1 is equivalent to death, used to weight time lived with disability in DALYs.".

column2: Disability weight of the sequela in an incidence-based count
column24: A HEAO disability weight supplies DW. The module describes Disability weight of the sequela in an incidence-based count as "Severity on a scale from 0 (full health) to 1 (equivalent to death)."; HEAO defines disability weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the loss of health in a health state on a scale on which 0 is full health and 1 is equivalent to death, used to weight time lived with disability in DALYs.".

column2: Discounted total of a level yearly amount counted at the end of each year
column24: The closed-form annuity is constant rate discounting of a level stream. The module describes Discounted total of a level yearly amount counted at the end of each year as "Gives the present value of the same amount q in each of T years when each year's amount is counted at the end of that year, so the first year carries the factor 1/(1 + r) and the last 1/(1 + r)^T. The fraction (1 minus (1 + r) to the power minus T) divided by r is the sum of the T yearly discount factors, the annuity form in the article's worked example. It tends to T as r falls towards zero, where the closed form itself cannot be evaluated."; HEAO defines constant rate discounting method as "A discounting method in which the discount factor for an amount t years after the base time is 1/(1+r)^t, for a constant annual discount rate r.".

column2: Discounted total of a level yearly amount counted at the end of each year
column24: A level yearly gain is discounted to a total by this closed form. The module describes Discounted total of a level yearly amount counted at the end of each year as "Gives the present value of the same amount q in each of T years when each year's amount is counted at the end of that year, so the first year carries the factor 1/(1 + r) and the last 1/(1 + r)^T. The fraction (1 minus (1 + r) to the power minus T) divided by r is the sum of the T yearly discount factors, the annuity form in the article's worked example. It tends to T as r falls towards zero, where the closed form itself cannot be evaluated."; HETO names the step Calculate discounted totals and gives it no definition.

column2: Discounted cost per QALY of a one-off treatment cost with a level yearly QALY gain
column24: A RHEO model result that is a cost per discounted QALY of a one-off treatment is computed by this ratio. The module describes Discounted cost per QALY of a one-off treatment cost with a level yearly QALY gain as "Divides an incremental cost paid entirely at the start (year 0), which discounting leaves unchanged, by the discounted total of a level yearly QALY gain counted at the end of each year, as in HE-FM-DISC-001. Only the QALYs shrink, so the ratio rises with the rate. This is the calculation behind the article's worked example."; RHEO defines model result as "A data entity produced by a model run, such as a total cost, total quality-adjusted life years or an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio, for a stated option or comparison.".

column2: Discounted cost per QALY of a one-off treatment cost with a level yearly QALY gain
column10: Calculate incremental cost-effectiveness ratios or net monetary benefit
column24: Calculating an ICER for a one-off treatment uses this ratio. The module describes Discounted cost per QALY of a one-off treatment cost with a level yearly QALY gain as "Divides an incremental cost paid entirely at the start (year 0), which discounting leaves unchanged, by the discounted total of a level yearly QALY gain counted at the end of each year, as in HE-FM-DISC-001. Only the QALYs shrink, so the ratio rises with the rate. This is the calculation behind the article's worked example."; HETO names the step Calculate incremental cost-effectiveness ratios or net monetary benefit and gives it no definition.

column2: Simple hyperbolic discount factor at a delay of t periods
column24: The simple hyperbola 1/(1 + alpha t) is the HEAO hyperbolic discounting method (HEMO-HOOK-02). The module describes Simple hyperbolic discount factor at a delay of t periods as "Gives the weight on an outcome t periods ahead under the simple hyperbola that Frederick, Loewenstein and O'Donoghue attribute to Herrnstein and to Mazur. The weight is 1 for an outcome now and falls as the delay grows, but more slowly at long delays than the constant-rate factor 1/(1 + r)^t of HE-FM-DR-001, so distant outcomes keep more weight. The parameter alpha sets how quickly the rate of impatience declines, and the per-period rate it implies is in HE-FM-HYPD-002."; HEAO defines hyperbolic discounting method as "A non-constant rate discounting method in which the implied discount rate falls continuously as the delay grows, as with a discount factor of 1/(1+at) for a parameter a.".

column2: Simple hyperbolic discount factor at a delay of t periods
column24: The hyperbolic weight is a discount factor of non-exponential form. The module describes Simple hyperbolic discount factor at a delay of t periods as "Gives the weight on an outcome t periods ahead under the simple hyperbola that Frederick, Loewenstein and O'Donoghue attribute to Herrnstein and to Mazur. The weight is 1 for an outcome now and falls as the delay grows, but more slowly at long delays than the constant-rate factor 1/(1 + r)^t of HE-FM-DR-001, so distant outcomes keep more weight. The parameter alpha sets how quickly the rate of impatience declines, and the per-period rate it implies is in HE-FM-HYPD-002."; HEAO defines discount factor as "A valuation weight equal to the present value of one unit of cost or health occurring at a stated time, derived from a discount rate and the time from the base year, such as 1/(1+r)^t under constant rate discounting.".

column2: Closed-form EVSI for two options with normal incremental net benefit
column24: The closed-form EVSI for two options with normal incremental net benefit is an EVSI estimate (HEMO-HOOK-19). The module describes Closed-form EVSI for two options with normal incremental net benefit as "Applies the unit normal loss integral to the preposterior distribution of incremental net benefit, which is normal with the prior mean m0 and the preposterior variance s2 of HE-FM-EVSI-002. EVSI is the expected gain from switching away from the option preferred now in the results that reverse the sign of the posterior mean, s times phi_z less the absolute value of m0 times Q_z, where z is the absolute prior mean in preposterior standard deviations. phi_z is the standard normal density written out with exp and sqrt, and Q_z is the standard normal upper-tail probability at z, entered from Excel's 1-NORM.S.DIST(z,TRUE) because the calculator has no normal distribution function. With s2 equal to the prior variance the same expression gives per-person EVPI under normality, the bound in HE-FM-VOI-001."; HEAO defines EVSI estimate as "A value of information estimate of the expected gain in net benefit per person from deciding after a study of stated design and sample size reports.".

column2: Population EVSI for a constant annual beneficiary population over the decision's lifetime
column24: The population EVSI is the per-person EVSI times the discounted beneficiary population (HEMO-HOOK-21). The module describes Population EVSI for a constant annual beneficiary population over the decision's lifetime as "Scales per-person EVSI to everyone whose treatment the study result would inform, N people a year for Y years, with later cohorts discounted at rate r, the population value of research in equation 15 of the second ISPOR value of information report. The factor D is the present value of one person a year in years 0 to Y minus 1, so the first cohort is not discounted, as in population EVPI (HE-FM-VOI-002), which allows a different N_t in each period. Population EVSI is the figure set against the cost of the study, and their difference, the expected net benefit of sampling, has its own package."; HEAO defines population EVSI estimate as "A value of information estimate equal to the EVSI per person multiplied by the discounted number of people expected to be affected by the decision over its expected lifetime.".

column2: Equity-weighted QALY gain summed over population groups
column24: Multiplying the QALY gain of each group by its weight is equity weighting (HEMO-HOOK-13). The module describes Equity-weighted QALY gain summed over population groups as "Multiplies the incremental QALY gain in each group by that group's equity weight to give the group's equity-weighted value, and adds these values over the groups that the programme affects. The calculator form is written for two groups, V_1 and V_2, and each further group adds one more term w_g times Delta_E_g to the sum. A weight above 1 counts each QALY gained in a priority group as more than one QALY, and a weight of 1 leaves a group's gain unchanged. The result replaces the unweighted QALY gain in the ICER and in net health benefit, so the comparison with costs follows the usual rules once the weights are fixed."; HEAO defines equity weighting as "A decision modifier weighting in which health or money already valued is weighted by an equity weight, or aggregated with an inequality aversion parameter, to express a social value judgement about whose gains or losses count for more.".

column2: Equity-weighted QALY gain summed over population groups
column24: An equity-weighted value record holds the weighted total. The module describes Equity-weighted QALY gain summed over population groups as "Multiplies the incremental QALY gain in each group by that group's equity weight to give the group's equity-weighted value, and adds these values over the groups that the programme affects. The calculator form is written for two groups, V_1 and V_2, and each further group adds one more term w_g times Delta_E_g to the sum. A weight above 1 counts each QALY gained in a priority group as more than one QALY, and a weight of 1 leaves a group's gain unchanged. The result replaces the unweighted QALY gain in the ICER and in net health benefit, so the comparison with costs follows the usual rules once the weights are fixed."; HEAO defines equity-weighted value record as "A data entity recording health or money after an equity weight has been applied, on an equity-weighted value scale, kept apart from the unweighted QALY record or cost record it was calculated from.".

column2: Equity weight on the QALY gain of one population group
column24: A HEAO equity weight supplies w_1, such as a severity weight, which HEAO places under equity weight. The module describes Equity weight on the QALY gain of one population group as "Multiplier applied to each QALY gained by the first group, 1 for no priority and above 1 for a priority group, for example 1.2 or 1.7 under the NICE severity modifier."; HEAO defines equity weight as "A decision modifier QALY weight applied according to the group, condition or circumstance of the people who gain or lose, expressing a social value judgement about distribution rather than an individual's preference for a health state.".

column2: Equity weight on the QALY gain of a second population group
column24: A HEAO equity weight supplies w_2. The module describes Equity weight on the QALY gain of a second population group as "Multiplier applied to each QALY gained by the second group, 1 when that group has no priority."; HEAO defines equity weight as "A decision modifier QALY weight applied according to the group, condition or circumstance of the people who gain or lose, expressing a social value judgement about distribution rather than an individual's preference for a health state.".

column2: DALYs for a cause as the sum of its years of life lost and years lived with disability
column24: A RHEO DALY record states the sum of years of life lost and years lived with disability. The module describes DALYs for a cause as the sum of its years of life lost and years lived with disability as "Adds the fatal and non-fatal parts of the health loss from one cause, both calculated for the same cause, sex, age group and year, as in WHO's Global Health Estimates and the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study. One DALY is one lost year of healthy life, so a death and a period of illness are counted on one scale. Each part comes from its own formula, and the DALY is their sum."; RHEO defines DALY record as "A data entity recording the disability-adjusted life years of a person or a group over a stated period, as the sum of years of life lost to premature death and years lived with disability.".

column2: DALYs for a cause as the sum of its years of life lost and years lived with disability
column24: An OHEO DALY estimate is the output of this sum. The module describes DALYs for a cause as the sum of its years of life lost and years lived with disability as "Adds the fatal and non-fatal parts of the health loss from one cause, both calculated for the same cause, sex, age group and year, as in WHO's Global Health Estimates and the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study. One DALY is one lost year of healthy life, so a death and a period of illness are counted on one scale. Each part comes from its own formula, and the DALY is their sum."; OHEO defines DALY estimate as "A health-adjusted life year estimate of health lost, equal to years of life lost to premature death plus years lived with disability.".

column2: EQ-5D-3L utility as one minus a constant, level decrements and an N3 term
column24: An additive value set is a weight function whose form is one minus a constant and the level decrements (HEMO-HOOK-03). The module describes EQ-5D-3L utility as one minus a constant, level decrements and an N3 term as "Subtracts from full health a constant for any problem at all, the decrement attached to the level reported on each of the five dimensions and a single N3 decrement when any dimension is at level 3. The decrements are zero at level 1, so state 11111 scores 1, and the constant and N3 term are each charged once whatever the number of dimensions with problems. Any value set of this form can be scored by entering its own coefficients, and HE-FM-EQ3L-002 fixes them at the UK tariff."; HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed.".

column2: EQ-5D-3L utility as one minus a constant, level decrements and an N3 term
column24: Scoring a profile with a value set applies this form. The module describes EQ-5D-3L utility as one minus a constant, level decrements and an N3 term as "Subtracts from full health a constant for any problem at all, the decrement attached to the level reported on each of the five dimensions and a single N3 decrement when any dimension is at level 3. The decrements are zero at level 1, so state 11111 scores 1, and the constant and N3 term are each charged once whatever the number of dimensions with problems. Any value set of this form can be scored by entering its own coefficients, and HE-FM-EQ3L-002 fixes them at the UK tariff."; HEAO defines preference-based index scoring as "A health state scoring in which a person's health state profile on a preference-based measure is converted into a single utility by applying a value set, without the person valuing health states themselves.".

column2: EQ-5D-3L utility as one minus a constant, level decrements and an N3 term
column24: An OHEO value set of the additive decrement form, whose coefficients stay in OHEO, is scored by this formula. The module describes EQ-5D-3L utility as one minus a constant, level decrements and an N3 term as "Subtracts from full health a constant for any problem at all, the decrement attached to the level reported on each of the five dimensions and a single N3 decrement when any dimension is at level 3. The decrements are zero at level 1, so state 11111 scores 1, and the constant and N3 term are each charged once whatever the number of dimensions with problems. Any value set of this form can be scored by entering its own coefficients, and HE-FM-EQ3L-002 fixes them at the UK tariff."; OHEO defines value set as "A multi-attribute utility function that assigns a utility to every health state of a health state classification system, estimated from preferences elicited from a stated population by a stated valuation method. Each named value set in OHEO is a class whose instances are its published releases.".

column2: Per-person EVPI as the mean opportunity loss of the current decision
column24: The mean opportunity loss is the EVPI per person (HEMO-HOOK-17). The module describes Per-person EVPI as the mean opportunity loss of the current decision as "In each draw s the opportunity loss L_s is the highest net benefit available in that draw less the net benefit, in the same draw, of the option d* chosen on current evidence. EVPI is the mean of L_s over the S equally weighted draws. Because d* is the option with the highest mean net benefit, the result equals the mean of the maxima less the maximum of the means in HE-FM-VOI-001, and it also shows which draws carry the loss. L_s is zero in every draw where d* is also the best option."; HEAO defines EVPI estimate as "A value of information estimate of the expected gain in net benefit per person from resolving all uncertainty in the parameters of a decision model before choosing, equal to the expected value of the maximum net benefit across options minus the maximum of the expected net benefits.".

column2: Two-level nested Monte Carlo EVPPI estimator from incremental net benefit
column24: The two-level nested Monte Carlo estimator gives the EVPPI estimate (HEMO-HOOK-18). The module describes Two-level nested Monte Carlo EVPPI estimator from incremental net benefit as "Draws K values of the parameters of interest theta_i in an outer loop and, for each, J values of the remaining parameters theta_c in an inner loop, averages the incremental net benefit of the new option over the inner draws and keeps the larger of that mean and zero, the value of standard care. The average of the K kept values, less the larger of zero and the mean of the inner means, estimates EVPPI for theta_i, the double-loop scheme of Brennan, Kharroubi, O'Hagan and Chilcott and of Algorithm 2 in the second ISPOR report. The calculator form is written for K = 2 outer and J = 2 inner draws, with INB_kj the run at outer draw k and inner draw j; larger loops add terms in the same pattern, as the Excel and the Computational Function do. With more than two options the maximum is taken over the inner means of every option, and Strong, Oakley and Brennan note that the value is unchanged when net benefits are expressed relative to a baseline option. When theta_i holds every parameter the inner runs at each outer draw are identical and the estimator becomes the per-person EVPI of HE-FM-VOI-001."; HEAO defines EVPPI estimate as "A value of information estimate of the expected gain in net benefit per person from resolving the uncertainty in a stated subset of parameters before choosing, with the uncertainty in the other parameters left unresolved.".

column2: Two-level nested Monte Carlo EVPPI estimator from incremental net benefit
column24: The nested Monte Carlo method computes this estimator. The module describes Two-level nested Monte Carlo EVPPI estimator from incremental net benefit as "Draws K values of the parameters of interest theta_i in an outer loop and, for each, J values of the remaining parameters theta_c in an inner loop, averages the incremental net benefit of the new option over the inner draws and keeps the larger of that mean and zero, the value of standard care. The average of the K kept values, less the larger of zero and the mean of the inner means, estimates EVPPI for theta_i, the double-loop scheme of Brennan, Kharroubi, O'Hagan and Chilcott and of Algorithm 2 in the second ISPOR report. The calculator form is written for K = 2 outer and J = 2 inner draws, with INB_kj the run at outer draw k and inner draw j; larger loops add terms in the same pattern, as the Excel and the Computational Function do. With more than two options the maximum is taken over the inner means of every option, and Strong, Oakley and Brennan note that the value is unchanged when net benefits are expressed relative to a baseline option. When theta_i holds every parameter the inner runs at each outer draw are identical and the estimator becomes the per-person EVPI of HE-FM-VOI-001."; HEAO defines nested Monte Carlo EVPPI method as "A value of information calculation method in which the EVPPI of a subset of parameters is estimated by an outer sample of those parameters and an inner sample of the remaining parameters for each outer draw.".

column2: ENBS of one study design from its population EVSI and the study cost
column24: The expected net benefit of sampling is the population EVSI less the study cost (HEMO-HOOK-22). The module describes ENBS of one study design from its population EVSI and the study cost as "Gives the net value of one proposed design of sample size n as its population EVSI less the expected total cost of the study, the definition used by the ISPOR task force. Population EVSI comes from HE-FM-EVSI-004, which multiplies the design's per-person EVSI by the discounted number of people whose treatment the result will inform, scaled in the same way as population EVPI in HE-FM-VOI-002. A positive value means the design is expected to repay its cost, and the design with the greatest value among those feasible is the efficient one (HE-CF-ENBS-001)."; HEAO defines ENBS estimate as "A value of information estimate equal to the population EVSI of a proposed study minus the expected cost of the study, which is maximised over sample sizes and allocations to choose the design of further research.".

column2: Green Book discount factor for a year under the stepped long-term schedule
column24: A product of one-year factors at the rate in force each year is the stepped declining rate method (HEMO-HOOK-23). The module describes Green Book discount factor for a year under the stepped long-term schedule as "Gives the discount factor for year t when the rate steps down after year 30 and again after year 75, the declining regime of Table 3.A of the supplementary guidance. Each band's rate compounds only over the years that fall in that band, so the factor for a year after 30 is the year-30 factor times (1 + r_2) to the power minus the years past 30. With 3.5%, 3.0% and 2.5% it reproduces the standard factors of Annex A Table A.1, 0.3459 for year 31 and 0.1468 for year 60, and with the health rates 1.5%, 1.286% and 1.071% it gives 0.4955 for year 50 as in Table A.2. For years up to 30 it is the single-amount factor of HE-FM-DR-001, and totals over a stream are in HE-CF-TPR-001."; HEAO defines stepped declining rate discounting method as "A non-constant rate discounting method in which the discount rate is constant within stated periods and lower in later periods, so that the rate steps down as the delay grows, as in long-horizon schedules for public sector appraisal.".

column2: Foreign price or cost converted to the home currency at a market exchange rate
column24: Converting at a market exchange rate is a currency conversion (HEMO-HOOK-10). The module describes Foreign price or cost converted to the home currency at a market exchange rate as "Multiplies a price or cost observed in another country's currency by the exchange rate expressed as home-currency units per unit of that currency, the p_i e_i term of the article's reference-price rule. The same step converts any cost record between currencies. A rate published the other way round, as local currency units per US dollar in the GLOBE Model final rule, is divided into the price instead. The converted prices feed the basket aggregates of HE-FM-BOC-003, and conversion at purchasing power parity is HE-FM-BOC-002."; HEAO defines currency conversion as "A monetary revaluation in which an amount of money is converted from one currency to another by applying a market exchange rate or a purchasing power parity conversion factor.".

column2: Foreign price or cost converted to the home currency at a market exchange rate
column24: A RHEO currency conversion estimate supplies the exchange rate e_i. The module describes Foreign price or cost converted to the home currency at a market exchange rate as "Multiplies a price or cost observed in another country's currency by the exchange rate expressed as home-currency units per unit of that currency, the p_i e_i term of the article's reference-price rule. The same step converts any cost record between currencies. A rate published the other way round, as local currency units per US dollar in the GLOBE Model final rule, is divided into the price instead. The converted prices feed the basket aggregates of HE-FM-BOC-003, and conversion at purchasing power parity is HE-FM-BOC-002."; RHEO defines currency conversion estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the rate at which amounts in one currency or price year convert to another, such as an exchange rate or a purchasing power parity conversion factor.".

column2: Cost converted between currencies at purchasing power parity
column24: Dividing by the source PPP factor and multiplying by the target factor is a purchasing power parity conversion (HEMO-HOOK-10). The module describes Cost converted between currencies at purchasing power parity as "Divides a cost in the source currency by the source country's PPP conversion factor, which gives international dollars, and multiplies by the target country's factor, which gives the target currency. Both factors are local currency units per international dollar, so the route through international dollars follows from their units (derived here), and a target factor of 1 returns international dollars. The World Bank describes PPPs as eliminating differences in price levels between countries in the process of conversion, and the CCEMG-EPPI-Centre Cost Converter page notes that pure exchange-rate conversion, the market rate of HE-FM-BOC-001, does not. Where the cost also comes from another price year, the year is moved first with HE-FM-COST-002 and HE-CF-BOC-001 sets out the two orders."; HEAO defines purchasing power parity conversion as "A currency conversion in which a purchasing power parity conversion factor is applied, so that the converted amount buys the same quantity of goods and services in the target country as the original amount bought in the source country.".

column2: Computational function for discounted QALYs and cost per QALY of a one-off treatment under a chosen timing convention
column24: The computational function returns discounted QALYs and cost per QALY under a chosen timing convention. The module describes Computational function for discounted QALYs and cost per QALY of a one-off treatment under a chosen timing convention as "Takes the inputs a one-off treatment analysis usually holds, an incremental cost paid at the start, a yearly QALY gain, the number of years it lasts, an annual rate and a flag for counting each year at its start or its end, and returns the sum of the discount factors, the discounted QALYs, the discounted and undiscounted cost per QALY and the rise caused by discounting. It builds one factor for each year, so it also works at a zero rate where the closed form fails, and chains HE-FM-DISC-001 or HE-FM-DISC-002 with HE-FM-DISC-004. The inputs therefore differ from the formulas' variables, which assume one timing convention and a positive rate."; HETO names the step Calculate discounted totals and gives it no definition.

column2: Kolm equally distributed equivalent health with absolute inequality aversion
column24: The parameter a is the HEAO absolute inequality aversion parameter (HEMO-HOOK-24). HEMO defines Kolm equally distributed equivalent health with absolute inequality aversion as "Gives the level of health which, if everyone had it, would be judged as good as the actual distribution, when concern for inequality depends on absolute differences in health between people."; HEAO defines absolute inequality aversion parameter as "An inequality aversion parameter of an absolute, Kolm, social welfare function, in which concern about inequality depends on absolute differences in health between people.".

column2: Kolm equally distributed equivalent health with absolute inequality aversion
column24: The equally distributed equivalent is the equity-weighted value of a distribution of health that the hook asks for (HEMO-HOOK-24). HEMO defines Kolm equally distributed equivalent health with absolute inequality aversion as "Gives the level of health which, if everyone had it, would be judged as good as the actual distribution, when concern for inequality depends on absolute differences in health between people."; HEAO defines equity weighting as "A decision modifier weighting in which health or money already valued is weighted by an equity weight, or aggregated with an inequality aversion parameter, to express a social value judgement about whose gains or losses count for more.".

column2: NICE size of benefit QALY weight for highly specialised technologies
column24: The rule of PMG36 table 6.2 (HEMO-HOOK-25). HEMO defines NICE size of benefit QALY weight for highly specialised technologies as "Gives the QALY weight NICE applies by size of benefit for highly specialised technologies, 1 for 10 or fewer incremental QALYs per patient over a lifetime horizon, 3 for 30 or more, and equal increments between."; HEAO defines size of benefit weighting rule as "A decision modifier rule that sets the weight given to QALYs by the size of the incremental QALY gain per patient over a lifetime horizon, such as the weights from 1 to 3 in table 6.2 of the NICE manual for highly specialised technologies.".

column2: NICE size of benefit QALY weight for highly specialised technologies
column24: The output w is the HEAO size of benefit weight. HEMO defines NICE size of benefit QALY weight for highly specialised technologies as "Gives the QALY weight NICE applies by size of benefit for highly specialised technologies, 1 for 10 or fewer incremental QALYs per patient over a lifetime horizon, 3 for 30 or more, and equal increments between."; HEAO defines size of benefit weight as "A decision modifier QALY weight applied according to the size of the incremental QALY gain per patient, such as the weight of 1 at 10 QALYs or fewer, 3 at 30 QALYs or more and equal increments between, in table 6.2 of the NICE manual.".

column2: WELLBYs from a change in life satisfaction and their money value
column24: WELLBYs value time by life satisfaction (HEMO-HOOK-27). HEMO defines WELLBYs from a change in life satisfaction and their money value as "Gives the wellbeing-adjusted life years of a change in life satisfaction on a 0 to 10 scale, held by a number of people for a number of years, and their value in money at a stated money value of a WELLBY."; HEAO defines wellbeing-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which a change in life satisfaction, measured on a 0 to 10 scale, is converted into wellbeing-adjusted life years (WELLBYs), one WELLBY being a one-point change in life satisfaction for one person for one year.".

column2: WELLBYs from a change in life satisfaction and their money value
column24: The money value of a WELLBY converts W to money. HEMO defines WELLBYs from a change in life satisfaction and their money value as "Gives the wellbeing-adjusted life years of a change in life satisfaction on a 0 to 10 scale, held by a number of people for a number of years, and their value in money at a stated money value of a WELLBY."; HEAO defines monetary value of wellbeing as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per WELLBY, used to convert wellbeing into money in social cost-benefit analysis.".

column2: Informal care cost by the proxy good method
column24: Valuing hours of informal care is an informal care valuation (HEMO-HOOK-28). HEMO defines Informal care cost by the proxy good method as "Gives the cost of informal care valued at the market price of a close substitute, such as a paid home carer, for each hour of care given."; HEAO defines informal care valuation as "A resource valuation in which the time informal carers spend giving care is converted into money, by the proxy good method, the opportunity cost method, contingent valuation or the well-being valuation method.".

column2: Informal care cost by the proxy good method
column24: The substitute's price is the proxy good. HEMO defines Informal care cost by the proxy good method as "Gives the cost of informal care valued at the market price of a close substitute, such as a paid home carer, for each hour of care given."; HEAO defines proxy good method as "A market price method in which informal care time is valued at the market price of a close substitute, such as the wage of a professional home carer.".

column2: MCDA weighted sum of three criterion values
column24: The weighted sum is the MCDA valuation (HEMO-HOOK-29). HEMO defines MCDA weighted sum of three criterion values as "Gives the overall value of an option in a multiple criteria decision analysis as the sum of its partial values on each criterion times the criterion weights, which add to 1."; HEAO defines MCDA weighted sum valuation as "A valuation in which the scores of an option on several criteria are combined into one overall value by weighting each score by its MCDA criterion weight and summing, as in the additive model of multi-criteria decision analysis.".

column2: MCDA weighted sum of three criterion values
column24: The w_j are HEAO MCDA criterion weights. HEMO defines MCDA weighted sum of three criterion values as "Gives the overall value of an option in a multiple criteria decision analysis as the sum of its partial values on each criterion times the criterion weights, which add to 1."; HEAO defines MCDA criterion weight as "A valuation weight expressing the relative importance a decision maker gives to one criterion of a multi-criteria decision analysis, used to combine the scores of an option on several criteria into one value.".

column2: MCDA weighted sum of three criterion values
column24: The v_j are values of partial value functions. HEMO defines MCDA weighted sum of three criterion values as "Gives the overall value of an option in a multiple criteria decision analysis as the sum of its partial values on each criterion times the criterion weights, which add to 1."; HEAO defines partial value function as "A weight function that converts the performance of an option on one criterion of a multi-criteria decision analysis into a score on a common value scale.".

column2: Stock balance over one period
column24: A RHEO stock measurement at the end of the period is checked against this balance. HEMO defines Stock balance over one period as "Gives the size of a stock at the end of a period, such as a waiting list, from its size at the start, the inflow and the outflow during the period."; RHEO defines stock measurement as "A measurement datum recording how many members a stock or a group had at a stated time, such as people waiting for treatment at the end of a month or beds available.".

column2: Stock balance over one period
column24: RHEO flow measurements give the inflow F_in and the outflow F_out. HEMO defines Stock balance over one period as "Gives the size of a stock at the end of a period, such as a waiting list, from its size at the start, the inflow and the outflow during the period."; RHEO defines flow measurement as "A measurement datum recording how many entities moved out of a stated origin, into a stated destination, or from one to the other, during a stated period, such as referrals added to a waiting list in a month or vaccine doses administered from a stock.".

column2: Net budget impact from patient-years on treatment
column24: RHEO projected counts of treated patients give the patient-years. HEMO defines Net budget impact from patient-years on treatment as "Gives the net budget impact of a year as the patient-years on treatment times the annual drug cost less the annual cost of the care it displaces."; RHEO defines projected count as "A data entity produced by a model run that gives the projected number of members of a group or stock at a time, or the projected number moving between two groups or stocks in a period.".

column2: Nested Monte Carlo EVPPI estimator for K outer and J inner draws
column24: The nested Monte Carlo estimator gives the EVPPI estimate (HEMO-HOOK-18). HEMO defines Nested Monte Carlo EVPPI estimator for K outer and J inner draws as "Gives the expected value of partial perfect information per person about a parameter set from a nested Monte Carlo sample of the incremental net benefit of one option over another, K outer draws of the parameters of interest and J inner draws of the others for each."; HEAO defines EVPPI estimate as "A value of information estimate of the expected gain in net benefit per person from resolving the uncertainty in a stated subset of parameters before choosing, with the uncertainty in the other parameters left unresolved.".

column2: Nested Monte Carlo EVPPI estimator for K outer and J inner draws
column24: The nested Monte Carlo method computes this estimator. HEMO defines Nested Monte Carlo EVPPI estimator for K outer and J inner draws as "Gives the expected value of partial perfect information per person about a parameter set from a nested Monte Carlo sample of the incremental net benefit of one option over another, K outer draws of the parameters of interest and J inner draws of the others for each."; HEAO defines nested Monte Carlo EVPPI method as "A value of information calculation method in which the EVPPI of a subset of parameters is estimated by an outer sample of those parameters and an inner sample of the remaining parameters for each outer draw.".

column2: QALY-weighted incremental net health benefit
column24: The health forgone Delta_C over k is a health opportunity cost valuation, set against the weighted QALY gain. HEMO defines QALY-weighted incremental net health benefit as "Gives the incremental net health benefit of an option with its QALY gain weighted by a decision modifier, such as a severity weight, at a stated money value of a QALY, as NICE asks for at GBP 25,000 and GBP 35,000 per QALY with and without the weighting."; HEAO defines health opportunity cost valuation as "A health-money exchange in which a cost falling on a constrained health budget is converted into the health expected to be forgone elsewhere in that system, by dividing it by a money value of a QALY taken to reflect the marginal productivity of the budget, either an estimated supply-side threshold value or a value a decision-making body has adopted for that purpose.".

column2: Flagship three-state Markov cohort model structure
column24: A RHEO economic model version of the demonstrator implements this structure. HEMO defines Flagship three-state Markov cohort model structure as "The equations of the three-state Stable, Progressed and Dead cohort model of the Build demonstrator, version 1.1, for one arm. Transition probabilities come from a progression probability, a relative risk of progression and death probabilities. The cohort trace is updated once a cycle, the trapezoidal half-cycle correction gives the occupancy of each cycle, and costs and QALYs are weighted by the cycle length and discounted at the start of each cycle."; RHEO defines economic model version as "An information content entity that is a fixed, identified state of an economic model, with a defined structure and set of parameters, that can be run to produce results.".

column2: Flagship three-state Markov cohort model structure
column24: The RHEO transition specification of the demonstrator states which transitions the equations allow. HEMO defines Flagship three-state Markov cohort model structure as "The equations of the three-state Stable, Progressed and Dead cohort model of the Build demonstrator, version 1.1, for one arm. Transition probabilities come from a progression probability, a relative risk of progression and death probabilities. The cohort trace is updated once a cycle, the trapezoidal half-cycle correction gives the occupancy of each cycle, and costs and QALYs are weighted by the cycle length and discounted at the start of each cycle."; RHEO defines transition specification as "A directive information entity, part of an economic model version or adopted for recording under a classification scheme version, stating which transitions between states are allowed, such as that no transition leaves the state dead, or that treatment cannot restart after it has stopped.".

column2: Flagship three-state Markov cohort model structure
column10: Implement the model calculations, including discounting
column24: Implementing the model calculations, including discounting, evaluates these equations. HEMO defines Flagship three-state Markov cohort model structure as "The equations of the three-state Stable, Progressed and Dead cohort model of the Build demonstrator, version 1.1, for one arm. Transition probabilities come from a progression probability, a relative risk of progression and death probabilities. The cohort trace is updated once a cycle, the trapezoidal half-cycle correction gives the occupancy of each cycle, and costs and QALYs are weighted by the cycle length and discounted at the start of each cycle."; HETO names the step Implement the model calculations, including discounting and gives it no definition.

column2: RR in HEMO-MS-FLAG-001
column24: The relative risk of progression carries the claim that Intervention X lowers progression. RHEO holds it as a relative effect estimate. HEMO defines RR in HEMO-MS-FLAG-001 as "Relative risk of progression applied in this arm, 1 for standard care."; RHEO defines relative effect estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the effect of an intervention relative to a comparator, expressed as a ratio or a difference, such as a hazard ratio or a relative risk.".

column2: u_S in HEMO-MS-FLAG-001
column24: A HEAO preference-based utility weight supplies u_S. HEMO defines u_S in HEMO-MS-FLAG-001 as "Utility of Stable."; HEAO defines preference-based utility weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the preference for a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, with values below 0 for states worse than dead, used to weight time lived in that state.".

column2: u_P in HEMO-MS-FLAG-001
column24: A HEAO preference-based utility weight supplies u_P.
