Notation follows the Differential Discounting article."; HEO defines Differential Discounting as "Differential discounting applies a lower annual discount rate to future health effects, such as QALYs, than to future costs in an economic evaluation.".

column2: Dirichlet distribution for one row of a transition matrix, moments, conjugate update from transition counts and beta marginals
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Dirichlet Distribution. The module describes Dirichlet distribution for one row of a transition matrix, moments, conjugate update from transition counts and beta marginals as "Treats the probabilities of moving from one health state to each of K destinations as a single uncertain vector that always adds to one, with one positive parameter per destination. The ratios of the parameters fix the means and their sum fixes the precision; observed transition counts add to a Dirichlet prior to give a Dirichlet posterior, and each component on its own follows a beta distribution. Sampling a row from normalised gamma draws is HE-FM-BETA-005 on the beta distribution page. Notation follows the Dirichlet Distribution article."; HEO defines Dirichlet Distribution as "The Dirichlet distribution is a multivariate distribution for proportions that sum to one, used for uncertain transition probabilities from a model state.".

column2: Anchor-based thresholds for a minimal clinically important difference and their use for responder shares and trial size
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Minimal Clinically Important Difference. The module describes Anchor-based thresholds for a minimal clinically important difference and their use for responder shares and trial size as "Maps a meaningful step on an external anchor, usually a patient's global rating of change, onto the score scale of an outcome measure. The between-group estimate subtracts the mean change of patients reporting no change from that of patients reporting a small change; the ROC cut-off chooses the change score that best separates anchor-improved patients from the rest; the 95 per cent limit cut-off sits above almost all unchanged patients. A threshold then gives the share of patients reaching it in each arm, and a between-group difference sets the target difference of a sample size calculation. Distribution-based yardsticks are HE-FM-DMID-001 to HE-FM-DMID-003 on the Distribution-Based MID page. Notation follows the Minimal Clinically Important Difference article."; HEO defines Minimal Clinically Important Difference as "The minimal clinically important difference (MCID) is the smallest change in an outcome score that patients perceive as important, beneficial or harmful.".

column2: Matrix root of an annual transition matrix for a shorter model cycle
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Transition Matrix. The module describes Matrix root of an annual transition matrix for a shorter model cycle as "Converts a transition matrix estimated over one interval into the matrix for a cycle n times shorter by taking the n-th root of the whole matrix, so that n short cycles reproduce the original matrix, including movements through intermediate states within the interval. Cohort propagation with a matrix is HE-FM-MM-001, the matrix exponential of a rate matrix HE-CF-CONT-001, competing exits HE-FM-TP-004 and cell-by-cell rescaling of a single probability HE-FM-TP-003. Notation follows the Transition Matrix article."; HEO defines Transition Matrix as "A transition matrix is the table of probabilities of moving between, or staying in, health states in one cycle of a Markov model, with rows summing to one.".

column2: Years lived with disability counted from incident cases or from prevalent cases of a sequela
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Years Lived with Disability. The module describes Years lived with disability counted from incident cases or from prevalent cases of a sequela as "Multiplies time spent with a non-fatal health state by its disability weight, counting the time either from the cases that begin in the reference year (all their future health loss, the GBD 1990 incidence perspective) or from everyone living with the state in the reference year (that year's health loss only, the perspective of GBD 2010 onwards and WHO's Global Health Estimates). Prevalence-based YLDs for one sequela are HE-FM-DWT-001 and their comorbidity adjustment HE-FM-DWT-004 on the disability weight page; steady-state prevalence from incidence and duration is HE-FM-XSD-002. Notation follows the Years Lived with Disability article."; HEO defines Years Lived with Disability as "Years lived with disability (YLDs) measure non-fatal health loss, usually as prevalence times disability weight; adding years of life lost gives the DALY.".

column2: Tunnel-state expansion of a cohort state-transition model
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Tunnel State. The module describes Tunnel-state expansion of a cohort state-transition model as "Maps a clinical state whose risks, costs or utilities depend on time since entry into a chain of K one-cycle tunnel states followed by a long-term state, so that a cohort model carries time in the state as well as the state itself. The expanded matrix P_tunnels is run with the cohort update s_(t+1) = s_t P of the Markov Model page (HE-FM-MM-001), which is not restated. Three existing records complete the method: tunnel probabilities from a survival curve for time since entry come from the rise in cumulative hazard across each cycle (HE-FM-CUMH-002), with the clock restarting on entry as HE-AS-CUMH-004 notes; the constant probability of a memoryless comparator calibrated to the same three-year survival is the rescaling formula HE-FM-TP-003 (p_old = 0.29344, Delta_old = 3 and Delta_new = 1 give 0.10933, as in the article); and life years from the expanded trace under a counting rule are HE-FM-CSIM-001 and HE-CF-CSIM-001. Notation follows the Tunnel State article."; HEO defines Tunnel State as "A tunnel state is one of a fixed sequence of one-cycle temporary states in a Markov model, letting risks, costs or utilities vary with time in a state.".

column2: Partitioned survival state occupancy and area-under-the-curve QALY function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Partitioned Survival Model. The module describes Partitioned survival state occupancy and area-under-the-curve QALY function as "Maps a set of survival curves that are not mutually exclusive, usually progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) for each treatment arm, to the share of the cohort in each health state over time, and then to mean time in each state and QALYs as utility-weighted areas under the curves. State membership is read from the curves rather than built from transition probabilities, which is what separates a partitioned survival model from a state transition model. Linked records cover the parts this package does not repeat: the restricted mean from a Kaplan-Meier curve (HE-FM-ADMC-003), QALYs summed over periods (HE-FM-QALY-001), discounted totals (HE-FM-DR-002), a treatment curve from a baseline curve and a hazard ratio (HE-FM-HR-003) and the continuous discount rate (HE-FM-CONT-003)."; HEO defines Partitioned Survival Model as "A partitioned survival model is a cancer economic model that uses PFS and OS curves to split a cohort into progression-free, progressed and dead states.".

column2: Discounted and episode-level occupancy of a time-homogeneous absorbing Markov chain
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Markov Chain. The module describes Discounted and episode-level occupancy of a time-homogeneous absorbing Markov chain as "Maps the transient block Q of a time-homogeneous absorbing Markov chain to the expected number of cycles spent in each transient state, either with each cycle discounted at a constant rate or split into separate episodes of a state that can be left and re-entered. The undiscounted fundamental matrix N, the expected cycles before absorption t = Nc and the absorption probabilities B = NR are HE-FM-ABS-001 and HE-FM-ABS-002, the cohort update s_(t+1) = s_t P is HE-FM-MM-001 and a cohort trace with counting weights and discounting is HE-FM-CSIM-001. Notation follows the Markov Chain article."; HEO defines Markov Chain as "A Markov chain is a random process moving between states in which the next state depends only on the current state. It underlies Markov cohort models.".

column2: Cure rate model survival and lifetime mean survival with a cure fraction
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cure Rate Model. The module describes Cure rate model survival and lifetime mean survival with a cure fraction as "Maps a cure fraction, the expected survival of the matched general population and the survival of uncured patients to all-cause survival over time and to the lifetime mean survival and QALYs that drive an appraisal. Cured patients face background mortality only; uncured patients also carry an excess hazard from the disease. The mixture form weights the two groups directly, the non-mixture form bounds the excess cumulative hazard so that relative survival falls to the cure fraction, and mean survival is the cure-fraction weighted average of the two group means. Reused, not repeated here: the all-cause hazard as background plus excess hazard HE-FM-BTH-005, the continuous discount rate log(1 plus d) HE-FM-CONT-003, the per-cycle probability from a hazard HE-FM-TP-001 and the restricted mean from a Kaplan-Meier curve HE-FM-ADMC-003. Notation follows the Cure Rate Model article."; HEO defines Cure Rate Model as "A cure rate model is a survival model that estimates the cure fraction and survival of uncured patients, used in HTA to extrapolate long-term survival.".

column2: Expected value of an uncertain cost, health outcome or model output
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Value. The module describes Expected value of an uncertain cost, health outcome or model output as "Maps the probability distribution of an uncertain quantity, such as a cost per patient, a QALY total or a model output that depends on uncertain parameters, to its probability-weighted mean, which carries the units of the quantity. The discrete form applied at chance nodes is HE-FM-CHN-001 on the chance node page, the Monte Carlo mean over probabilistic simulations is HE-FM-ENB-001 and the constant-hazard event probability used below is HE-FM-TP-001. The records here cover the cases in which the mean of a function differs from the function of the means: a product of correlated quantities, a curved output with an uncertain parameter, an event probability under a gamma-distributed hazard and the mean of a log-normal cost. Notation follows the Expected Value article."; HEO defines Expected Value as "Expected value is the probability-weighted mean of an uncertain outcome, such as a cost or QALY total, across all its possible values.".

column2: Years of life lost from deaths weighted by a loss function of age at death
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Years of Life Lost. The module describes Years of life lost from deaths weighted by a loss function of age at death as "Converts deaths from a cause into years of life lost by multiplying the deaths at each age by the years that a loss function assigns to a death at that age, then summing over ages. In the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study from 2010 onwards and in WHO's Global Health Estimates (GHE) the loss function is the remaining life expectancy at the age of death in a normative standard life table (HE-FM-YLL-001). Potential years of life lost replace it with the years from the age at death to a fixed cut-off age (HE-FM-YLL-002), and the original DALY discounted the standard years (HE-FM-YLL-003). YLLs added to years lived with disability (HE-FN-YLD-001, HE-FM-DWT-001) give DALYs. Notation follows the Years of Life Lost article."; HEO defines Years of Life Lost as "Years of life lost (YLL) measure premature mortality as deaths times standard remaining life expectancy at the age of death, the fatal part of the DALY.".

column2: Incremental utility-cost function as the inverse of an incremental cost-utility ratio
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Incremental Cost-Utility Ratio. The module describes Incremental utility-cost function as the inverse of an incremental cost-utility ratio as "Maps the incremental QALYs and the incremental cost of an intervention against one comparator to the QALYs gained per one million units of net expenditure, the form New Zealand's PHARMAC prefers to the cost per QALY. The incremental cost-utility ratio itself, ICUR = Delta_C / Delta_QALY, is HE-FM-CUA-001 and the general two-option ratio is HE-FM-ICER-001. Checks against a threshold use the incremental net monetary benefit HE-FM-NMB-002 or the incremental net health benefit HE-FM-CET-002. Notation follows the Incremental Cost-Utility Ratio article, which writes the QALY difference as Delta_Q."; HEO defines Incremental Cost-Utility Ratio as "The incremental cost-utility ratio (ICUR) is the ICER of a cost-utility analysis: extra cost over a comparator divided by extra QALYs gained.".

column2: Per-trial risk ratio input function for a pairwise meta-analysis of head-to-head trials
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Pairwise Meta-Analysis. The module describes Per-trial risk ratio input function for a pairwise meta-analysis of head-to-head trials as "Maps the event counts and arm sizes of one head-to-head trial of drug A against drug B to the risk ratio, its natural log and the variance of that log, the per-trial inputs that an inverse-variance pairwise meta-analysis of a dichotomous outcome pools. The pooling steps are existing records: the fixed-effect estimate HE-FM-ADMA-001, Cochran's Q HE-FM-ADMA-002, I-squared HE-FM-ADMA-003, the DerSimonian and Laird between-study variance HE-FM-ADMA-004 and the random-effects mean HE-FM-ADMA-005, all run in one pass by HE-CF-ADMA-001 with each trial's standard error taken as the square root of v. Applying the pooled risk ratio to a baseline risk from another source in an economic model is HE-FM-ARR-002. Notation follows the Pairwise Meta-Analysis article."; HEO defines Pairwise Meta-Analysis as "Pairwise meta-analysis is the statistical pooling of trials of the same two treatments, such as head-to-head RCTs, into one estimate of relative effect.".

column2: Bound corrections of the concentration index for binary and bounded health variables
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Concentration Index. The module describes Bound corrections of the concentration index for binary and bounded health variables as "Maps the standard concentration index of a health variable, its mean and the bounds of its measurement scale to an index whose feasible range does not depend on the mean. For a binary variable the standard index can only lie between mu minus 1 and 1 minus mu in large samples, so Wagstaff divides it by 1 minus the mean, while Erreygers multiplies it by 4 times the mean over the range of the scale, which equals 8 times the covariance of health and fractional rank over that range. The standard index itself, C = 2 cov_hr / mu, is HE-FM-HINQ-005, computed from grouped data in HE-CF-HINQ-001; the curve form by trapezoids is HE-FM-VEQ-002, the horizontal inequity index C_M minus C_N is HE-FM-HEQ-003 and the rule of 75 is HE-FM-HEQ-004. Notation follows the Concentration Index article."; HEO defines Concentration Index as "The concentration index measures socioeconomic inequality in a health variable; a negative value means it is disproportionately held by the poor.".

column2: Prevalence ratio function for cross-sectional comparisons and attributable cost inputs
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Prevalence Ratio. The module describes Prevalence ratio function for cross-sectional comparisons and attributable cost inputs as "Maps the prevalence of a condition among exposed people and among unexposed people, measured at the same time, to their ratio, and carries that ratio into the prevalence odds ratio, a population attributable fraction of prevalent cases and subgroup prevalences for cost-of-illness and budget impact work. Applying the attributable fraction to aggregate annual costs is the top-down attributable burden HE-FM-COI-002, and the attack rate ratio HE-FM-ATR-003 has the same ratio form for new cases in an outbreak. Survey-weighted prevalence and the link between prevalence, incidence and duration are HE-FM-XSD-001 and HE-FM-XSD-002. Notation follows the Prevalence Ratio article."; HEO defines Prevalence Ratio as "The prevalence ratio (PR) is the prevalence of a condition in an exposed group divided by that in an unexposed group, used to compare disease burden.".

column2: Economically justifiable price function solving the ICER for the unit price
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Economically Justifiable Price. The module describes Economically justifiable price function solving the ICER for the unit price as "Maps a cost-effectiveness threshold, the incremental QALYs per patient, the incremental cost per patient other than the new medicine's acquisition cost and the discounted number of units per patient to the highest price per unit at which the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio equals the threshold. It solves the two-option ICER of HE-FM-ICER-001 with the medicine's price as the unknown, and the same price sets the incremental net monetary benefit of HE-FM-NMB-002 to zero. The algebra matches the break-even price HE-FM-BEA-001 and, per patient, the payer's maximum price HE-FM-BARG-002; this package adds the threshold range, the NICE severity weight and the probabilistic forms used in an EJP analysis. Notation follows the Economically Justifiable Price article."; HEO defines Economically Justifiable Price as "The economically justifiable price (EJP) is the top price a manufacturer can defend on cost-effectiveness grounds at a given payer's threshold.".

column2: Last observation carried forward imputation and the bias it adds to an analysed mean
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Last Observation Carried Forward. The module describes Last observation carried forward imputation and the bias it adds to an analysed mean as "Maps a participant's last observed value to every later scheduled visit, so that the value used at visit k is the value recorded at the last completed visit d whenever k is after d, and then maps the fraction of each arm imputed this way, with the true means at the last observed visit and at the final visit, to the expected mean and between-arm difference that the completed data return. The difference between those expected values and the true final-visit values is the bias that the imputation adds. Trapezoidal QALYs reuse HE-FM-QALY-002 and the cost-effectiveness ratio reuses HE-FM-ICER-001; this package adds the mixture mean, the between-arm bias under unequal dropout and a function that carries both into incremental QALYs and the ICER."; HEO defines Last Observation Carried Forward as "Last observation carried forward (LOCF) fills missing trial follow-up values with each participant's last observed value, assuming no change after dropout.".

column2: Discounting of yearly cost and QALY streams to present-value totals
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Discounting. The module describes Discounting of yearly cost and QALY streams to present-value totals as "Maps a stream of yearly costs or QALYs, an annual discount rate, a time horizon and a timing convention to one discounted total, by multiplying each year's amount by its discount factor and adding the results. Totals for costs and for QALYs are formed separately and then compared across options, for example as an incremental cost per QALY. The present value of a single amount, the general sum over a stream and separate rates for costs and health are on the Discount Rate page (HE-FM-DR-001 to HE-FM-DR-003), and unequal rates on the Differential Discounting page (HE-FN-DDIS-001). This package adds the totals of a level yearly stream counted at the end of each year, at the start of each year and continuously, and the discounted cost per QALY of a one-off treatment with a lasting gain, as in the article's worked example."; HEO defines Discounting as "Discounting converts future costs and health effects, such as QALYs, into present values so that options with different timings can be compared.".

column2: Capital outlay annualisation function at the evaluation discount rate
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Annualisation. The module describes Capital outlay annualisation function at the evaluation discount rate as "Maps a one-off capital outlay to the equal annual sum charged in each year of the asset's useful life. Its inputs are the purchase price K, the resale or residual value S, the annual discount rate r and the useful life n, and its output is the equivalent annual cost E, set so that the present value of E over n years equals K less the present value of S. It is the inverse of present-value discounting at the same rate (HE-FN-DR-001), applied to a single capital input in economic costing, and it moves no money, unlike the annuity payment contract of HE-FN-AP-001. The same equation appears in the Cost package as HE-FM-COST-003; this package adds the zero-resale form, the comparison with straight-line depreciation and the year-by-year split of the charge. Notation follows the Annualisation article."; HEO defines Annualisation as "Annualisation is the conversion of a capital outlay into an equal yearly cost over the asset's useful life, using an annuity factor and the discount rate.".

column2: Precision-weighted regression of study effect estimates on study characteristics
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Meta-Regression. The module describes Precision-weighted regression of study effect estimates on study characteristics as "Maps the effect estimate y_i of each study in a meta-analysis, its within-study variance v_i and the study's value x_i of a characteristic such as dose, mean age or baseline risk to a regression line for the expected effect, together with the between-study variance tau2 that the characteristic leaves unexplained. Studies are weighted by the precision of their estimates, and the random-effects form adds the residual between-study variance to each study's own variance. Ratio measures enter as natural logarithms. In health technology assessment the fitted line gives the relative effect expected for the decision population instead of the average over the trials, and the slope is an association between studies, not a randomised comparison."; HEO defines Meta-Regression as "Meta-regression is a precision-weighted regression of study effect estimates on study characteristics, explaining heterogeneity in meta-analyses for HTA.".

column2: Hyperbolic discount weight function with impatience that declines with delay
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Hyperbolic Discounting. The module describes Hyperbolic discount weight function with impatience that declines with delay as "Maps a delay t, counted from the moment of choice, and the parameters of a chosen non-constant discount function to the weight placed on an outcome t periods ahead and to the per-period discount rate that the weights imply. Under the constant-rate factor of the Discount Rate page (HE-FM-DR-001), and in the stream totals of the Discounting page (HE-FN-DISC-001 and its formulas), the rate between two adjacent periods is the same at every delay, whereas the forms here let it fall as the delay grows. The package gives the simple hyperbola and its per-period rate, the generalised hyperbola of Loewenstein and Prelec, the quasi-hyperbolic beta-delta form, and a check for a preference reversal between a smaller-sooner and a larger-later outcome. Notation follows the Hyperbolic Discounting article."; HEO defines Hyperbolic Discounting as "Hyperbolic discounting is time preference in which the discount rate falls as delay grows, so plans made for later are often reversed when the time comes.".

column2: Expected value of sample information function for a proposed study design
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Value of Sample Information. The module describes Expected value of sample information function for a proposed study design as "Maps the current uncertainty about a decision model's parameters, the sampling distribution of the data a proposed study would collect and the net benefit of each option to the expected gain from choosing after the study reports rather than now. EVSI equals the expectation, over the datasets X the study could produce, of the largest posterior expected net benefit among the options, less the largest expected net benefit on current evidence, the form given as equation 10 of the second ISPOR value of information report and equation 2 of Kunst and colleagues. It replaces the perfect knowledge of a parameter subset in EVPPI (HE-FM-VOI-003) with the data of a study of stated design and size, so it is never negative and does not exceed EVPPI for the parameters the study informs or per-person EVPI (HE-FM-VOI-001). This package gives the exact form for a study with two possible results, the normal preposterior variance, closed-form EVSI for two options and population EVSI over the decision's lifetime on the basis used for population EVPI (HE-FM-VOI-002). The expected net benefit of sampling, population EVSI less the cost of the study, has its own package. Notation follows the Expected Value of Sample Information article."; HEO defines Expected Value of Sample Information as "Expected value of sample information (EVSI) is the expected net benefit gained by deciding after a specific proposed study reports instead of deciding now.".

column2: Equity-weighted QALY gain, ICER, net health benefit and switching weight function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Equity-Weighted Analysis. The module describes Equity-weighted QALY gain, ICER, net health benefit and switching weight function as "Maps the incremental QALY gain of a programme in each population group, an equity weight for each group, the incremental cost and the value placed on a QALY to the equity-weighted QALY gain, the equity-weighted ICER, the equity-weighted net health benefit and the weight at which the programme would break even. The weights act on the incremental QALYs only, while costs and the health displaced elsewhere stay unweighted, and with every weight equal to 1 the outputs reduce to the unweighted ICER (HE-FM-ICER-001) and incremental net health benefit (HE-FM-CET-002). The weights come from outside the function, for example the NICE severity weight from absolute and proportional shortfall (HE-FM-ASF-001 and HE-FM-ASF-003) or the weight implied by an Atkinson inequality aversion parameter (HE-FM-ATK-004), and neither is redrafted here. The break-even weight differs from the switching weight between two options in the weighted two-group social welfare formula of the Welfare Economics package, because it compares one programme with the health displaced by its cost. Notation follows the Equity-Weighted Analysis article."; HEO defines Equity-Weighted Analysis as "Equity-weighted analysis is a cost-effectiveness analysis in which health gains for priority groups, such as the severely ill, are weighted more heavily.".

column2: Disability-adjusted life years for a cause or a scenario from years of life lost and years lived with disability
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Disability-Adjusted Life Year. The module describes Disability-adjusted life years for a cause or a scenario from years of life lost and years lived with disability as "Maps the deaths and the non-fatal health loss from a cause, or in one scenario of an economic evaluation, to disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) by adding the years of life lost (YLL) to the years lived with disability (YLD), each calculated by its own formula. YLLs are deaths times a standard loss function of the age at death (HE-FN-YLL-001, HE-FM-YLL-001, with the discounted form HE-FM-YLL-003 and the age-group total HE-CF-YLL-001), and YLDs are prevalent cases times a disability weight (HE-FM-DWT-001) or incident cases times the weight and the duration (HE-FN-YLD-001, HE-FM-YLD-001, discounted in HE-FM-YLD-002). This package adds the sum itself, the DALYs of a cohort in one scenario, DALYs averted and cost per DALY averted between two scenarios, the continuously discounted cohort form and the DALY rate per 100,000 population. DALYs averted by a change in disability weights alone, with mortality unchanged, are HE-FM-DWT-005, and the general incremental ratio is HE-FM-ICER-001. Notation follows the Disability-Adjusted Life Year article."; HEO defines Disability-Adjusted Life Year as "The disability-adjusted life year (DALY) measures health loss by adding years of life lost to premature death and years lived with disability.".

column2: EQ-5D-3L value set scoring function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept EQ-5D-3L Value Set. The module describes EQ-5D-3L value set scoring function as "Maps an EQ-5D-3L profile, the level from 1 to 3 reported on each of mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain or discomfort and anxiety or depression, to a single utility under the coefficients of a chosen value set. The main-effects form with a constant for any departure from full health and an N3 term for any dimension at level 3 is the one Dolan used for the UK time trade-off tariff, and many of the time trade-off sets tabulated in the EuroQol reference volume follow it. It is the EQ-5D-3L counterpart of the additive 15D score in HE-FM-15D-001, and the utilities it returns are the weights in QALYs from periods of constant utility (HE-FM-QALY-001) and the baselines for utility decrements (HE-FN-DISU-001). Notation follows the EQ-5D-3L Value Set article."; HEO defines EQ-5D-3L Value Set as "EQ-5D-3L value sets are utility weights, elicited from a population's health state valuations, that score all 243 EQ-5D-3L states for QALY calculation.".

column2: Expected value of perfect information function for a single adoption decision
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Value of Perfect Information. The module describes Expected value of perfect information function for a single adoption decision as "Maps the net benefit of every option in every probabilistic draw, at a stated cost-effectiveness threshold, to the expected net benefit forgone per person by choosing on current evidence rather than with all uncertainty removed. Its inputs are the draw by option table of net benefit NB_ds and the threshold lambda, and its output is EVPI, in QALYs when net health benefit is used and in currency when net monetary benefit is used. The mean of the maxima less the maximum of the means is live in the Value of Information package as HE-FM-VOI-001, with population scaling in HE-FM-VOI-002, the partial form in HE-FM-VOI-003 and the error probability in HE-FM-CEAC-003. This package adds the opportunity-loss form, the two-option form in health units, the split of EVPI into error probability and loss when wrong, and the closed form for a normally distributed incremental net benefit. Notation follows the Expected Value of Perfect Information article."; HEO defines Expected Value of Perfect Information as "Expected value of perfect information (EVPI) is the expected gain from removing all uncertainty in a funding decision, the upper limit on research value.".

column2: Estimation of the expected value of partial perfect information from a probabilistic analysis
column10: Expected Value of Partial Perfect Information
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Value of Partial Perfect Information. The module describes Estimation of the expected value of partial perfect information from a probabilistic analysis as "Maps a decision model, or the probabilistic sample it has produced, and a chosen group of parameters of interest theta_i to an estimate of the expected value of partial perfect information (EVPPI) per person. Each estimator approximates the expected net benefit of every option given theta_i, takes the best option for each value of theta_i, averages, and subtracts the value of the best option on current information. The definition and its order of expectation and maximisation, with a discrete worked case, are on the Value of Information page (HE-FM-VOI-003), the per-person EVPI that bounds every EVPPI from the same sample is HE-FM-VOI-001, and population scaling is HE-FM-VOI-002. This package adds the estimators set out by the ISPOR Value of Information Task Force, with checks that each estimate is at least zero and no larger than the EVPI. Notation follows the Expected Value of Partial Perfect Information article."; HEO defines Expected Value of Partial Perfect Information as "Expected value of partial perfect information (EVPPI) is the expected gain in net benefit from knowing selected model parameters exactly before deciding.".

column2: Expected net benefit of sampling as population sample information less the cost of a study
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Net Benefit of Sampling. The module describes Expected net benefit of sampling as population sample information less the cost of a study as "Maps one proposed study design, through its population expected value of sample information and its expected total cost, to the expected net benefit of sampling, the net value of that study. Per-person EVPI and its population form are on the Value of Information page (HE-FM-VOI-001 and HE-FM-VOI-002), and the expected net benefit that fixes the current decision is on the Expected Net Benefit page (HE-FN-ENB-001). EVSI is defined on the EVSI page (HE-FN-EVSI-001), and population EVSI, per-person EVSI scaled by the discounted beneficiary population, is HE-FM-EVSI-004 there. This package adds ENBS for one design, the expected cost of a study with the opportunity loss to participants, the cost of waiting under only in research, the ceiling set by population EVPI and a search for the efficient sample size. Notation follows the Expected Net Benefit of Sampling article."; HEO defines Expected Net Benefit of Sampling as "Expected net benefit of sampling (ENBS) is a proposed study's population expected value of sample information minus its expected total cost.".

column2: Net benefit approach to a two-option cost-effectiveness decision and its sampling uncertainty
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Net Benefit Approach. The module describes Net benefit approach to a two-option cost-effectiveness decision and its sampling uncertainty as "Maps a threshold lambda and the differences in mean effect and mean cost between a new option and its comparator, or the per-arm trial data behind them, to incremental net benefit, whose sign gives the adoption decision, and to the sampling uncertainty around it. Option-level and incremental net monetary benefit, the maximum net monetary benefit rule and expected net benefit from simulations are on the Net Monetary Benefit and Expected Net Benefit pages (HE-FM-NMB-001 to HE-FM-NMB-003, HE-FM-ENB-001 and HE-FM-ENB-002). Incremental net health benefit at a threshold is HE-FM-CET-002, the ICER is HE-FM-ICER-001 and dominance is HE-FM-DOM-001. A normal interval for incremental net benefit built from the standard errors of the two differences is HE-FM-AN-004 with HE-CF-AN-001, its bootstrap variance is HE-FM-BSE-003, the acceptability curve and frontier are HE-FM-CEAC-001 to HE-FM-CEAC-003 and EVPI is HE-FM-VOI-001. This package adds Stinnett and Mullahy's interval for incremental net health benefit from two independent trial arms, the identity that links the sign of incremental net benefit to the ICER in each quadrant of the cost-effectiveness plane, and net-benefit regression. Notation follows the Net Benefit Approach article."; HEO defines Net Benefit Approach as "The net benefit approach is a cost-effectiveness decision framework that ranks options by net benefit at a stated threshold instead of by ratios.".

column2: Cost-effectiveness frontier from the expected costs and QALYs of mutually exclusive strategies
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness Frontier. The module describes Cost-effectiveness frontier from the expected costs and QALYs of mutually exclusive strategies as "Maps the expected total costs C_j and expected total QALYs Q_j of a set of mutually exclusive strategies, estimated for one population, perspective and time horizon, to the strategies on the cost-effectiveness frontier, the slopes of the segments joining them and, at a value λ placed on one QALY, the strategy chosen. It builds on live records and does not restate them. The dominance screen is HE-FM-DOM-001 and HE-FM-DOM-002, the extended dominance condition and the blend of neighbours are HE-FM-EXD-001 and HE-FM-EXD-002, the ratio between adjacent frontier strategies is the sequential ICER HE-FM-CEA-001 and the maximum net monetary benefit rule is HE-FM-NMB-003. This package adds the range of λ over which each frontier strategy is chosen, the net monetary benefit a strategy gives up against the frontier choice, the gradient of the IQWiG efficiency frontier and two computational functions that build the frontier for any number of strategies. Notation follows the Cost-Effectiveness Frontier article."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Frontier as "The cost-effectiveness frontier joins the strategies not ruled out by strict or extended dominance on a plot of expected cost against health effect.".

column2: Health forgone for equity, switching weight and implied inequality aversion function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Equity-Efficiency Trade-off. The module describes Health forgone for equity, switching weight and implied inequality aversion function as "Takes two options of equal cost, the population share of a worse-off and a better-off group, each group's net health gain per person under each option after the health displaced elsewhere, and each group's baseline health. It returns the total health forgone by choosing the fairer option (HE-FM-EET-001), the weight on the worse-off group's gain at which the two options tie, and the Atkinson inequality aversion that this weight implies at baseline health (HE-FM-EET-003). The weight is the switching weight w_s of the live record HE-FM-WE-004 (function HE-FN-WE-001), with each group's QALYs read as its population share times its net gain per person, and it is cited there rather than restated. It exceeds 1 by the health forgone divided by the share-weighted extra gain to the worse-off group, the link that HE-VT-EET-003 checks, and it differs from the equity switching weight HE-FM-EQWA-004, which sets one programme against the health displaced by its cost. The implied aversion inverts the live Atkinson relative weight HE-FM-ATK-004, whose test HE-VT-ATK-005 recovers epsilon from a weight. Equally distributed equivalent health itself is live as HE-FM-ATK-002 and HE-FM-ATK-003 (function HE-FN-ATK-001, computational function HE-CF-ATK-001) and is not restated, and the exact switching value of the aversion parameter, found by solving the EDE comparison numerically, belongs to the Distributional Cost-Effectiveness package. Notation follows the Equity-Efficiency Trade-off article."; HEO defines Equity-Efficiency Trade-off as "The equity-efficiency trade-off is the total health given up for a fairer distribution when the option that maximises health is not the fairest one.".

column2: Memoryless transition property of a Markov state and the sojourn-time distribution it implies
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Markov Assumption. The module describes Memoryless transition property of a Markov state and the sojourn-time distribution it implies as "Maps the state a person occupies at cycle t, the cycle itself and the path H_t before it to the probability of each next state, under the restriction that the path adds nothing once the current state and cycle are known. With a constant probability p_ii of staying in state i the restriction makes the number of cycles spent in i on one visit geometric, and in continuous time a constant exit rate makes the time spent in i exponential, so in both cases the chance of leaving does not depend on the time already spent in the state. The package gives the geometric distribution of a stay with its median, the residual-stay identity behind memorylessness with a check of a survival curve for time since entry, the exponential residual stay and median, and the gap between the discrete and continuous mean stays at the same rate. Existing records are cited and not restated. The mean episode length 1 divided by 1 minus p_jj is HE-FM-MKCH-002, the cohort update is HE-FM-MM-001 with the trace totals of HE-FN-CSIM-001 and HE-FM-CSIM-001, rate and probability conversion is HE-FN-TP-001 with HE-FM-TP-001 to HE-FM-TP-004 and HE-CF-TP-001 and HE-CF-TP-002, exponential survival and the mean 1 divided by lambda are HE-FM-BTH-003 and HE-FM-CONT-002, the fundamental matrix is HE-FM-ABS-001 with its discounted form HE-FM-MKCH-001 and HE-CF-MKCH-001, the six-month root of an annual matrix is HE-FM-TMAT-001, and relaxing the assumption with tunnel states is HE-FN-TUN-001, HE-FM-TUN-001 to HE-FM-TUN-003 and HE-CF-TUN-001. Notation follows the Markov Assumption article."; HEO defines Markov Assumption as "The Markov assumption is that the next transition in a state-transition model depends only on the current state and model time, not on earlier history.".

column2: Distributional cost-effectiveness comparison of options by social group function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Distributional Cost-Effectiveness. The module describes Distributional cost-effectiveness comparison of options by social group function as "Maps each social group's baseline health, its QALY gain from a programme, its share of the health opportunity cost and its size, together with a chosen inequality aversion, to the group's health under the programme, the change in equally distributed equivalent (EDE) health and in the Atkinson index against the comparator, the programme's quadrant on the equity-efficiency impact plane, and the inequality aversion at which two options give equal EDE health. The health opportunity cost of the incremental cost is the live record HE-FM-CET-002, and the EDE and Atkinson index of each distribution are the live records HE-FM-ATK-002, HE-FM-ATK-003, HE-CF-ATK-001 and HE-FM-ATK-001, which are cited here and not redrafted. Other inequality indices for grouped data, such as the absolute gap and the concentration index, are in HE-FN-HINQ-001, and direct equity weights on QALY gains are in HE-FN-EQWA-001. The two-group closed approximation to the switching aversion belongs to the equity-efficiency trade-off package, while the computational function here solves the EDE comparison itself for any number of groups. Notation follows the Distributional Cost-Effectiveness article."; HEO defines Distributional Cost-Effectiveness as "Distributional cost-effectiveness analysis (DCEA) is an economic evaluation showing who gains and loses health from a policy and its effect on inequality.".

column2: Social time preference rate, stepped long-term discount factors and implied individual rates for health
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Time Preference. The module describes Social time preference rate, stepped long-term discount factors and implied individual rates for health as "Maps the components of social time preference to the HM Treasury social time preference rate and its health discount rate, maps a stepped long-term schedule of rates to the discount factor for any year of an appraisal, and maps one answer to a stated choice between ill health at two dates to the constant annual rate it implies. The rates it returns feed the single-amount factor of the Discount Rate page (HE-FM-DR-001) and the stream totals of the Discounting page (HE-FN-DISC-001, HE-FM-DISC-001 to HE-FM-DISC-004 and HE-CF-DISC-001). A health rate derived from growth in the consumption value of health is HE-FM-DDIS-002 under HE-FN-DDIS-001, and the quasi-hyperbolic weight D(k) = beta lambda^k of the article is HE-FM-HYPD-004 under HE-FN-HYPD-001, so neither is repeated here. Notation follows the Time Preference article."; HEO defines Time Preference as "Time preference is the preference for benefits sooner and costs later; in health economics it is one reason future costs and QALYs are discounted.".

column2: Health social welfare function ranking distributions of health
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Social Welfare Function. The module describes Health social welfare function ranking distributions of health as "Maps the health of n people, or of n groups of equal size, and the parameters theta that state a distributional value judgement to a single social welfare value W, so that allocations can be ranked when they differ in who gains as well as in how much is gained. When W rises whenever one person's health rises and nobody's falls, every Pareto improvement raises welfare. The package gives Atkinson's isoelastic additive form for epsilon other than 1, its logarithmic form at epsilon of 1, the maximin limit, the two-group CES form of Wagstaff and the slope of its social indifference curve. The equally distributed equivalent (EDE) health that gives the same W is live as HE-FM-ATK-002 and HE-FM-ATK-003, the Atkinson index as HE-FM-ATK-001, the relative weight on a small gain as HE-FM-ATK-004 and equity-weighted QALY totals as HE-FM-EQWA-001, and HE-FM-WE-004 holds the linear two-group welfare with a switching weight; none is redrafted here. The health forgone for equity and the inequality aversion at which two options swap rank are left to the Equity-Efficiency Trade-off and Distributional Cost-Effectiveness packages. Notation follows the Social Welfare Function article."; HEO defines Social Welfare Function as "A social welfare function (SWF) combines individual health or wellbeing into overall social welfare, setting how equality is weighed against the total.".

column2: Age-weighted healthy years lost under the GBD 1990 exponential age-weight function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Age Weighting. The module describes Age-weighted healthy years lost under the GBD 1990 exponential age-weight function as "Maps an age, or a span of ages from the age at death or onset a over L years, together with the age-weight constants C and beta, the modulation constant K, a discount rate r and, for a case of illness, a disability weight DW, to the weight on a year lived at that age and to the age-weighted, discounted healthy years lost over the span. With K = 0 the age weights drop out and the result is the continuously discounted years of HE-FM-YLL-003 for a death and HE-FM-YLD-002 for an incident case, the per-death and per-case inputs of HE-FN-YLL-001, HE-FN-YLD-001 and the DALY records HE-FN-DALY-001 and HE-FM-DALY-004. The package adds the weight function and its peak, the undiscounted age-weighted years lost, the age-weighted discounted years lost per death of the original DALY, and the same expression for years lived with disability. Notation follows the Age Weighting article."; HEO defines Age Weighting as "Age weighting values a year of healthy life by the age at which it is lived, as in the original GBD DALY, which gave years in young adulthood most weight.".

column2: Interim value of information function for the stop or continue decision in an ongoing trial
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Adaptive Value of Information. The module describes Interim value of information function for the stop or continue decision in an ongoing trial as "Maps the evidence held at an interim look of an ongoing trial, the size of the remaining sample, the population whose treatment the result will inform and the cost of continuing to the expected gain from continuing the trial over stopping it now. Vervaart and colleagues define the value of extending an ongoing study as the expectation, over the further data given the data already collected, of the largest posterior expected net benefit, less the largest expected net benefit given the data so far, so the baseline is the decision that would be made on the interim evidence (their equation 2). The general EVSI is HE-FN-EVSI-001, and for normal incremental net benefit the live formulas apply with interim inputs, the interim posterior mean in place of the prior mean in the closed form of HE-FM-EVSI-003 and the interim effective sample size in place of n0 in the preposterior variance of HE-FM-EVSI-002, with population scaling as in HE-FM-EVSI-004. The interim normal update is HE-FM-BAD-001, whose precision form gives the effective sample size form of Chick and colleagues when the prior variance is the sampling variance per pair divided by n0 and the data variance is that variance divided by the pairs observed. ENBS and its cost terms are HE-FN-ENBS-001 and HE-FM-ENBS-001 to HE-FM-ENBS-003, and the interim EVPI ceiling is HE-FM-EVPI-004 at the posterior standard deviation. This package adds the one-stage comparison of continuing with stopping in the model of Chick, Forster and Pertile with a switching cost and online learning, and its computational function runs the decision for one interim look. The net gain of continuing with the participants' opportunity loss is HE-FM-ENBS-001 for the remaining pairs, with the cost of HE-FM-ENBS-002 at n equal to 2m, a variable cost of c/2 per participant, a share of one half on the arm expected to be inferior and the cost of the further analysis in place of the committed fixed cost, so it is computed in the computational function and not restated. Group sequential stopping on clinical evidence by alpha spending (HE-FN-ASP-001) is a different rule. Notation follows the Adaptive Value of Information article."; HEO defines Adaptive Value of Information as "Adaptive value of information applies VOI analysis to staged research, re-valuing further data at each interim look to decide whether to continue.".

column2: Agent state update function of an agent-based model
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Agent-Based Model. The module describes Agent state update function of an agent-based model as "Maps the state of agent i at step t, the set of agents in contact with it, the state of the environment, the intervention in force and a random input to the state of that agent at step t+1, the rule X_i(t+1) = F(X_i(t), N_i(t), E(t), A(t), U_i(t)) of the article. In an infection model the rule for a susceptible agent reduces to a per-step infection probability from its k infectious contacts, the complement of the binomial probability of no events (HE-FM-BINOM-002), followed by a comparison of the agent's own uniform random number with that probability. A per-contact probability built from a transmission rate uses the constant-rate conversion HE-FM-TP-001, and a probability observed over another interval is rescaled with HE-FM-TP-003; neither is restated here. Population outputs are averaged over independent runs, and the Monte Carlo standard error of such a mean is the standard deviation across runs divided by the square root of the number of runs, the form of HE-FM-ANTV-002 with one observation per run and the divisor of HE-FM-BSE-001. This package adds the number of runs needed for a target standard error of a mean and of a share of runs. Attack rates and the final size relation are in HE-FN-ATR-001 and HE-CF-ATR-001, the cohort simulation without interaction is HE-FN-CSIM-001, and expected onward infections and the reproduction number belong to the Basic Reproduction Number page. Notation follows the Agent-Based Model article."; HEO defines Agent-Based Model as "An agent-based model (ABM) simulates individuals as agents that follow rules and interact, so outcomes such as infections, costs and QALYs emerge.".

column2: Background mortality function for the cycle death probability of a modelled cohort
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Background Mortality. The module describes Background mortality function for the cycle death probability of a modelled cohort as "Maps the attained age of a cohort, the cycle length and a disease-specific death probability to the probability of dying of other causes in each model cycle and to the all-cause probability of death, and relates all-cause survival to the survival expected in the general population. The split of the all-cause hazard into a background and an excess hazard is live as HE-FM-BTH-005 and is not restated; the formulas here give its survival-scale form (relative survival), its cycle-probability form for two independent risks, and the expected hazard of a cohort that mixes sexes or ages. A background probability for one cycle comes from a life-table annual probability q_x through the rescaling formula HE-FM-TP-003 with an observed interval of one year (HE-CF-TP-002 performs the same step), and HE-FM-TP-004 splits a cycle's deaths between background and disease death states. A multiplier on background mortality, such as a standardised mortality ratio, enters a cycle probability in the same way as the hazard ratio of HE-FM-HR-004. Related live records cover cure models in the relative survival form (HE-FN-CRM-001 and HE-FM-CRM-001 to HE-FM-CRM-004), cycle probabilities from a cumulative hazard (HE-FN-CUMH-001, HE-FM-CUMH-001 to HE-FM-CUMH-003), general-population QALYs from a life table (HE-FM-ASF-002), the cohort trace that carries the probabilities (HE-FN-CSIM-001) and tunnel states, whose clock restarts on entry while attained age keeps running (HE-FN-TUN-001). Years of life lost (HE-FN-YLL-001) use a normative standard life table, a different purpose from the national table used here. Notation follows the Background Mortality article."; HEO defines Background Mortality as "Background mortality is the death rate a model's patients would face without the disease, usually taken from general population life tables by age and sex.".

column2: Basic reproduction number function from transmission parameters or a next-generation matrix
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Basic Reproduction Number. The module describes Basic reproduction number function from transmission parameters or a next-generation matrix as "Maps the transmission parameters of an infection in a fully susceptible population, either a transmission rate and a recovery rate or a next-generation matrix of expected new cases by group, to the basic reproduction number R_0, a count of cases per case with no time unit. The same package derives the effective reproduction number once part of the population is immune, the herd immunity threshold with the critical vaccination coverage, and the reproduction number implied by an early exponential growth rate. R_0 estimated after a completed epidemic from its final attack rate is HE-FM-ATR-005, and the final attack rate and infections averted for a given R_0 and pre-epidemic coverage are computed in HE-CF-ATR-001, so neither is restated here. Vaccine effectiveness from attack rates (HE-FM-ATR-004) supplies E, the epidemic doubling time used in HE-FM-CFR-003 converts to the growth rate r, a per-cycle recovery probability for a cohort model follows the rate conversion of HE-FN-TP-001, and the economic treatment of herd protection as an external benefit is HE-FM-EXT-002. Notation follows the Basic Reproduction Number article."; HEO defines Basic Reproduction Number as "The basic reproduction number (R0) is the average number of infections one typical case causes in a fully susceptible population, used in vaccine models.".

column2: Basket-of-countries reference price and currency conversion function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Basket of Countries. The module describes Basket-of-countries reference price and currency conversion function as "Maps the prices of one medicine observed in a basket of reference countries, each in its own currency, and the exchange rates or purchasing power parities that express them in one currency, to a domestic reference price under an aggregation rule and to a ceiling for a proposed domestic price. The same conversions move any cost record between currencies. A cost from another year is first moved to the common price year with the live price-year adjustment HE-FM-COST-002 of the resource costing function HE-FN-COST-001, and the index itself belongs to the Consumer Price Index concept. A basket price reflects what other countries list, while the economically justifiable price HE-FM-EJP-001 and the break-even price HE-FM-BEA-001 give the highest price at which a technology is cost-effective at home. Notation follows the Basket of Countries article."; HEO defines Basket of Countries as "The basket of countries is the set of foreign markets whose drug prices a regulator compares in external reference pricing to set a domestic price.".

column2: Population mean outcome of a cohort model run by stratum against one cohort at averaged inputs
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cohort Model. The module describes Population mean outcome of a cohort model run by stratum against one cohort at averaged inputs as "Maps the shares of a starting population in two strata and the constant per-cycle death probability of each stratum to the population mean life expectancy found by running each stratum as its own cohort and weighting the results, to the life expectancy of one cohort run at the share-weighted mean probability, and to the gap between the two. HE-CF-COHM-001 carries the same comparison through a treatment that cuts each probability in proportion, to the QALY gains and ICERs of the article's worked example. TSD 15 states that a cohort run on average characteristics gives a biased estimate of the population mean where outcomes are non-linear in those characteristics, and the ISPOR-SMDM report states that outputs for a population-based starting cohort need one run for each stratum, aggregated across strata. Existing records are cited and not restated. The article's constant-risk life expectancy, 1/q minus one half, is the one-state case of HE-FM-ABS-001, whose 1/q cycles equal the mean geometric stay L_j of HE-FM-MKCH-002 and D_mean of HE-FM-MKA-004 with cycles of one year, less the half cycle that HE-ER-ABS-002 and HE-CF-MKCH-001 subtract for a cohort counted at the start of each cycle. The life years one stratum gains from a treatment are the difference of two values of that life expectancy, the ICER of the resulting QALY gain is HE-FM-ICER-001, and a proportional cut e gives the intervention risk of HE-FM-ARR-002 with a relative risk of 1 minus e, so none of these is restated. The share-weighted population effect is HE-FM-ATE-001, the value of deciding by subgroup is HE-FM-ATE-004, and HE-ER-CHN-002 shows why subgroup ICERs are not averaged. The cohort update and trace totals are HE-FM-MM-001, HE-FN-CSIM-001, HE-FM-CSIM-001 and HE-CF-CSIM-001, the second-order approximation to the mean of a curved output is HE-FM-EV-002, the background hazard of a mixed-sex cohort is HE-FM-BGM-003 with the error of reading a hazard at the mean age in HE-ER-BGM-007, and continuous-time life expectancy at constant rates is HE-FM-CONT-002. Notation follows the Cohort Model article."; HEO defines Cohort Model as "A cohort model is a health economic decision model that estimates mean costs and outcomes for a patient group as a whole, without simulating individuals.".

column2: Compartment flow balance function of a compartmental model
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Compartmental Model. The module describes Compartment flow balance function of a compartmental model as "Maps the numbers of people in the compartments of a population model, the flows between compartments per unit time and any inflow from or outflow to outside the model to the rate of change of each compartment, or, after a time step of length dt, to the next set of compartment counts. The flows can be fixed rates times compartment sizes, as in a static model, or can depend on the number infectious through the force of infection, which makes the model dynamic and nonlinear. A Markov cohort update (HE-FN-MM-001, HE-FM-MM-001) applies one fixed transition matrix to a closed cohort, the agent-based update HE-FN-ABM-001 with the per-contact infection probability HE-FM-ABM-001 follows individuals instead of pools, and a per-cycle probability from a constant rate follows HE-FM-TP-001. Reproduction numbers of the SIR model and of stratified models are in HE-FN-BRN-001 (HE-FM-BRN-001 to HE-FM-BRN-005 and HE-CF-BRN-001), and the final size of an epidemic and R_0 estimated from it are in HE-FN-ATR-001, HE-CF-ATR-001 and HE-FM-ATR-005, so none of them is restated here. Notation follows the Compartmental Model article."; HEO defines Compartmental Model as "A compartmental model splits a population into compartments, such as susceptible, infectious and recovered, and uses equations for the flows between them.".

column2: Consumer price index from a fixed basket with Jevons elementary aggregates, chain-linking and average inflation rates
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Consumer Price Index. The module describes Consumer price index from a fixed basket with Jevons elementary aggregates, chain-linking and average inflation rates as "Maps the base-period and current prices of a fixed basket, with the quantities or expenditure of an earlier weight reference period, to a Lowe-type index level, and combines the matched prices of one elementary aggregate by the Jevons geometric mean. It also joins yearly links into a long series on the 2015 = 100 reference and maps two index values and the months between them to an average annual inflation rate. The ratio of two index values is the I_b / I_a input of the live price-year adjustment HE-FM-COST-002 under HE-FN-COST-001, which is not repeated here, and a ratio of the US CPI for all urban consumers enters the Medicaid additional rebate of HE-FM-340B-002. Currency conversion and purchasing power parities are left to the Basket of Countries page. Notation follows the Consumer Price Index article."; HEO defines Consumer Price Index as "The consumer price index (CPI) measures change in the prices households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, used to adjust costs for inflation.".

column2: League-table allocation of a fixed budget across independent programmes ranked by ICER
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness League Table. The module describes League-table allocation of a fixed budget across independent programmes ranked by ICER as "Takes the incremental cost Delta_C_i and incremental health gain Delta_E_i of each of a set of independent programmes, each measured against its own comparator, and a fixed budget B. It returns the share of each programme funded when programmes are funded in ascending order of ICER until the budget is exhausted, the health the budget buys, the critical ratio of the last programme funded and, under the alternative fixed ratio rule, the budget that a stated threshold implies. Each programme's ratio is the two-option ICER of HE-FM-ICER-001, or the ratio against doing nothing of HE-FM-ACER-002 when doing nothing is the comparator, and is not restated here. A league table ranks independent programmes competing for one budget, while mutually exclusive options for the same patients are ranked on the cost-effectiveness frontier (HE-FN-CEF-001, HE-CF-CEF-001), and the table takes such a set at its sequential ratios along the frontier (HE-FM-CEA-001). Ties and cost-saving programmes follow the dominance rule HE-FM-DOM-001, the threshold as marginal spending over marginal health is HE-FM-CET-001, and the health a new programme displaces at a threshold, Delta_C divided by k, and its incremental net health benefit are HE-FM-CET-002. This package adds the funded share of each programme, the critical ratio, the fill for programmes that must be funded whole and the budget implied by a fixed ratio, with a computational function that fills the table for any number of programmes. Notation follows the Cost-Effectiveness League Table article."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness League Table as "A cost-effectiveness league table ranks health care interventions by cost per QALY or a similar ratio so decision makers can compare value for money.".

column2: Country-specific value set comparison function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Country-Specific Value Set. The module describes Country-specific value set comparison function as "Takes one EQ-5D-3L health profile, or the pair of profiles a treatment moves patients between, and the coefficients of two national value sets, and returns the utility gain under each set, the gap between the two gains and the resulting change in the QALY gain and in the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio. The scoring rule itself is live and is not restated here. The main-effects form with a constant and level decrements, which the article writes as U(s) equal to 1 minus c I(s) minus the sum of the level decrements beta_d(l_d), is HE-FM-EQ3L-001 with the N3 decrement set to zero; HE-FM-EQ3L-002 fixes it at the UK MVH tariff, HE-CF-EQ3L-001 scores any constant and N3 set such as the Dutch one, and HE-FM-EQ3L-003 gives the QALY difference between two states under one set. The records here compare sets. HE-FM-CSVS-001 splits the cross-set gap in a utility gain by term, HE-FM-CSVS-002 turns two QALY gains into relative changes in the gain and the ICER (HE-FM-CUA-001), and HE-FM-CSVS-003 gives the count-based D1 form that the US set uses in place of a constant. Five-level value sets belong to the EQ-5D-5L value set concept, and QALYs from different sets are not added (HE-ER-QALY-003). Notation follows the Country-Specific Value Set article."; HEO defines Country-Specific Value Set as "A country-specific value set is a set of utility weights, elicited from one country's general public, that turns EQ-5D or similar responses into utilities.".

column2: Decision uncertainty function giving the probability that the expected-value choice is wrong
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Decision Uncertainty. The module describes Decision uncertainty function giving the probability that the expected-value choice is wrong as "Takes the uncertain net benefit of each option at a stated cost-effectiveness threshold and returns P_error, the probability that the option chosen on expected net benefit is not the option with the highest net benefit, the decision uncertainty that PMG36 section 4.7.2 asks a model to quantify. From a table of probabilistic draws P_error is one minus the acceptability of the chosen option, live as HE-FM-CEAC-003 (function HE-FN-CEAC-001), where the share N_d*/N of the article is the multi-option CEAC of HE-FM-CEAC-002 or the two-option CEAC of HE-FM-CEAC-001, and the draws procedure for three options is HE-CF-EVPI-001. With two options and a normal incremental net benefit the acceptability of the chosen option is the standard normal cumulative probability at the absolute mean divided by its standard deviation, the probability of HE-FM-AN-004 read for the chosen option, so P_error is the upper normal tail at that ratio, the same tail that enters the loss term of HE-FM-EVPI-004. That combination of live records is cited, not restated. The split of EVPI into P_error times the mean loss when wrong is HE-FM-EVPI-003, EVPI itself is HE-FM-VOI-001 and HE-FM-EVPI-001, population EVPI is HE-FM-VOI-002, the incremental net monetary benefit of the article's worked example is HE-FM-NMB-002 and the maximum net benefit rule is HE-FM-NMB-003. The Monte Carlo standard error of an error probability estimated from N draws is the binomial standard error of HE-FM-BINOM-004 with N in place of n, and the number of runs belongs to the PSA package, so neither is restated. This package adds the error probability read from the p-value of a test of incremental net benefit. Notation follows the Decision Uncertainty article."; HEO defines Decision Uncertainty as "Decision uncertainty is the probability that the option preferred on current evidence is not the best, given uncertainty in costs and health effects.".

column2: Probabilistic sensitivity analysis run that turns joint parameter draws into stored decision outputs
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis. The module describes Probabilistic sensitivity analysis run that turns joint parameter draws into stored decision outputs as "Maps a decision model f, the joint distribution of its uncertain inputs and a cost-effectiveness threshold lambda to the outputs stored for every draw and their summaries. Each of the N draws theta_i is one complete set of inputs, applied to every option so that incremental results keep their dependence, and the model returns each option's cost and QALYs in that draw. The summaries are live records and are not restated here. Expected net monetary and net health benefit from the draws are HE-FM-ENB-001 and HE-FM-ENB-002, the probability that each option is cost-effective and the acceptability frontier are HE-FM-CEAC-001 to HE-FM-CEAC-003, and per-person EVPI from the same draws is HE-FM-VOI-001 with the forms in HE-FM-EVPI-001 to HE-FM-EVPI-004. A probabilistic ICER is the two-option ratio HE-FM-ICER-001 taken on expected values (HE-AS-ICER-003). The Monte Carlo standard error of a mean output over independent draws is the standard deviation across draws divided by the square root of N, the form of HE-FM-ANTV-002 with one observation per draw, and the number of draws for a target standard error is HE-FM-ABM-003 (HE-FM-ABM-004 for a share of draws); antithetic pairs are HE-FN-ANTV-001. Why a run at the mean inputs differs from the mean of the runs is covered by HE-FM-EV-001 to HE-FM-EV-004, and input distributions by HE-FN-BETA-001, HE-CF-BETA-001, HE-FM-BETA-005 and HE-FM-DIRI-001. The probability of a wrong decision and the Monte Carlo error of that probability belong to the Decision Uncertainty page. This package adds the two-parameter Cholesky step that draws a correlated pair of normal inputs, the expected loss of each of two options with the identity that links the two losses to expected net health benefit, and a computational function that runs the whole analysis on a small fixed set of draws. Notation follows the Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis article."; HEO defines Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis as "Probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA) runs a decision model many times on jointly drawn inputs to estimate expected outcomes and decision uncertainty.".

column2: Patient time cost function from service use, hours per use and an hourly value of time
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Patient Time Cost. The module describes Patient time cost function from service use, hours per use and an hourly value of time as "Maps the number of times a patient uses each type of health service, the hours each use takes in travel, waiting and care, and an hourly value of time to the money value of the patient's time in care over a period, per visit and in total. It is the resource costing sum HE-FM-COST-001 with patient hours as the resource and the hourly value as the unit cost, so the package keeps only the steps particular to patient time, which are hours built up from service counts (HE-FM-PTC-001 and HE-CF-PTC-001), the change in an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio when the time cost is added (HE-FM-PTC-002) and a value of time that depends on employment status (HE-FM-PTC-003). Productivity cost is a different cost category. The absence records HE-FN-ABSN-001, HE-FM-ABSN-002 and HE-FM-ABSN-003 value time lost from paid work as lost output, under the human capital approach or within the friction period, whereas patient time cost values the hours spent in care whether they are taken from paid work, unpaid work or leisure, and an hour taken from paid work is counted under one heading only. A value of time from another price year is moved with HE-FM-COST-002, time costs in later years are discounted with HE-FN-DISC-001, and a national total from a mean time cost per patient follows HE-FM-COI-001. Notation follows the Patient Time Cost article."; HEO defines Patient Time Cost as "Patient time cost is the value of the hours patients spend travelling to, waiting for and receiving health care, often valued at a wage rate.".

column2: EQ-5D-5L value set scoring function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept EQ-5D-5L Value Set. The module describes EQ-5D-5L value set scoring function as "Maps an EQ-5D-5L profile, the level 1 to 5 reported on each of mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain or discomfort and anxiety or depression, to a single utility under the coefficients of a chosen five-level value set. The five-level instrument describes 3,125 states, and a main-effects value set gives each dimension its own decrement at each of levels 2 to 5, 20 decrements in all, plus a constant where the set reports one. Once the decrement for the reported level of each dimension has been looked up (HE-FM-EQ5L-001), the profile score is the main-effects form of HE-FM-EQ3L-001 with the N3 decrement set to zero, and the three-level tariff itself is HE-FM-EQ3L-002; the 15D counterpart is HE-FM-15D-001. The utilities it returns weight time in QALYs (HE-FM-QALY-001), and a QALY difference between two scored states is HE-FM-EQ3L-003, which applies only when both states are scored with the same set. Scoring one profile under the value sets of two countries belongs to the Country-Specific Value Set page. Notation follows the EQ-5D-5L Value Set article."; HEO defines EQ-5D-5L Value Set as "EQ-5D-5L value set is a scoring algorithm, estimated from a general public valuation study, that gives each of the 3,125 EQ-5D-5L states a QALY utility.".

column2: Life years gained as the area between two survival curves and the share observed within a trial
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Life Years Gained. The module describes Life years gained as the area between two survival curves and the share observed within a trial as "Maps the survival curves of an intervention and its comparator, a trial follow-up time tau and a model horizon T to the life years gained within follow-up, the life years gained over the horizon, the share of that gain lying within follow-up and the gain lying after it. The gain over a horizon is the area between the two curves, the integral of S_1(t) minus S_0(t), which Royston and Parmar give as the difference in restricted mean survival time between two arms. Existing records are cited and not restated. The area under one curve is the restricted mean survival time of HE-FM-ADMC-003 for a Kaplan-Meier step function, the interval area A_j of HE-FM-BTH-001 under a constant hazard and the trapezoid life years of HE-CF-PSM-001, so the undiscounted gain is the difference of two such areas. The discounted gain is the present value of a stream, HE-FM-DR-002, applied to the yearly gains; the article's step 3, with year 1 undiscounted, places the gain of year k at time k minus 1 (t starting at 0 in HE-FM-DR-002, the start-of-year timing of HE-FM-DISC-002), whereas HE-CF-PSM-001 discounts each interval at its midpoint. The share of a gain that discounting removes, 1 minus the discounted total over the undiscounted total, equals rise divided by (1 plus rise) for the level stream of HE-CF-DISC-001 (derived here), so it is not drafted either. The cost per life year gained is HE-FM-ICER-001 with life years as the effect, and the QALY gain when both arms live at one constant utility is that utility times the life years gained, the constant-utility case of HE-FM-QALY-001 and of HE-FM-PSM-003 with equal state utilities. Mean survival with a cure fraction is HE-FN-CRM-001, the expected cycles alive of a constant-risk cohort follow from HE-FM-ABS-001, and the share of one arm's mean survival that comes from an exponential tail is P_tail of HE-FM-ADMC-004. Discounted quality-adjusted life expectancy belongs to the QALY Shortfall concept. Notation follows the Life Years Gained article."; HEO defines Life Years Gained as "Life years gained (LYG) are the extra years of mean survival an intervention gives over its comparator, without quality adjustment, in economic evaluation.".

column2: Health production function mapping medical care, own time and schooling to gross investment in health and its least cost
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Health Production Function. The module describes Health production function mapping medical care, own time and schooling to gross investment in health and its least cost as "Maps a person's medical care, own time and stock of schooling to gross investment in health, Grossman's I = I(M, TH; E), and, given the price of care, the wage and an outlay or a target, to the least-cost input mix and the unit cost of gross investment.
