It uses the Cobb-Douglas member of the class that Grossman fitted, with the intercept suppressed, and treats schooling as an efficiency shift. The output I is the gross investment term of the live stock update HE-FM-DFH-001, which carries the stock into the next period, and the unit cost of HE-FM-HPF-003 is the marginal cost of gross investment pi_(t-1) that the pure investment condition HE-FM-DFH-002 takes as an input, since constant returns and fixed input prices make marginal and average cost equal. The package keeps the production side only, with the Cobb-Douglas gross investment in HE-FM-HPF-001, the least-cost split of an outlay in HE-FM-HPF-002, the unit cost and outlay for a target in HE-FM-HPF-003, and the outlay that holds the stock on a target path in HE-CF-HPF-001. A mix that costs more than the least-cost mix for its output is measured by the cost efficiency ratio of HE-FM-EFF-002. The production of care by providers belongs to the healthcare production function concept and is not drafted here. Notation follows the Health Production Function article."; HEO defines Health Production Function as "A health production function shows how medical care, other market goods and own time produce health, with education raising efficiency (Grossman model).".

column2: Specific attachment point expected reimbursement, variance and claims inflation response function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Attachment Point. The module describes Specific attachment point expected reimbursement, variance and claims inflation response function as "Maps the distribution of one covered person's eligible claims for a contract year, a specific attachment point A, a cap on claims U and a coinsurance rate c to the mean, second moment, variance and standard deviation of the stop-loss or reinsurance reimbursement for that person, and maps a uniform claims inflation rate g to the proportional rise in the expected reimbursement of an uncapped excess layer whose attachment point stays fixed. The one-year payment rule of the article, R equal to c times the positive part of min(C, U) minus A, is the payment rule of HE-FM-ASL-001 applied to one person's claims C in place of the group's net claims S, with a layer limit M equal to U minus A, multiplied by c, because for any cap at or above the attachment point min(max(C minus A, 0), U minus A) equals max(min(C, U) minus A, 0) (derived, checked numerically), so the rule is cited and not restated. The aggregate side of a stop-loss policy is live as HE-FM-ASL-001 to HE-FM-ASL-005 and HE-CF-ASL-001, including the normal approximation to an expected excess (HE-FM-ASL-005), and the standard deviation of a total over independent members is the square-root rule of HE-FM-ASL-003. A probability-weighted mean in general is HE-FN-EV-001 (HE-FM-CHN-001 at a chance node), a member's cost sharing under a deductible, coinsurance and out-of-pocket maximum is HE-FM-AV-002, a gross premium with loadings is HE-FM-ACTA-002 and moving a cost from one price year to another with an index is HE-FM-COST-002. This package adds the variance of the specific reimbursement over a discrete claims distribution, with its mean, and the response of an excess layer to claims inflation. Notation follows the Attachment Point article."; HEO defines Attachment Point as "An attachment point is the claims level at which stop-loss insurance or health reinsurance starts to pay, per person (specific) or per group (aggregate).".

column2: Landmark survival comparison by a status reached during follow-up and the immortal-time bias of grouping from the start
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Landmark Analysis. The module describes Landmark survival comparison by a status reached during follow-up and the immortal-time bias of grouping from the start as "Maps follow-up data for patients grouped by a status reached after follow-up begins, such as tumour response, to a comparison of the groups that does not credit the time before the status to one group, made either by restarting the clock at a landmark time s for the patients still event free at s or by splitting person-time at the change of status, and to the bias of the naive grouping from the start. HE-FM-LMA-002 gives that bias as a factor F in a constant-hazard rate ratio of responders when the person-time responders spent before responding is counted as responder time, each rate ratio having the form of HE-FM-HR-005. The article's conditional survival S(t | T > s) = S(t) / S(s) is the live HE-FM-LTR-001, S_cond = S_t / S_l with the entry time l in the place of the landmark s, and is not restated. The article's whole-cohort value 0.495 / 0.85, about 0.582, is that formula applied, and so are its landmark proportions, since in the naive non-responder group of 130 patients survival to the landmark is 100/130 and 0.385 divided by 100/130 is 0.50. The fall in the naive survival gap is HE-FM-LTR-001 again, because the responder proportion 49/70 is the same in both groupings and the gap falls by S_cond minus S_t of the naive non-responder group, 0.50 minus 0.385, the 11.5 points between the article's gaps of 31.5 and 20 points; each gap has the form of HE-FM-ARR-001. The same ratio is the residual stay R_ab of HE-FM-MKA-002 and S_res of HE-FM-MKA-003 for geometric and exponential stays, and one minus it over a single cycle is the cycle probability of HE-FN-CUMH-001 and HE-FM-CUMH-002, since 1 minus exp(minus (H(t) minus H(t minus Delta))) equals 1 minus S(t) / S(t minus Delta). Relative survival HE-FM-BGM-001 divides by expected background survival at the same time, not by the cohort's own survival at an earlier time, so it is a different ratio. Landmark survival from patient records is the left-truncated Kaplan-Meier curve of HE-CF-LTR-001 run in each status group with every entry time set to s, built on the product-limit step of HE-FM-ADMC-002. The landmark Cox model h(t | x(s), T > s) = h_0s(t) exp(beta_s x(s)) is an ordinary Cox model fitted to the patients at risk at s, with its hazard ratio from the coefficient as in HE-FM-HR-002; it has no closed-form calculator line and is given for reading only. Notation follows the Landmark Analysis article."; HEO defines Landmark Analysis as "A survival technique restricting analysis to patients event-free up to a predefined time point, then examining survival from that point forward.".

column2: Hedges' g small-sample correction, sampling variance and bias of the standardised mean difference
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Hedges' G. The module describes Hedges' g small-sample correction, sampling variance and bias of the standardised mean difference as "Maps Cohen's d, the uncorrected standardised mean difference of HE-FM-CD-001, and the two group sizes to Hedges' g, the same difference multiplied by a correction factor J that removes the upward small-sample bias of d, and to the variance and standard error of g that an inverse-variance meta-analysis needs. It also gives the standard error that Review Manager attaches to the same statistic, and the expected overstatement of a population standardised difference by d at a given number of degrees of freedom. The pooled standard deviation and d itself are HE-FM-CD-001 and are not restated. A confidence interval for g is the large-sample interval HE-FM-AN-001 applied with the standard error of g, the logistic conversion to a log odds ratio is HE-FM-CD-002 with g in place of d, and pooling g across studies is HE-FM-ADMA-001 for a common effect or HE-FM-ADMA-005 for random effects. Notation follows the Hedges' g article."; HEO defines Hedges' G as "A standardised effect size measure similar to Cohen's d but corrected for small sample size bias.".

column2: Pigouvian subsidy bill, inframarginal transfer and net welfare with costly public funds
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Pigouvian Subsidy. The module describes Pigouvian subsidy bill, inframarginal transfer and net welfare with costly public funds as "Maps linear marginal private benefit, constant marginal cost and falling marginal external benefit curves, a per-unit subsidy and the marginal excess burden of taxation to the subsidy bill, the part of it paid to people who would have taken up the activity anyway, the net welfare change of the subsidy and the uniform rate that maximises it. The efficient quantity and the Pigouvian subsidy s = MEB(Q_s) with these curve shapes are HE-FM-EXT-002, within the social marginal benefit framework HE-FM-EXT-001, so the article's efficient 72 thousand courses, its subsidy of GBP 12 and its welfare loss of GBP 90,000 a year without a subsidy are re-applications of HE-FM-EXT-002 and are not drafted again. The subsidy set at the external benefit observed before the subsidy has the same algebra as the tax record HE-FM-PIGT-003 with the sign of the external term reversed (an external cost of minus 30 plus 0.25Q for the article's curves), which returns the article's 75 thousand courses and loss of 5.625. HE-FM-PIGT-003 is written for an external cost of zero or above (HE-VR-PIGT-025, HE-AS-PIGT-006, HE-VT-PIGT-006), and for a subsidy the overshoot lies above the efficient quantity, so the package reads that case through HE-FM-PIGS-002 at a rate equal to the external benefit at Q_p (HE-EX-PIGS-006) and does not draft it again. The excess burden of financing is the marginal excess burden of HE-FM-DWL-004 applied to the subsidy bill. The new steps are the bill and its split between inframarginal and induced users (HE-FM-PIGS-001), the net welfare of any uniform or targeted rate (HE-FM-PIGS-002) and the welfare-maximising uniform rate (HE-FM-PIGS-003). Notation follows the Pigouvian Subsidy article."; HEO defines Pigouvian Subsidy as "A Pigouvian subsidy is a payment for an activity that benefits others, set equal to its marginal external benefit at the socially efficient level.".

column2: Delta-adjusted analysis of QALYs lost to follow-up with its tipping-point shift
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Loss to Follow-Up. The module describes Delta-adjusted analysis of QALYs lost to follow-up with its tipping-point shift as "Takes each arm's mean QALYs among participants still followed, the proportion of each arm lost to follow-up, an assumed shift delta in the mean QALYs of those lost from the new treatment arm, a ratio r that sets the shift for those lost from usual care at r times delta, the incremental cost and a cost-effectiveness threshold, and returns the delta-adjusted QALY gain and ICER under that shift and the tipping-point shift at which the conclusion changes. The arm mean over everyone randomised, E_bar, is one minus p times E_obs plus p times (E_obs plus delta), which equals E_obs plus p times delta. That is the two-part mixture of HE-FM-LOCF-001 with tau read as p, mu_end as E_obs and mu_last as E_obs plus delta, so its bias_mu, tau times (mu_last minus mu_end), becomes p times delta. The QALY gain under shifts in both arms is Delta_tilde of HE-FM-LOCF-002 with the same reading in each arm, the observed gain plus p_T times delta_T minus p_C times delta_C, here with delta_T equal to delta and delta_C equal to r times delta. The ICER under a shift is HE-FM-ICER-001 and the gain needed at the threshold, Delta_C / lambda, is H_d of HE-FM-CET-002. These live records are cited, not restated, and HE-CF-LTFU-001 runs them in sequence for the article's scenarios. The inverse probability of censoring weights of HE-FN-DCEN-001 and HE-FM-DCEN-001 to HE-FM-DCEN-004 assume that censoring is unrelated to the unseen outcome once measured covariates are allowed for, and the administrative censoring time of HE-FM-ADMC-001 is set by design, so neither represents a departure from missing at random. This package adds the shift at which the delta-adjusted QALY gain falls to Delta_C / lambda. Notation follows the Loss to Follow-Up article."; HEO defines Loss to Follow-Up as "Loss to follow-up occurs when trial participants stop providing data before follow-up ends, so later outcomes, costs and QALYs can be missing.".

column2: Case-mix adjusted provider cost comparison with a ranking reversal rule
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Case-Mix Adjustment. The module describes Case-mix adjusted provider cost comparison with a ranking reversal rule as "Maps the actual costs, case numbers and expected costs at national mean unit costs of two providers to the ratio of their crude costs per case, the ratio of their expected costs per case, the ratio of their indirectly standardised cost indices and a flag for a crude ranking that the adjustment reverses. The article's three methods are live and are cited, not restated. Cost per weighted case, C_h divided by the sum of the case weights, is C_h / CM_h with CM_h = sum n_hg w_g of HE-FM-CWT-003, equal to c_bar times R_h, and the case mix index CMI_h = CM_h / n_h is an output of HE-CF-CWT-001, so the article's (C_h / n_h) / CMI_h is the same quantity. With the weights w_g = c_bar_g / c_bar of HE-FM-CWT-001 the expected cost E_h = sum n_hg c_bar_g equals CM_h times c_bar, so the cost index I_h = 100 A_h / E_h is 100 times R_h of HE-FM-CWT-003, and HE-FM-ALOS-004 applies the same indirect standardisation to bed-days. The PROMs adjusted score Adj_j is the mean over a provider's patients of the need-standardised value of HE-FM-HEQ-002, y_i minus yX_i plus y_bar, with the case-mix prediction in place of yX_i. Direct standardisation on a common mix is the weighted sum of HE-FM-INEQ-001, with case groups in place of age groups, unit costs in place of rates and the pooled case shares as the standard. HE-ER-CWT-004 and HE-ER-ALOS-006 show in numbers a crude ranking that adjustment reverses, and this package adds the condition under which the reversal happens. HE-AS-CWT-006 states that up-coding raises CM_h and lowers R_h with no change in efficiency. The article's upcoding step is HE-FM-CWT-003 recomputed on the recoded counts, an expected cost of E_h plus the number of cases moved times the gap between the two groups' national mean unit costs, so it is cited, not restated. The case mix index and the observed-to-expected benchmark comparison have their own pages. Notation follows the Case-Mix Adjustment article."; HEO defines Case-Mix Adjustment as "Case-mix adjustment corrects comparisons of providers' costs or outcomes for differences in the patients they treat, so that like is compared with like.".

column2: Function for the negative likelihood ratio of a negative result on two tests with conditional dependence
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Negative Likelihood Ratio. The module describes Function for the negative likelihood ratio of a negative result on two tests with conditional dependence as "Takes the sensitivities Se_1 and Se_2 and specificities Sp_1 and Sp_2 of two tests and their conditional covariances, C_pos among people with the condition and C_neg among people without it, and returns the negative likelihood ratio LR_neg_12 of a negative result on both, through the combined sensitivity and specificity of the rule that calls a person positive when either test is positive. LR_neg = (1 minus Se) / Sp is live as HE-FM-DXA-002, and the post-test probability after a negative result, one minus the negative predictive value of HE-FM-DXA-003, is the odds update that HE-VT-DXA-006 checks. The highest pre-test probability at which a negative result brings the risk down to p*, p* / (p* + (1 minus p*) LR_neg), and the largest ratio that does so at a pre-test probability p, p* (1 minus p) / ((1 minus p*) p), are that live update with one minus the negative predictive value set to p* and solved for p or for the ratio, so they are cited here and not drafted (derived). In the article's example the first is about 21.9%, and it is also the pre-test probability above which confirming everyone beats testing first when the triage test is free (derived). The article's threshold p* = C_conf / L_miss is the decision-curve threshold HE-FM-DCA-004 with G = L_miss minus C_conf and L = C_conf (derived). The pathway's net monetary benefit against confirming everyone and its break-even pre-test probability are HE-FM-DXA-005 and HE-CF-DXA-001 with confirming everyone entered as a test of sensitivity 1, specificity 0 and no cost (derived), which returns the article's 19.0%. Deeks and Altman note that likelihood ratios can be treated like risk ratios for confidence intervals, so the interval for LR_neg is HE-FM-PWMA-001 with a = FN, n1 = TP + FN, c = TN and n2 = TN + FP, exponentiated as in HE-FM-HR-006. Notation follows the Negative Likelihood Ratio article, with the two-test symbols added here."; HEO defines Negative Likelihood Ratio as "Negative Likelihood Ratio (LR-): (1 minus sensitivity) over specificity, the factor by which a negative test multiplies disease odds in decision models.".

column2: Copas selection model publication probability and implied number of unpublished studies
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Copas Model. The module describes Copas selection model publication probability and implied number of unpublished studies as "Takes the two selection parameters of the Copas selection model, gamma_0 and gamma_1, and the standard errors of the published studies, and returns each study's probability of publication, Phi(gamma_0 + gamma_1 / s), and the number of unpublished studies those parameters imply, M. In a Copas sensitivity analysis gamma_0 and gamma_1 are fixed over a grid, and at each point the mean effect theta, the heterogeneity tau and the correlation rho are estimated by maximising the likelihood of the published estimates conditional on publication. That adjusted estimate has no closed form and comes from software such as the copas function of the R package metasens, so it is not written as a formula here; the publication probability and M are the quantities that label each grid point. The unadjusted estimate the analysis starts from is the common-effect inverse-variance mean of HE-FM-ADMA-001 (random-effects form HE-FM-ADMA-005), and the article's unadjusted 0.3671 is HE-FM-ADMA-001 applied to its twelve illustrative trials. A rank test for small-study effects is HE-FN-BEGG-001, with HE-FM-BEGG-002 and HE-CF-BEGG-001. Carrying an adjusted odds ratio into a decision model uses HE-FM-NMA-004 for the response probability on the new therapy and HE-FM-ICER-001 for the cost per extra responder. Notation follows the Copas Model article."; HEO defines Copas Model as "The Copas model is a selection model for publication bias in meta-analysis that re-estimates the pooled effect under assumed rates of non-publication.".

column2: Derived demand for medical care from the Grossman demand for the health stock
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Derived Demand for Healthcare. The module describes Derived demand for medical care from the Grossman demand for the health stock as "Maps the elasticity of the marginal efficiency of health capital, the time share of the cost of gross investment, the schooling efficiency parameter and a change in the wage, the marginal cost of gross investment or the price of care, schooling and the depreciation rate to the proportional change in the health stock demanded, in gross investment and in medical care demanded, in the pure investment version of the Grossman model with a zero real-own rate of interest. HE-FM-DDHC-001 gives Grossman's demand function for the health stock and HE-FM-DDHC-002 his reduced-form demand function for medical care with its wage, price, schooling and depreciation coefficients. Both build on live records that this package does not restate, the pure investment condition HE-FM-DFH-002, the stock update HE-FM-DFH-001 (gross investment of about delta H when net investment is small), the Cobb-Douglas gross investment of HE-FM-HPF-001, the least-cost care of HE-FM-HPF-002 and the unit cost pi of HE-FM-HPF-003. Because Grossman suppresses the intercepts, both formulas compare two states, such as two ages of one person or two people, as ratios, and for a change in one price alone each ratio has the constant-elasticity form of HE-FM-XPE-003. Notation follows the Derived Demand for Healthcare article."; HEO defines Derived Demand for Healthcare as "Derived demand for healthcare is the idea that people want medical care mainly as an input for producing health, the thing they actually value.".

column2: Net days in accounts receivable function for a provider paid claim by claim
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Days in Accounts Receivable. The module describes Net days in accounts receivable function for a provider paid claim by claim as "Maps a provider's net patient receivables, its net patient service revenue and the calendar days of the revenue period to net days in accounts receivable, the receivables balance expressed as days of average daily net revenue. The measure belongs to providers paid claim by claim, under fee-for-service or case-based payment such as the case-weighted payment per case of HE-FM-CWT-002, where every episode of care becomes a receivable until it is collected. HE-FM-DAR-001 gives the measure and HE-CF-DAR-001 builds its denominator from monthly revenue and actual calendar days as HFMA MAP Key FM-1 requires. Split by payer group, the overall figure is the revenue-weighted mean of the groups' own figures, the weighted mean of HE-FM-CRAT-001 and of the first part of HE-FM-CWT-001 with daily revenue in place of member or case numbers, so it is not drafted again. Since the balance equals r_bar times DAR, the cash released when collection shortens is r_bar times the fall in days, and the annual cost of carrying the balance at a cost of capital i is i times the receivables balance, the same rate-times-balance product as the return R_t = r * B_t on the balance still tied up in HE-CF-ANLS-002. The article's other use of released cash, held as cash and divided by daily cash operating expenses to give extra days cash on hand, is an alternative to the saving, not an addition to it. DAR equals the mean time a unit of revenue waits for cash, the W of Little's law in HE-FM-DES-003, only in a steady state with constant daily revenue, where the closing balance equals the time-average balance (derived); away from that state the two differ. Notation follows the Days in Accounts Receivable article."; HEO defines Days in Accounts Receivable as "Days in accounts receivable (AR days) is a provider's net receivables divided by average daily net patient revenue, giving days of revenue still unpaid.".

column2: Heterotrait-monotrait ratio of indicator correlations for discriminant validity
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Discriminant Validity. The module describes Heterotrait-monotrait ratio of indicator correlations for discriminant validity as "Maps the correlation matrix of the indicators of two or more multi-item constructs, with each indicator assigned to one construct, to the heterotrait-monotrait ratio HTMT_ij for each pair of constructs, the mean correlation between the indicators of constructs i and j divided by the geometric mean of the mean correlations among the indicators within each construct, for comparison with a cut-off of 0.85 or 0.90. HE-FM-DISV-001 writes the ratio for two indicators per construct, the case of the article's worked example, and HE-CF-DISV-001 computes it for any numbers of indicators and every pair of constructs. The article's known-groups step is the live HE-FM-CD-001 applied to the mild and moderate groups (pooled standard deviations of 0.2102 and 17.03, standardised differences of 0.24 and 0.94), its QALY gains of 0.10 and 0.24 are HE-FM-QALY-001, the sum of utility times duration, for two constant-utility states over 2 years differenced, and its ratios of £30,000 and £12,500 per QALY are HE-FM-ICER-001, so none of them is restated. The factor of 2.4 by which the ratio would be overstated is two HE-FM-ICER-001 ratios with the same incremental cost divided, which equals the inverse ratio of the two QALY gains. The multitrait-multimethod checks in the article's steps 1 to 3 are differences of correlations set against the analyst's prespecified cut-offs and have no formula record. Correcting prevalence and cost for misclassification against a gold standard is HE-FN-CRV-001, a criterion-validity function and a different property. Notation follows the Discriminant Validity article."; HEO defines Discriminant Validity as "Discriminant validity is evidence that a health measure correlates less with measures of other constructs than with its own, as predicted in advance.".

column2: Healthcare production function mapping staff, capital, consumables and technology to provider activity
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Healthcare Production Function. The module describes Healthcare production function mapping staff, capital, consumables and technology to provider activity as "Maps a provider's labour L, capital K, drugs and consumables M and technology and organisation T to the maximum activity Q it can produce in a period, such as consultations or case-mix-adjusted episodes. It is the provider counterpart of the household function HE-FN-HPF-001, in which health itself is the output. The quantities read off the function are held in live records and are cited here, not restated. The Cobb-Douglas form with exponents summing to one is HE-FM-HPF-001 with A = exp(rho_H E), alpha = 1-K and beta = K, K there being the own time share, and the marginal products, each exponent times output over the input, and their ratio, the marginal rate of technical substitution, take the form of those in HE-FM-HPF-002, which computes them only for exponents summing to one; the same form holds for any exponents (derived). Marginal cost as the price of an input over its marginal product, MC = w / MP_L when labour is the only variable input, is Grossman's condition held in HE-SR-HPF-003 and tested in HE-VT-HPF-006, and average variable cost w / AP_L is the unit labour cost w / a_h of HE-FM-BAUM-001. A discrete marginal product from a production schedule is a change in output over a change in input, the same difference-quotient form as HE-FM-ICER-001, and an average product is a partial productivity ratio such as the bed turnover rate of HE-FM-BTO-001. Distance from an estimated frontier is measured by HE-FM-EFF-001 to HE-FM-EFF-003. Average cost, cost functions and the marginal cost of a change in scale belong to the Average Cost, Cost Function and Marginal Analysis pages. This package adds the degree of returns to scale of a Cobb-Douglas function whose output elasticities are estimated freely (HE-FM-HCPF-001). Notation follows the Healthcare Production Function article."; HEO defines Healthcare Production Function as "A healthcare production function gives the maximum care output, such as visits or hospital episodes, obtainable from given staff, capital and technology.".

column2: Health state utility from a time trade-off answer
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Utility. The module describes Health state utility from a time trade-off answer as "Maps one respondent's answer to a time trade-off question, the years T_y in full health judged equal to T_x years in a health state, to the utility of that state on the scale with full health at 1 and immediate death at 0. The standard gamble needs no separate formula, since the expected value of a gamble giving full health, valued at 1, with probability p and immediate death, valued at 0, otherwise is HE-FM-CHN-001 with two branches (the general form is HE-FN-EV-001) and equals p, so the indifference probability is itself the utility. The time trade-off rule HE-FM-UTIL-001 is the equality of the QALYs of the two sides of the question, each valued with HE-FM-QALY-001, solved for the utility. Lipman, Brouwer and Attema print it, and no live record states it. The utilities enter QALYs through HE-FM-QALY-001 and cost per QALY through HE-FM-ICER-001 and HE-FM-CUA-001 (HE-CF-ICUR-001 from arm-level costs and QALYs), and the article's worked example, including its toxicity period valued at minus 0.20, is a re-application of HE-FM-QALY-001, HE-FM-DISU-001 and HE-FM-ICER-001 and is not restated. Utilities of EQ-5D profiles come from value sets, HE-FN-EQ3L-001 and the UK time trade-off tariff HE-FM-EQ3L-002, and utility decrements from HE-FN-DISU-001 and HE-CF-DISU-001. Notation follows the Utility article, with the time trade-off durations of Lipman, Brouwer and Attema."; HEO defines Utility as "Utility is a numerical measure of preference; in health economics, a health utility values a health state on a scale where 1 is full health and 0 is dead.".

column2: Phelps welfare loss and optimal coinsurance function for medical insurance
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Moral Hazard in Health Insurance. The module describes Phelps welfare loss and optimal coinsurance function for medical insurance as "Maps a coinsurance rate C, the coefficient of absolute risk aversion r, the standard deviation sigma and mean mu of annual medical spending without insurance, and the absolute price elasticity of demand eps to the expected welfare loss per person of a policy with that rate, and maps the same parameters to the coinsurance rate that minimises the loss. The loss is the second-order approximation of Phelps, the risk premium of the share of spending the patient still bears plus the welfare-loss triangle of insurance-induced care. The triangle is the live HE-FM-MH-002 written in spending units (HE-FM-MH-001 gives it from prices and quantities, and HE-FN-MH-001 is the general ex post moral hazard function), and HE-FM-DWL-003 gives the fall in that loss when the rate rises, from spending at the two rates (with straight-line demand it equals the triangle at the lower rate minus the triangle at the higher rate, derived). The risk premium has no live record, since HE-FM-EV-002 gives the second-order expansion only in the output's own units. The cost-sharing split of a plan with a deductible and an out-of-pocket maximum is HE-FM-AV-002, the RAND arc elasticity behind the usual elasticity estimates is HE-FM-MH-003, and the fair premium in the article's Nyman illustration is HE-FM-ACTA-001 with HE-FM-ACTA-002 at zero loadings. Notation follows the Moral Hazard in Health Insurance article."; HEO defines Moral Hazard in Health Insurance as "Moral hazard in health insurance is extra healthcare use when cover lowers the price patients pay, and any reduced effort to stay healthy once insured.".

column2: 0-1 integer programming function for funding indivisible health programmes within a fixed budget
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Integer Programming. The module describes 0-1 integer programming function for funding indivisible health programmes within a fixed budget as "Takes the QALY gain q_i and the budget cost c_i of each of n candidate programmes or medicines, each funded in full or not at all, and a fixed budget B, and returns the package of funding decisions x_i, each 0 or 1, that gives the most QALYs with the cost of the package at most B, together with the QALYs H_star it buys. The league-table rule for whole programmes, HE-FM-CELT-003, funds in ascending order of ICER and passes over a programme that no longer fits, so it returns a package that fits the budget but not always the best one, and the divisible fill of HE-FM-CELT-001, filled for a whole table by HE-CF-CELT-001, part-funds the marginal programme and so gives health that whole programmes may not be able to deliver. Neither record searches the packages, and HE-FM-CELT-003 leaves the best choice of whole programmes to this article. HE-FM-IPH-001 gives H_star for four programmes by checking every package, with its gap to the health of a funding rule and its distance below the divisible fill, and HE-CF-IPH-001 enumerates the packages for any number of programmes and adds programmes that a rule requires to be funded. The critical ratio of a league table is HE-FM-CELT-002 and the budget implied by a threshold is HE-FM-CELT-004; shadow prices and Lagrangian conditions belong to the Constrained Optimisation article. The article's set-up cost form, a fixed cost switched on by a binary set-up variable plus a cost per person covered, is a model-building device for mixed-integer programmes and is not drafted here. Notation follows the Integer Programming article."; HEO defines Integer Programming as "Integer programming chooses which indivisible health programmes or medicines to fund to maximise health gain, such as QALYs, within a fixed budget.".

column2: Capacity utilisation of a health service with plant capacity measured on a frontier
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Capacity Utilisation. The module describes Capacity utilisation of a health service with plant capacity measured on a frontier as "Maps a health service's use of its capacity to a capacity utilisation figure. The simple measure in the article, capacity used over capacity available in the same units and period times 100, is a plain proportion of the form of the first part of HE-FM-PR-001, P_1 = a / (a + b), with a the capacity used and b the spare capacity, and of HE-FM-PDC-001, so it is not restated. Its bed form, occupied over available bed-days, is the occupancy o defined in HE-VR-ALOS-006 and used in HE-FM-ALOS-002, HE-FM-BTO-003 and HE-FM-BTO-004, and the empty bed-days of a period are the numerator of HE-FM-BTO-002. The fixed cost of a bed spread over the patients it served is HE-FM-BTO-005, the break-even volume of a service with fixed costs is HE-FM-BEA-002, annualised capital cost is HE-FM-COST-003 and HE-CF-ANLS-001, and the utilisation of a single-server queue is rho in HE-FM-ARRP-005. The average cost form AC = F / Q + v of the article belongs to the average-cost concept. HE-FM-CAPU-001 is plant capacity utilisation in frontier analysis, which divides the output efficiency of a unit when only its fixed inputs constrain production by its output efficiency when all inputs do, so that technical inefficiency (HE-FM-EFF-001) is set aside before unused plant capacity is measured. It is built like scale efficiency HE-FM-EFF-003 but compares a different pair of frontiers. Notation follows the Capacity Utilisation article, which describes the plant capacity measure in words, with the symbols of Valdmanis and colleagues."; HEO defines Capacity Utilisation as "Capacity utilisation is the share of available health care capacity, such as staffed beds, theatre sessions or scanner time, that is used over a period.".

column2: Health spending as a share of GDP function
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Health Spending as GDP Share. The module describes Health spending as a share of GDP function as "Maps the current health expenditure and the gross domestic product of one country in one year, both in the same national currency at current prices, to the share of GDP spent on health, reported as a percentage. The change in the share between two years is HE-FM-HGDP-001 evaluated in each year and divided, which regroups as the growth factor of spending divided by the growth factor of GDP (derived identity, not a separate formula). Spending per person in international dollars is a cost converted at purchasing power parity with HE-FM-BOC-002 and a target factor of 1, as in HE-EX-BOC-005, then divided by the population. The administrative share of current health expenditure is HE-FM-ACR-001, and the Baumol records give a relative unit cost and a model share of working hours (HE-FN-BAUM-001) and a component of real health spending growth (HE-FM-BAUM-004), which HE-ER-BAUM-008 separates from a change in the GDP share. If spending is proportional to GDP raised to an income elasticity eta, the share is proportional to GDP raised to eta minus 1 and rises with GDP only when eta exceeds 1 (derived); the only live income elasticity is the Variable HE-VR-XPE-021. Notation follows the Health Spending as GDP Share article."; HEO defines Health Spending as GDP Share as "Health spending as GDP share is current health expenditure divided by gross domestic product, used to compare health spending across countries and years.".

column2: Endemic vaccination externality function from coverage at birth to infection risk, benefit split and voluntary uptake
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Vaccination Externalities. The module describes Endemic vaccination externality function from coverage at birth to infection risk, benefit split and voluntary uptake as "Maps the basic reproduction number R_0 of an endemic infection, the share v of each birth cohort vaccinated at birth, the loss L per infection and the private cost c of one vaccination to the lifetime infection risk of an unvaccinated child and the infections per birth (HE-FM-VEXT-001), the private and external benefit of one more vaccination (HE-FM-VEXT-002) and the coverage that voluntary uptake reaches (HE-FM-VEXT-003), all in the long-run steady state of an SIR model with births and deaths. The marginal social benefit as marginal private plus marginal external benefit is HE-FM-EXT-001, the herd immunity threshold H = 1 minus 1/R_0 is HE-FM-BRN-003 and the effective reproduction number is HE-FM-BRN-002, so none of them is restated here; the Pigouvian vaccination subsidy with linear curves is HE-FM-EXT-002, with its bill and net welfare under HE-FN-PIGS-001. The article's social cost per 1,000 births, GBP 250,000 under voluntary uptake, GBP 212,500 under free provision and GBP 200,000 at the threshold, is 1,000 times the expected cost per birth at a chance node, HE-FM-CHN-001, with a vaccinated branch of probability v costing the full resource cost of a vaccination whoever pays it and an unvaccinated branch of probability 1 minus v costing the expected loss L times pi from HE-FM-VEXT-001, so it is not drafted as a formula. The lifetime chance lambda/(lambda + mu) of infection before death is the long-horizon limit of the competing-hazards record HE-FM-TP-004, the final size of a closed epidemic is HE-CF-ATR-001 and vaccine effectiveness from attack rates is HE-FM-ATR-004. Notation follows the Vaccination Externalities article."; HEO defines Vaccination Externalities as "Vaccination externalities are the benefits one person's vaccination gives others by cutting disease spread, benefits that person ignores when choosing.".

column2: Erlang loss sizing function for hospital beds with refused admissions
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Capacity Planning. The module describes Erlang loss sizing function for hospital beds with refused admissions as "Maps a ward's daily arrival rate, mean length of stay and number of staffed beds to the offered load, the share of arriving patients who find every bed full and are refused, the refusals a year and the occupancy the beds then achieve, and uses these to find the beds needed for a refusal target or at the lowest total cost of beds and refusals. The first estimate of beds, expected bed-days divided by the bed-days one bed supplies at a target occupancy, is the live throughput identity HE-FM-ALOS-002 solved for the beds with admissions in place of discharges, and the average number of occupied beds is Little's law, HE-FM-DES-003; neither is drafted again. The loss probability is not the Poisson overflow of HE-CF-ARRP-001, which gives the chance that more patients arrive in one hour than the service can absorb, a count of arrivals rather than of occupied beds, and not the single-server wait of HE-FM-ARRP-005, in which patients queue. HE-FM-CAPP-001 writes the loss model term by term for a six-bed unit, and HE-CF-CAPP-001 runs it for any number of beds by the Erlang B recursion and finds the beds for a refusal target and the number beyond which one more bed costs more than the refusals it avoids. Notation follows the Capacity Planning article."; HEO defines Capacity Planning as "Capacity planning estimates the beds, staff, theatre time and equipment a health service needs to meet expected demand to a stated standard of access.".

column2: Value measurement function for MCDA in HTA from criterion performance, ranges and swing points
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept MCDA in HTA. The module describes Value measurement function for MCDA in HTA from criterion performance, ranges and swing points as "Maps each technology's performance on each criterion, the fixed range of each criterion and the swing points given to each criterion to a partial value score per criterion on a 0 to 100 interval scale, a normalised weight per criterion and an overall value per technology. This is the value measurement approach, which the first ISPOR MCDA task force report describes as by far the most widely used in health care. HE-FM-MCDH-001 gives the linear partial value score, HE-FM-MCDH-002 the swing weights and the additive overall value, and HE-CF-MCDH-001 runs both for three technologies with a ranking and a scan of one weight. The second report notes that additive functions are also used in health-related quality of life instruments, and HE-FM-15D-001, the 15D score as an additive weighted sum of level values with importance weights elicited from population samples, is a live instance of that form; here the weights come from swing points elicited over stated ranges. When one weight varies and the others keep their ratio, each total is linear in that weight, and the weight at which the totals of two technologies are equal, a change of ranking only when it is at least 0 and at most 1, takes the form of the switching weight w_s of HE-FM-WE-004, which that record computes only for the QALYs of two groups, here with the other-criteria blend in place of group A QALYs and the first score less that blend in place of group B QALYs (derived). Dividing a cost by an overall value takes the form of HE-FM-ACER-001, and the second report states that such a cost-benefit ratio needs benefits on a ratio scale, which these totals lack. The partial value score has the algebra of 100 times the blend share p of HE-FM-EXD-002, which that record computes only for the expected effects of three options ordered along a frontier; here the ends are the anchors of a criterion's fixed range and run in decreasing order when lower performance is better. The weights have the algebra of the share in HE-FM-CJA-003, which that record computes for conjoint part-worth ranges, and the overall value equals the points-weighted mean (p_1 v_1 + p_2 v_2 + p_3 v_3) / (p_1 + p_2 + p_3), the form of HE-FM-CRAT-001, which computes it for member counts and expected costs (derived). The swing of HE-FM-OWSA-001 is the width of a tornado bar, not a swing weight. Notation follows the MCDA in HTA article, with v_1, v_2 and v_3 for v_j(x_aj) and V for V(a)."; HEO defines MCDA in HTA as "MCDA in HTA uses multi-criteria decision analysis to appraise health technologies on explicit, often weighted, criteria such as health gain and severity.".

column2: Designer's problem of a direct mechanism with incentive and participation constraints in its two-type screening form
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Mechanism Design. The module describes Designer's problem of a direct mechanism with incentive and participation constraints in its two-type screening form as "Maps the designer's objective, the distribution of participants' private types and a candidate allocation rule x(theta) and payment rule t(theta) to the designer's expected objective, subject to incentive compatibility, under which each type does at least as well reporting truthfully as mimicking any other type, and participation, under which each type does at least as well as by staying out, as in the article's display. The general problem is an optimisation over functions and has no calculator form. Its simplest instance, one supplier whose unit cost is low (theta_L) or high (theta_H) and a purchaser who offers a menu of output and transfer pairs, is the screening model of Laffont and Martimort, in which the allocation is a quantity q and the payment a transfer t. HE-FM-MECH-001 checks whether a given menu satisfies the four constraints and reports the information rents, HE-FM-MECH-002 gives the purchaser's second-best menu with a linear marginal value of output, and HE-CF-MECH-001 compares that menu with shutting out the high-cost type and with the complete-information benchmark when the supplier has a positive outside option. A type's payoff on its own contract, transfer less cost times quantity, takes the form of the margin in HE-FM-CTH-001 with no reimbursed share, which computes it per case of hospital care. The Ellis and McGuire records HE-FN-CTH-001 to HE-CF-CTH-001 set a payment rule for a provider whose parameters are known, with no hidden type. The article's tender profit of GBP 60,000, a margin of GBP 0.60 per pack times 100,000 packs, is a price margin times a volume, the form of HE-FM-CSKM-002 with one risk group, and the second-price rule that sets the price belongs to the auction-theory-health concept, so neither is restated here. Matching and kidney exchange rules are algorithms on a compatibility graph and have no formula record. Notation follows the Mechanism Design article for the general problem and Laffont and Martimort for the two-type case."; HEO defines Mechanism Design as "Mechanism design uses game theory to set rules, such as auctions, tenders or matching schemes, under which self-interested choices serve a chosen goal.".

column2: Incentive bonus and limited liability rent for unobserved effort paid on an imperfect indicator
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Principal-Agent Problem. The module describes Incentive bonus and limited liability rent for unobserved effort paid on an imperfect indicator as "Maps the extra cost to an agent of a high effort level, the probabilities that a verifiable indicator is met with and without that effort, and the most the agent can be made to pay the principal, to the smallest bonus per indicator met that makes the agent choose the high effort, the principal's expected payment and the agent's expected rent. This is the hidden action, or moral hazard, form of the principal-agent problem with a risk-neutral agent protected by limited liability, as in chapter 4 of Laffont and Martimort. The mechanism-design records HE-FN-MECH-001, HE-FM-MECH-001, HE-FM-MECH-002 and HE-CF-MECH-001 treat hidden information instead, a supplier's cost type known only to itself and screened with a menu of contracts, and the Ellis and McGuire records HE-FN-CTH-001 to HE-CF-CTH-001 set a mixed payment on the case and its recorded cost, both verifiable, with no payment on an indicator of unobserved effort. Demand-side moral hazard in insurance is HE-FM-MH-001 and HE-FM-MHHI-002. The expected payment is a two-branch expected value of the form of HE-FM-CHN-001, and the rent takes the form of the margin of HE-FM-CTH-001 with no reimbursed share. Whether the principal should buy the effort at all compares the gain in its expected benefit with the expected payment, condition (4.23) of Laffont and Martimort when ell = 0, a single comparison that needs no separate formula (HE-ER-PAP-002). Multitasking and gaming are described in the article without an equation. Notation follows the Principal-Agent Problem article, with the liability limit ell taken from Laffont and Martimort."; HEO defines Principal-Agent Problem as "The principal-agent problem arises when patients or payers rely on providers who know more than they do, act unobserved and may pursue other interests.".

column2: Nash equilibria of a two-player game with two strategies each
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Nash Equilibrium. The module describes Nash equilibria of a two-player game with two strategies each as "Maps the payoffs of two players, each with two pure strategies, over the four strategy pairs to the game's Nash equilibria, the pairs in which each player's strategy is a best reply to the other's, u_i(s_i*, s_-i*) >= u_i(s_i, s_-i*) for every strategy s_i of every player i, as in the article's display. The general condition over any finite strategy sets has no calculator form. For a 2 x 2 game HE-FM-NASH-001 tests each of the four cells as a pure-strategy equilibrium and classifies it as strict or weak, HE-FM-NASH-002 gives the mixed equilibrium in which each player randomises so as to leave the other indifferent, and HE-CF-NASH-001 lists every equilibrium of a game without payoff ties and values the outcome of mixed play. Each player's expected payoff at the mixed equilibrium and the expected value of an outcome measure such as total surplus are probability-weighted sums, the form of HE-FM-CHN-001, and the probability of each cell under independent mixing is the product of HE-FM-CHN-002, so neither is restated. Dominance between interventions in cost-effectiveness analysis (HE-FM-DOM-001) compares the incremental cost and effect of options for one decision maker and is a different test. The Nash bargaining solution (HE-FN-BARG-001, with the negotiated price of HE-FM-BARG-001) divides a surplus between parties who can make a binding agreement, Rubinstein's first proposer's share (HE-FM-BARG-003) comes from the perfect equilibrium of a sequential alternating-offers game, and the voluntary vaccination coverage of HE-FM-VEXT-003 is the equilibrium of a population game solved through an infection risk; all are separate records. Notation follows the Nash Equilibrium article, with u_jk and v_jk for the row and column players' payoffs when the row player chooses its strategy j and the column player its strategy k."; HEO defines Nash Equilibrium as "A Nash equilibrium is a set of strategies, one per player, from which no player, such as a payer, provider or patient, gains by changing strategy alone.".

column2: Equilibrium use, rent dissipation and corrective fee function for a shared depletable resource
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Tragedy of the Commons. The module describes Equilibrium use, rent dissipation and corrective fee function for a shared depletable resource as "Maps the value of one unit of a shared resource at full effectiveness, the private cost of a unit, the loss of value that each unit used imposes on every unit and the number of identical users to the use each user chooses when all act alone, the net value left to the group, the share of the attainable value lost and the per-unit fee that brings use back to the joint optimum. Each user keeps the whole value of a unit but bears only their own share of the loss, so the symmetric Nash equilibrium (HE-FM-TOTC-001) exceeds the joint optimum whenever there is more than one user, and the fee of HE-FM-TOTC-002 charges the part of the loss that falls on the others. The joint optimum is the efficient quantity Q_star of HE-FM-PIGT-001 with the slope of marginal private benefit b and of marginal external cost g both set to k and m set to zero, and the open-access limit (a less c) / k as the number of users grows is its Q_0 with b set to k, where the deadweight loss of HE-FM-PIGT-002 equals the whole attainable value. For a finite number of users the equilibrium total, the fee and the lost rent take the form of Q_0 and t_star of HE-FM-PIGT-001 and the deadweight loss of HE-FM-PIGT-002 with b set to k (N + 1) / N, g to k (N less 1) / N and m to zero (derived, and checked here on 448 parameter sets). Those records compute them only for b the slope of a demand curve in an otherwise undistorted market (HE-VR-PIGT-005, HE-AS-PIGT-001); these slopes exist only along the symmetric path of the users' game and depend on N, which no live record holds. The marginal external cost of one more unit is the MEC of HE-FM-EXT-001. Notation follows the Tragedy of the Commons article."; HEO defines Tragedy of the Commons as "The tragedy of the commons is the overuse of a shared resource, such as antibiotic effectiveness, when each user keeps the gain but the cost falls on all.".

column2: Expected price and equilibrium bids of a single-winner reverse auction with independent uniform costs
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Auction Theory. The module describes Expected price and equilibrium bids of a single-winner reverse auction with independent uniform costs as "Maps the lowest and highest possible unit costs c_low and c_high, the number of bidding suppliers N and, for a bid, one supplier's own cost c to the expected lowest cost E_c1, the expected price E_p the purchaser pays, the winner's expected margin M_w, the symmetric equilibrium bid b of a first-price (pay-as-bid) tender and the expected winning bid E_b, for a single-winner procurement auction in which each supplier knows only its own cost. HE-FM-AUCT-001 gives the expected costs, price and margin under the second-price rule, which by revenue equivalence is also the expected price under the first-price rule, and HE-FM-AUCT-002 gives the first-price bid and checks that its expected winning bid equals HE-FM-AUCT-001's price. HE-CF-AUCT-001 runs one tender under both rules and checks the closed forms by a seeded simulation. Both closed forms take the affine form of the Nash bargaining price HE-FM-BARG-001, a lower limit plus a weight times a range, but the weights 2 / (N + 1) and 1 / N come from order statistics of the cost draws, not from bargaining power (derived). The article's supply-risk comparison of one winner against two is an expected cost over delivery branches, HE-FM-CHN-001, with branch probabilities such as 0.81 that both suppliers deliver given by path products, HE-FM-CHN-002, so it is not restated here. The two-type screening of one supplier with a hidden cost is HE-FN-MECH-001, and the Medicare DMEPOS single payment amount, a median, maximum or 75th percentile of winning bids, is a programme rule and has no record here. Notation follows the Auction Theory article, with c_low and c_high for its lowest and highest possible unit costs."; HEO defines Auction Theory as "Auction theory in health economics studies how bidding rules in tenders set the price and supply of medicines, vaccines and medical equipment.".

column2: Medicare Shared Savings Program annual settlement of an accountable care organisation
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Accountable Care Organization. The module describes Medicare Shared Savings Program annual settlement of an accountable care organisation as "Maps an accountable care organisation's per capita benchmark, its assigned beneficiaries' per capita Medicare Parts A and B spending for the performance year and the parameters of its track to the shared savings payment CMS makes to it or the shared losses it repays, as set in 42 CFR 425.605 for the BASIC track and 425.610 for the ENHANCED track. HE-FM-ACO-001 gives the shared savings payment, gated by the minimum savings rate and capped by the performance payment limit, HE-FM-ACO-002 the shared losses of a two-sided BASIC level with its minimum loss rate and loss recoupment limit, and HE-FM-ACO-003 the shared losses of the ENHANCED track, whose loss rate falls as the quality score rises. Each settlement is gated, so the amount jumps from zero once the gap between spending and benchmark reaches the minimum rate and is then shared from the first dollar. This differs from a deductible layer such as the aggregate stop-loss payment HE-FM-ASL-001 (claims above an attachment point, capped at a maximum), the mean and variance of specific stop-loss reimbursement over a claims distribution HE-FM-ATTP-001 or the medical loss ratio rebate HE-FM-ACR-004 (the shortfall of the ratio below the standard times adjusted premium, floored at zero), all continuous in their claims or ratio argument. Only the final min step, a cap on the shared amount, takes the form of HE-FM-ASL-001 with no attachment point. The fee-for-service payments that continue underneath the settlement are not modelled, the per case blend of a fixed amount and a cost share is HE-FM-CTH-001, the margin reading of shared savings as a blend belongs to the blended-payment concept, and the expected profit per member that drives selection, payment minus expected cost, is HE-FM-CSKM-001. Notation follows the Accountable Care Organization article."; HEO defines Accountable Care Organization as "An accountable care organization (ACO) is a provider group that shares in savings if its patients' spending beats a benchmark and quality targets are met.".

column2: Spatial accessibility index function from provider capacity, population and travel times
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Geographic Accessibility of Healthcare. The module describes Spatial accessibility index function from provider capacity, population and travel times as "Maps the capacity of each provider location, the population of each residential location and the travel time or distance between every pair to an accessibility score for each residential location, in providers per head of population. Wang 2012 writes the family in one form, A_i equal to the sum over providers of S_j f(d_ij) divided by the sum over population locations of P_k f(d_kj), with f a distance decay function, so each provider's capacity is shared among the people who can reach it and each resident collects the shares within reach. HE-FM-ACCS-001 is the two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) method of Luo and Wang, in which f is 1 within a threshold travel time and 0 beyond it, and HE-FM-ACCS-002 is the gravity form with a population demand adjustment, in which f is a negative power of travel time; Luo and Wang show that the first is a special case of the second. Both are written out for the article's two practices and three neighbourhoods, and HE-CF-ACCS-001 and HE-CF-ACCS-002 run them for any number of sites. A count of providers over the residents of one bordered area is a plain ratio of the form of HE-FM-ACR-001 and is not drafted; the time cost borne by residents who travel further is HE-FM-PTC-001, and equity of use relative to need is HE-FN-HEQ-001. Notation follows the Accessibility article."; HEO defines Geographic Accessibility of Healthcare as "Accessibility is the dimension of health care access concerned with how easily people can reach services, given location, travel time, distance and cost.".

column2: Non-inferiority and superiority decision function for an active control trial
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Active Control Trial. The module describes Non-inferiority and superiority decision function for an active control trial as "Maps the proportions of patients with a favourable outcome in the test and active control arms of a two-arm randomised trial, the arm sizes, a normal critical value and a margin fixed in the protocol to the two-sided interval for the risk difference and to the readings for non-inferiority and superiority. The steps before the decision are live records. The risk difference d is the test proportion minus the control proportion, the difference of HE-FM-ARR-001 with its sign reversed, because HE-FM-ARR-001 subtracts the intervention risk of an adverse event from the comparator risk and HE-AS-ARR-002 reverses the subtraction for a beneficial outcome. Each arm's standard error is HE-FM-BINOM-004, the variance of a difference of two independent arm estimates is the sum of their variances as in HE-VR-AN-002 and HE-FM-NMA-001, and the interval limits are the Wald limits of HE-FM-AN-001. HE-FM-ACTR-001 adds the comparison of the lower limit with minus the margin and with zero. The article's economic check is a citation of live records, the incremental net health benefit being HE-FM-CET-002, its break-even shortfall in cures being HE-FM-CET-002 solved for the shortfall under the article's illustrative linear cost and QALY model (compare the break-even price of HE-FM-BEA-001), and the probability of a positive net health benefit following the z statistic of HE-FM-AN-004. Bioequivalence on the ratio scale is HE-FM-ANDA-001, and the least-cost choice once outcomes are shown to be equivalent is HE-FM-CMA-001. Notation follows the Active Control Trial article."; HEO defines Active Control Trial as "An active control trial is a randomised trial testing a new treatment against a known effective treatment, not placebo, for superiority or non-inferiority.".

column2: Sullivan active life expectancy from a period life table and dependency prevalence
column24: The module lists this mathematical function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Active Life Expectancy. The module describes Sullivan active life expectancy from a period life table and dependency prevalence as "Maps the survivors of a period life table at a starting age, the person-years it assigns to each later age band and the proportion of each band who are dependent in activities of daily living to active life expectancy, life expectancy and the expected years lived dependent at that age. Sullivan's method splits the person-years of each band by the dependency prevalence (HE-FM-ALE-001), and the Computational Function HE-CF-ALE-001 adds the standard binomial variance and a 95% interval for any number of bands. The sum takes the form of HE-FM-ASF-002 with r of 0 and of HE-FM-QALY-001, but both records are defined for utility values, while the weight here is the share of survivors free of dependency, with dependent years counted as zero. HALE weights non-healthy time by severity and draws on years lived with disability (HE-FM-DWT-001), and the years of life lost and DALY records (HE-FM-YLL-001, HE-FN-DALY-001) measure health gaps, not health expectancies. Expected care costs per person are HE-FM-COST-001 with the expected dependent years as the quantity and a cost per dependent year as the unit cost. A multistate life table follows transitions between independent, dependent and dead states; with constant rates and no recovery the expected time in each living state is HE-FM-CONT-002, and HE-FM-MKCH-002 splits expected time in a state that can be re-entered into episodes, so those records are cited, not restated. Notation follows the Active Life Expectancy article."; HEO defines Active Life Expectancy as "Active life expectancy (ALE) is the average number of years a person of a given age can expect to live free of dependency in activities of daily living.".

column2: Multi-option dominance screen
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Dominance. The module describes Multi-option dominance screen as "Flags option k as dominated when any other option in the set costs no more, produces no less health and is strictly better on at least one of the two. Flagged options are removed before sequential ICERs are calculated."; HEO defines Dominance as "Dominance in cost-effectiveness analysis excludes an option when another option, or a blend of two others, is no worse on cost or effect and better on one.".

column2: Extended dominance condition for three ordered options
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Extended Dominance. The module describes Extended dominance condition for three ordered options as "Subtracts the sequential ICER of the next more effective option from the sequential ICER of the middle of three consecutive options, ordered by expected effect. The middle option is extendedly dominated when the difference is greater than zero."; HEO defines Extended Dominance as "Extended dominance excludes an option in cost-effectiveness analysis when a blend of a less and a more effective option gives its health gain for less.".

column2: Cost of the blend that matches the middle option
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Extended Dominance. The module describes Cost of the blend that matches the middle option as "Finds the share p of the population given the more effective neighbour H, with the remainder given L, so that the blend matches the expected effect of M, then the saving of that blend against M. A positive saving means M lies above the frontier and is extendedly dominated."; HEO defines Extended Dominance as "Extended dominance excludes an option in cost-effectiveness analysis when a blend of a less and a more effective option gives its health gain for less.".

column2: Two-option CEAC at one threshold
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (CEAC). The module describes Two-option CEAC at one threshold as "Counts the probabilistic simulations in which the intervention has positive incremental net monetary benefit at threshold lambda and divides the count by the number of simulations. The indicator 1(condition) equals 1 when the condition holds and 0 otherwise. Apart from exact ties, the comparator's value is the complement."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (CEAC) as "A cost-effectiveness acceptability curve (CEAC) plots, across cost-effectiveness thresholds, the probability that each option is the most cost-effective.".

column2: Multi-option CEAC for option j
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (CEAC). The module describes Multi-option CEAC for option j as "Counts the simulations in which option j has the highest net monetary benefit among all included options at threshold lambda, and divides the count by the number of simulations. Each option's net monetary benefit in a draw is lambda times its simulated effect minus its simulated cost. With mutually exclusive options and consistent tie handling, the values for all options sum to 1 at each threshold. Because no option can exceed the maximum, the indicator 1(NMB_ij >= NMBmax_i) equals 1 exactly when option j attains the highest net monetary benefit in draw i."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (CEAC) as "A cost-effectiveness acceptability curve (CEAC) plots, across cost-effectiveness thresholds, the probability that each option is the most cost-effective.".

column2: Acceptability frontier and error probability
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (CEAC). The module describes Acceptability frontier and error probability as "Selects the option with the highest expected net monetary benefit, the mean across simulations, and takes that option's CEAC value as the cost-effectiveness acceptability frontier at threshold lambda. The error probability is the complement, the share of simulations in which the chosen option does not have the highest net monetary benefit."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (CEAC) as "A cost-effectiveness acceptability curve (CEAC) plots, across cost-effectiveness thresholds, the probability that each option is the most cost-effective.".

column2: Expected net monetary benefit from probabilistic simulations
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Net Benefit. The module describes Expected net monetary benefit from probabilistic simulations as "Averages option j's net monetary benefit over N probabilistic simulations, each valuing the simulated health effect at threshold lambda and subtracting the simulated cost. Because net benefit is linear in cost and effect, the result equals lambda times the mean effect minus the mean cost from the same simulations. The option-level formula on the net monetary benefit page is the deterministic counterpart."; HEO defines Expected Net Benefit as "Expected net benefit is the mean net benefit of a healthcare option across parameter uncertainty at a set threshold; the option with the highest is chosen.".

column2: Expected net health benefit from probabilistic simulations
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Net Benefit. The module describes Expected net health benefit from probabilistic simulations as "Averages option j's net health benefit, its simulated health effect minus its simulated cost divided by lambda, over N simulations. The result equals the expected net monetary benefit divided by lambda, so both forms rank options identically at any positive threshold. NICE asks for expected net health benefits alongside ICERs, using £25,000 and £35,000 per QALY."; HEO defines Expected Net Benefit as "Expected net benefit is the mean net benefit of a healthcare option across parameter uncertainty at a set threshold; the option with the highest is chosen.".

column2: Per-person EVPI from probabilistic draws
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Value of Information. The module describes Per-person EVPI from probabilistic draws as "Averages, over S equally weighted draws, the highest net benefit available in each draw, the value of choosing with perfect information, and subtracts the highest expected net benefit among the options, the value of the decision made on current information. The result is the expected opportunity loss of the current decision per person and an upper bound on the value of research for that person."; HEO defines Value of Information as "Value of information (VOI) analysis estimates the expected benefit of reducing decision uncertainty, to judge whether more research is worth its cost.".

column2: Population EVPI over the decision's lifetime
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Value of Information. The module describes Population EVPI over the decision's lifetime as "Multiplies per-person EVPI by the discounted number of people expected to face the decision in each period while it remains relevant. The result is compared with the cost of research: when it is below the cost of any feasible study, further research is not worthwhile on these grounds."; HEO defines Value of Information as "Value of information (VOI) analysis estimates the expected benefit of reducing decision uncertainty, to judge whether more research is worth its cost.".

column2: EVPPI for a subset of parameters
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Value of Information. The module describes EVPPI for a subset of parameters as "Values perfect information about a subset phi of the parameters, with the remaining parameters psi still uncertain. The inner expectation averages net benefit over psi given phi, the maximum picks the best option for that value of phi, the outer expectation averages over phi, and the value of the current decision is subtracted. The expected value of sample information replaces knowledge of phi with the data from a proposed study."; HEO defines Value of Information as "Value of information (VOI) analysis estimates the expected benefit of reducing decision uncertainty, to judge whether more research is worth its cost.".

column2: Swing of a one-way bar
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept One-Way Sensitivity Analysis. The module describes Swing of a one-way bar as "Takes the absolute difference between the model outputs at the lower and upper values of input j, each run with all other inputs at their base-case values. The swing is the width of the input's bar in a tornado diagram, and bars are ordered with the widest at the top."; HEO defines One-Way Sensitivity Analysis as "One-way sensitivity analysis (OWSA) varies one model input at a time, holding the rest at base case, to show which inputs drive cost-effectiveness results.".

column2: Switching value by linear interpolation
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept One-Way Sensitivity Analysis. The module describes Switching value by linear interpolation as "Finds the value of input j at which incremental net monetary benefit equals zero by interpolating between the results at the input's lower and upper values, with all other inputs at base case. The result is exact when incremental net monetary benefit is linear in the input and an approximation otherwise. NICE calls this value a switching value and asks how far it lies from the current best estimate."; HEO defines One-Way Sensitivity Analysis as "One-way sensitivity analysis (OWSA) varies one model input at a time, holding the rest at base case, to show which inputs drive cost-effectiveness results.".

column2: Supply-side threshold from marginal spending and health
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness Threshold. The module describes Supply-side threshold from marginal spending and health as "Divides a change in health-care expenditure by the change in health it produces through the services funded or displaced. The result is the additional cost that has to be imposed on the system to forgo one QALY through displacement, the definition Claxton and colleagues used to estimate the threshold for the English NHS."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Threshold as "A cost-effectiveness threshold is the maximum cost per QALY gained that a health system treats as value for money when deciding which treatments to fund.".

column2: Incremental net health benefit at threshold k
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness Threshold. The module describes Incremental net health benefit at threshold k as "Converts the incremental cost of an intervention into the health expected to be displaced elsewhere, Delta_C divided by k, and subtracts it from the incremental health gain. A positive value means population health increases overall; a negative value means the health gained does not offset the health lost from care not funded elsewhere. It gives the same decision as incremental net monetary benefit at the same threshold."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Threshold as "A cost-effectiveness threshold is the maximum cost per QALY gained that a health system treats as value for money when deciding which treatments to fund.".

column2: Transition probability from a constant rate
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Transition Probability. The module describes Transition probability from a constant rate as "Converts a constant event rate into the probability that the event occurs within an interval of length Delta, among people at risk at the start of the interval. The function exp is the exponential function."; HEO defines Transition Probability as "A transition probability is the chance of moving from one health state to another, or staying, during one cycle of a Markov or state-transition model.".

column2: Constant rate from a transition probability
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Transition Probability. The module describes Constant rate from a transition probability as "Recovers the constant rate implied by a probability observed over an interval of length Delta. The function log is the natural logarithm. The rate can then be rescaled to any cycle length or combined with a hazard ratio."; HEO defines Transition Probability as "A transition probability is the chance of moving from one health state to another, or staying, during one cycle of a Markov or state-transition model.".

column2: Transition probability rescaled to a new cycle length
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Transition Probability. The module describes Transition probability rescaled to a new cycle length as "Converts a probability observed over one interval into the probability for a model cycle of a different length, under a constant hazard. It combines the two conversions above without computing the rate explicitly."; HEO defines Transition Probability as "A transition probability is the chance of moving from one health state to another, or staying, during one cycle of a Markov or state-transition model.".

column2: Destination probabilities under constant competing hazards
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Transition Probability. The module describes Destination probabilities under constant competing hazards as "Splits the probability of leaving a state within an interval between two absorbing destinations with constant cause-specific hazards h_1 and h_2. The total exit probability depends on the summed hazard, and each destination receives its share h_1 or h_2 of that sum."; HEO defines Transition Probability as "A transition probability is the chance of moving from one health state to another, or staying, during one cycle of a Markov or state-transition model.".

column2: Hazard ratio from treatment and comparator hazards
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Hazard Ratio. The module describes Hazard ratio from treatment and comparator hazards as "Divides the treatment-group hazard by the comparator-group hazard at the same time. A value below 1 means a lower hazard of the named event in the treatment group."; HEO defines Hazard Ratio as "A hazard ratio (HR) is the ratio of the event rates (hazards) in two groups, the usual measure of a treatment effect on survival in trials and HTA models.".

column2: Hazard ratio from a Cox regression coefficient
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Hazard Ratio. The module describes Hazard ratio from a Cox regression coefficient as "Converts the estimated coefficient for a binary treatment covariate in a Cox or other proportional hazards regression into the hazard ratio. The function exp is the exponential function."; HEO defines Hazard Ratio as "A hazard ratio (HR) is the ratio of the event rates (hazards) in two groups, the usual measure of a treatment effect on survival in trials and HTA models.".

column2: Treatment survival from a baseline curve under proportional hazards
column24: The module lists this formula on the formulae page of the HEO concept Hazard Ratio. The module describes Treatment survival from a baseline curve under proportional hazards as "Applies a constant hazard ratio to the comparator survival probability at time t to give the treatment survival probability at the same time. It follows because the cumulative hazard of the treatment group is HR times that of the comparator.
