It chains HE-FM-BIC-001 and HE-FM-BIC-003, and the second and third steps use the whole vector produced by the step before, so the inputs are lists of models rather than the single values the formulae take. The count may be the number of uncensored events, as in HE-FM-BIC-001, or the number of patients, which gives the patient-count form recorded on the Akaike information criterion page."; HEO defines Bayesian Information Criterion as "Bayesian information criterion (BIC) ranks models fitted to the same data, such as HTA survival curves, by fit with a penalty that grows with sample size.".

column2: Bootstrap standard error and normal interval from a vector of replicates
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Bootstrap Standard Error. The module describes Bootstrap standard error and normal interval from a vector of replicates as "Takes the vector of bootstrap replicate values produced by resampling, together with the estimate from the original data, and returns the bootstrap standard error and a normal interval centred on the original estimate. It applies HE-FM-BSE-001 to the whole vector and uses the result in a second step, so the inputs are the stored replicates and the original estimate rather than the single values the formula's variables hold."; HEO defines Bootstrap Standard Error as "Bootstrap standard error is the standard deviation of an estimate, such as mean trial cost, recalculated across many resamples of the observed data.".

column2: Ideal paired bootstrap standard error of incremental net benefit from patient-level data
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Bootstrap Standard Error. The module describes Ideal paired bootstrap standard error of incremental net benefit from patient-level data as "Takes patient-level costs and QALYs in each arm and a threshold, and returns incremental net monetary benefit and its ideal bootstrap standard error under paired resampling within arms, the limit that the Monte Carlo estimate approaches as B grows. It forms each patient's net benefit, applies the closed form for a mean, HE-FM-BSE-002, within each arm, and adds the two variances because the arms are resampled independently. Working with each patient's net benefit keeps the cost and effect covariance that HE-FM-BSE-003 carries as a separate term."; HEO defines Bootstrap Standard Error as "Bootstrap standard error is the standard deviation of an estimate, such as mean trial cost, recalculated across many resamples of the observed data.".

column2: Brier score, Murphy partition and scaled score from predicted risks and outcomes
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Brier Score. The module describes Brier score, Murphy partition and scaled score from predicted risks and outcomes as "Takes a vector of predicted risks and a vector of observed binary outcomes, one entry per patient, and returns the Brier score, its Murphy partition and the scaled score. It applies HE-FM-BRIER-001 to the vectors, groups patients by identical predicted value to build the counts and observed rates that HE-FM-BRIER-002 needs, and then scales the score with HE-FM-BRIER-003, so the inputs are patient-level vectors rather than the group summaries the formulae take."; HEO defines Brier Score as "The Brier score is the mean squared difference between predicted risks and observed binary outcomes, used to judge prediction models; lower is better.".

column2: Exact binomial probability, cumulative probability and percentiles of an event count
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Binomial Distribution. The module describes Exact binomial probability, cumulative probability and percentiles of an event count as "Takes the inputs a model or a study summary usually holds, the number of patients, the event probability, a count and two percentile levels, and returns the exact probability of the count, the cumulative probability of at most that count and two percentiles of the count. The cumulative probability sums the probability function HE-FM-BINOM-001 over every count up to r, and each percentile is found by searching for the smallest count whose cumulative probability reaches the level, because the binomial percent point function has no closed form. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables: the levels a_lo and a_hi are extra, and the outputs include percentiles that the formula cannot give."; HEO defines Binomial Distribution as "The binomial distribution models how many of a fixed number of patients have an event when each has the same probability and outcomes are independent.".

column2: Likelihood ratio test p-value and critical value from two fitted models
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Chi-Square Distribution. The module describes Likelihood ratio test p-value and critical value from two fitted models as "Takes the two fitted models' maximised log-likelihoods and parameter counts and a significance level, and returns the likelihood ratio statistic, its degrees of freedom, the p-value and the critical value. It applies HE-FM-CHISQ-006 and then evaluates the right-hand tail of chi-square, which for most degrees of freedom has no closed form: it is the regularised upper incomplete gamma function with shape df/2 at LR/2, computed numerically by Excel CHISQ.DIST.RT, R pchisq and Python scipy.stats.chi2.sf, while the critical value needs the numerical inverse. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables: the level alpha is extra, and the outputs include a p-value and a critical value that the formula cannot give."; HEO defines Chi-Square Distribution as "The chi-square distribution describes a sum of squared independent standard normals and is the reference for likelihood ratio, heterogeneity and fit tests.".

column2: Kaplan-Meier curve, restricted mean and tail share from entry months, event times and a data cut-off
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Administrative Censoring. The module describes Kaplan-Meier curve, restricted mean and tail share from entry months, event times and a data cut-off as "Takes the data a trial arm usually holds, each patient's entry month, the event time where an event was seen by the cut-off, and the cut-off itself, and returns the censoring times, the observed records, the Kaplan-Meier curve, the restricted mean to the last observed follow-up and the share of mean survival from an exponential tail. It builds the risk sets n_j and deaths d_j of HE-FM-ADMC-002 from the observed records of HE-FM-ADMC-001, then applies HE-FM-ADMC-003 and HE-FM-ADMC-004. The inputs therefore differ from the Kaplan-Meier formula's variables: the formula takes the counts at one event time, while the function derives every count from patient-level data. When no tail hazard is supplied it uses events divided by person-time, HE-FM-AER-002."; HEO defines Administrative Censoring as "Administrative censoring is right censoring that occurs when a trial's planned end of follow-up or data cut-off arrives before a patient has the event.".

column2: Community-rated pool from group counts and expected costs to premium, cross-subsidies and fund balance
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Community Rating. The module describes Community-rated pool from group counts and expected costs to premium, cross-subsidies and fund balance as "Takes the inputs a regulator or insurer usually holds for a community-rated pool, the number of members and the expected annual cost in each risk group, and returns the community-rated premium, the cross-subsidy per member of each group, the risk equalisation transfer per member of each group and the balance of the equalisation fund. It applies HE-FM-CRAT-001 and then HE-FM-CRAT-002 and HE-FM-CRAT-003 with the premium it has just computed, so the later steps use the result of the first. Running it again with changed counts shows how the premium and the cross-subsidies move when low-risk members leave."; HEO defines Community Rating as "Community rating is a health insurance pricing rule that stops premiums varying with health or claims, allowing at most limited variation by age or area.".

column2: Cohort trace run with rewards accumulated under a counting rule
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cohort Simulation. The module describes Cohort trace run with rewards accumulated under a counting rule as "Runs a cohort simulation from the inputs a model holds, a starting distribution, a transition matrix, the reward per cycle in each state, a number of cycles, a counting rule and a discount rate per cycle, and returns the cohort trace and the expected total outcome per person. It first builds the trace row by row with the cohort update HE-FM-MM-001, then forms the counting weights and discount factors and applies HE-FM-CSIM-001. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables: the formula takes the trace rows, weights and discount factors as given, while the function generates them."; HEO defines Cohort Simulation as "Cohort simulation runs a Markov or other state-transition model by moving the expected shares of a hypothetical cohort between health states each cycle.".

column2: Trial summary data to an illustrative QALY gain through Cohen's d
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cohen's d. The module describes Trial summary data to an illustrative QALY gain through Cohen's d as "Takes the summary data a trial report gives, group means, standard deviations and sizes, together with the external inputs a cost-utility model needs, a comparator response probability, utility values for responders and non-responders and a duration, and returns an illustrative QALY gain per person. It chains four steps: Cohen's d from HE-FM-CD-001, the logistic conversion to an odds ratio from HE-FM-CD-002, the intervention response probability from the comparator probability and the odds ratio as in HE-FM-NMA-004, and the extra proportion responding multiplied by the utility difference and the duration. The inputs therefore differ from either formula's variables."; HEO defines Cohen's d as "Cohen's d is a standardised effect size: the difference between two group means divided by their pooled standard deviation, used to compare studies.".

column2: Case weights, hospital casemix, case payment and cost ratio from costing data
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Case Weight. The module describes Case weights, hospital casemix, case payment and cost ratio from costing data as "Takes the cases and mean cost of every group in a costing sample, one hospital's cases by group, a base rate, an adjustment factor and the hospital's actual cost, and returns the group weights, the hospital's casemix and average weight, its total case payment and its casemix-adjusted cost ratio. It chains HE-FM-CWT-001, HE-FM-CWT-002 summed over the hospital's cases, and HE-FM-CWT-003, so its inputs are costing-sample and hospital data rather than the symbols of any one formula. The hospital's average weight is its case mix index, returned as an intermediate output."; HEO defines Case Weight as "Case weight is a relative value for a diagnosis-related group showing its expected cost against the average case, used to scale payment from a base rate.".

column2: Proportion of days covered from a same-drug fill history with overlap shifting
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Proportion of Days Covered. The module describes Proportion of days covered from a same-drug fill history with overlap shifting as "Takes a patient's fill history for one drug, as dispensing days and days' supply, and the last day of the observation period, and returns the PDC. It sorts the fills by date, shifts each early refill to the day after the previous supply ends (HE-FM-PDC-002), counts the covered days on or before the end day (HE-FM-PDC-003) and divides by the days from the first fill to the end day inclusive (HE-FM-PDC-001). The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables: the formula needs the covered days and the period length, and the function builds both from the raw fills. An optional switch merges overlaps without shifting, for a sensitivity analysis of the overlap rule."; HEO defines Proportion of Days Covered as "The proportion of days covered (PDC) is the share of days in a period on which pharmacy refill records show a patient had medicine, each day counted once.".

column2: Medication possession ratio variants from a fill history and window
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Medication Possession Ratio. The module describes Medication possession ratio variants from a fill history and window as "Takes a patient's fill history for one medicine, as dispensing days and days' supply, and the last day of the observation period, and returns the fixed-interval MPR (HE-FM-MPR-001), the refill-interval MPR including the last fill (HE-FM-MPR-002), the MPRm excluding it (HE-FM-MPR-003) and the capped fixed-interval MPR (HE-FM-MPR-004). It keeps the fills dispensed on or before the end day, sorts them by date, and builds each denominator from the first and last dispensing days. The inputs therefore differ from the formulas' variables: the formulas need D, f_1, f_n and S_n, and the function derives them from the raw fills."; HEO defines Medication Possession Ratio as "The medication possession ratio (MPR) is the total days' supply dispensed divided by the days in the period. Unlike PDC, it can exceed 1 unless capped.".

column2: Begg test from study effect estimates and standard errors
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Begg Test. The module describes Begg test from study effect estimates and standard errors as "Takes the effect estimates of K studies on an approximately normal scale and their standard errors, and returns Kendall's tau, the normal statistic and its two-sided p-value. It computes the inverse-variance weights and pooled estimate (HE-FM-ADMA-001), standardises each estimate (HE-FM-BEGG-002), compares every pair of studies once by the signs of their differences in standardised effect and in variance, and applies HE-FM-BEGG-001 to the counts. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables: the formula needs the pair counts, and the function builds them from the raw estimates."; HEO defines Begg Test as "The Begg test is a rank correlation test (Kendall's tau) for small-study effects in a meta-analysis, a possible sign of publication bias.".

column2: Hazard ratio, interval and cycle probabilities from event counts and person-time
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Hazard Ratio. The module describes Hazard ratio, interval and cycle probabilities from event counts and person-time as "Takes the counts a trial report or registry extract usually gives, the events and person-time at risk in each arm, with the model's cycle length, and returns everything a cohort model needs from them: the two constant hazards, the hazard ratio (HE-FM-HR-005), its approximate 95% interval (HE-FM-HR-006), and the comparator and treatment probabilities of the event in one cycle (HE-FM-HR-004). The steps are chained, so later outputs use earlier ones. The inputs therefore differ from the formulas' variables: the transition probability formula needs p_C and HR, and the function derives both from the raw counts."; HEO defines Hazard Ratio as "A hazard ratio (HR) is the ratio of the event rates (hazards) in two groups, the usual measure of a treatment effect on survival in trials and HTA models.".

column2: Markov cycle probabilities and survival trace from a Weibull cumulative hazard
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cumulative Hazard. The module describes Markov cycle probabilities and survival trace from a Weibull cumulative hazard as "Takes the parameters of a fitted Weibull curve written as H(t) = lambda t^gamma, the model's cycle length and number of cycles, and an optional hazard ratio, and returns for every cycle the cumulative hazard at its end, survival, the cumulative hazard increment, the control cycle probability (HE-FM-CUMH-002) and the treated probability under proportional hazards (as HE-FM-HR-004). The inputs differ from the formula's: it builds the whole column of H values from two curve parameters before converting each increment."; HEO defines Cumulative Hazard as "Cumulative hazard, H(t), is the hazard rate summed over time in survival models. Survival equals exp(-H(t)), and unlike a probability H(t) can exceed 1.".

column2: Feldstein and Gruber deadweight loss reduction across insurance units
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Deadweight Loss. The module describes Feldstein and Gruber deadweight loss reduction across insurance units as "Takes each insurance unit's spending and coinsurance rate under the existing plan, the new coinsurance rate and a constant price elasticity, and returns each unit's spending under the new rate, its reduction in deadweight loss (HE-FM-DWL-003) and the average across units, the calculation Feldstein and Gruber ran for each individual in their survey data. The inputs differ from the formula's: E_1 is derived from the elasticity instead of being entered."; HEO defines Deadweight Loss as "Deadweight loss is the net loss of total surplus when a tax, subsidy, market power or insurance drives a wedge between price and marginal cost.".

column2: Maxdiff and sequential probabilities for every best and worst pair in a choice set
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Best-Worst Scaling. The module describes Maxdiff and sequential probabilities for every best and worst pair in a choice set as "Takes the utilities of the items in one choice set and returns the probability of every ordered best and worst pair under the maxdiff model (HE-FM-BWS-003) and under the sequential model (HE-FM-BWS-004), as two J by J matrices with zeros on the diagonal. The input is the whole vector of utilities rather than the summary sums the formulas take, and the function evaluates all J(J minus 1) pairs, which shows how far the two models disagree on the same utilities."; HEO defines Best-Worst Scaling as "Best-worst scaling (BWS) is a stated preference method in which people pick the best and worst item in each set, to rank priorities or value health states.".

column2: Interim look with posterior and predictive probabilities and the stopping decision
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Bayesian Adaptive Design. The module describes Interim look with posterior and predictive probabilities and the stopping decision as "Takes the prior mean and standard deviation, the interim estimate and its standard error, the planned second stage's standard error and the protocol's three thresholds, and returns the posterior summary (HE-FM-BAD-001), the boundary and predictive probability (HE-FM-BAD-002) and the protocol decision. It uses the inverse normal for the final rule instead of a rounded z_c, and the normal distribution function, which the formulas leave to Phi."; HEO defines Bayesian Adaptive Design as "Bayesian adaptive design is a clinical trial design in which pre-set rules on posterior or predictive probabilities trigger changes such as early stopping.".

column2: Lee and Liu predictive probability from responses so far
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Bayesian Adaptive Design. The module describes Lee and Liu predictive probability from responses so far as "Takes the responses and patients so far, the maximum sample size, the standard treatment's response rate, the final threshold and the beta prior, and returns the beta-binomial weights, the final posterior probabilities and the predictive probability (HE-FM-BAD-004). The inputs are the trial counts, from which the function builds both columns with the beta-binomial and beta distribution functions, which have no closed form in the calculator."; HEO defines Bayesian Adaptive Design as "Bayesian adaptive design is a clinical trial design in which pre-set rules on posterior or predictive probabilities trigger changes such as early stopping.".

column2: New quantities of several products from an own and cross price elasticity matrix
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cross-Price Elasticity. The module describes New quantities of several products from an own and cross price elasticity matrix as "Takes current quantities and prices of several products, their new prices and a matrix of own-price (diagonal) and cross-price (off-diagonal) elasticities, and returns each product's new quantity under constant elasticities (HE-FM-XPE-003 extended to any number of prices), the calculation behind policy models that apply an elasticity matrix to sales or to individual records. The inputs differ from the formula's: a whole matrix and price vectors instead of two prices."; HEO defines Cross-Price Elasticity as "Cross-price elasticity measures how demand for one good responds to a change in another good's price: positive for substitutes, negative for complements.".

column2: Group-time effects and event-time averages from cohort mean outcomes
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Difference-in-Differences. The module describes Group-time effects and event-time averages from cohort mean outcomes as "Takes a table of mean outcomes by adoption cohort and period, with never-treated units in the last row, the adoption period of each cohort and the number of units in each cohort, and returns every post-adoption ATT(g,t) (HE-FM-DID-004) and their averages by time since adoption e, weighting cohorts by size among those observed at e, as in Callaway and Sant'Anna's event-study aggregation. The inputs differ from the formula's: a whole panel of means instead of four."; HEO defines Difference-in-Differences as "Difference-in-differences (DiD) estimates a policy's causal effect by comparing outcome changes over time in an exposed group and a comparison group.".

column2: Decision curve from predicted risks and outcomes over a threshold grid
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Decision Curve Analysis. The module describes Decision curve from predicted risks and outcomes over a threshold grid as "Takes each patient's predicted risk and observed outcome and a grid of thresholds, and returns at each threshold the net benefit of the model (HE-FM-DCA-001), of intervening in everyone (HE-FM-DCA-002) and of intervening in no one (zero), with net interventions avoided per 100 against intervening in everyone (HE-FM-DCA-003). The inputs differ from the formula's: the true and false positive counts are derived from the risks for each threshold instead of being entered."; HEO defines Decision Curve Analysis as "Decision curve analysis (DCA) plots the net benefit of a prediction model or test across risk thresholds against treating all or no patients.".

column2: Comorbidity-adjusted and cause-attributed YLDs for any number of independent conditions
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Disability Weight. The module describes Comorbidity-adjusted and cause-attributed YLDs for any number of independent conditions as "Takes the population size, each condition's prevalence and its disability weight, enumerates every combination of conditions with its probability under independence, applies the multiplicative combined weight (HE-FM-DWT-002) and apportions it in proportion to stand-alone weights (HE-FM-DWT-003). It returns adjusted total YLDs (HE-FM-DWT-004), YLDs attributed to each condition and the unadjusted sum. This is the expected value that GBD 2010's microsimulation of 20,000 individuals estimates by sampling. The inputs differ from the formula's: prevalences and weights for any number of conditions instead of two YLD rates."; HEO defines Disability Weight as "A disability weight is a value from 0 (full health) to 1 (equivalent to death) rating health loss in a non-fatal state, used to calculate YLDs and DALYs.".

column2: K-means clustering with within-cluster sum of squares and silhouettes
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cluster Analysis. The module describes K-means clustering with within-cluster sum of squares and silhouettes as "Runs k-means (Lloyd's algorithm) from given starting centroids on any number of units and clustering variables, and returns each unit's cluster, the cluster means, W(K), the share of scatter removed (HE-FM-CLU-003) and each unit's silhouette (HE-FM-CLU-005). The inputs differ from the formula's: a data matrix and starting centroids instead of two sums of squares."; HEO defines Cluster Analysis as "Cluster analysis is an unsupervised method that sorts patients, providers or countries into groups whose members are more alike than those in other groups.".

column2: Least-squares part-worths, fit and relative importance from a ratings design
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Conjoint Analysis. The module describes Least-squares part-worths, fit and relative importance from a ratings design as "Fits the additive part-worth model to one respondent's ratings by least squares on dummy-coded attributes for any design, balanced or not, and returns the intercept and part-worths, R squared, each attribute's range and its relative importance (HE-FM-CJA-003). The inputs differ from the formula's: a design matrix and a vector of ratings instead of two mean ratings."; HEO defines Conjoint Analysis as "Conjoint analysis is a family of stated preference methods estimating how people value treatment or service attributes from ratings, rankings or choices.".

column2: Transition probability matrix from an intensity matrix by the matrix exponential
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Continuous Model. The module describes Transition probability matrix from an intensity matrix by the matrix exponential as "Computes the transition probability matrix over any interval from an intensity matrix of any size, P(t) = exp(tQ), by scaling and squaring a truncated Taylor series, for models with recovery or more states where no closed form like HE-FM-CONT-001 is at hand. The inputs differ from the formula's: a whole intensity matrix instead of three named rates."; HEO defines Continuous Model as "A continuous model is a decision model run in continuous time rather than fixed cycles, so health events can occur at any moment, governed by rates.".

column2: Bang and Tsiatis weighted mean cost from patient-level censored data
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Dependent Censoring. The module describes Bang and Tsiatis weighted mean cost from patient-level censored data as "Computes the Bang and Tsiatis simple weighted mean cost from patient-level data: it sorts patients by time, estimates the Kaplan-Meier probability of remaining uncensored with censoring as the event, weights each complete case by its inverse and averages over all patients, returning also the full-sample and complete-case means for comparison. The inputs differ from the formula's: raw times, status flags and costs instead of censoring probabilities."; HEO defines Dependent Censoring as "Dependent censoring occurs when the chance of being censored is linked to a patient's risk of the event, so standard survival estimates can be biased.".

column2: Gaussian process posterior and expected improvement over candidate values from any number of runs
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Bayesian Optimisation. The module describes Gaussian process posterior and expected improvement over candidate values from any number of runs as "Computes the Gaussian process posterior mean, standard deviation and expected improvement over a set of candidate values from any number of runs, with an optional noise variance, so that the next run can be chosen as the candidate with the highest expected improvement. The inputs differ from the formula's: vectors of evaluated values, losses and candidates instead of three correlations, and the normal distribution function is evaluated in the code."; HEO defines Bayesian Optimisation as "Bayesian optimisation seeks the inputs that optimise a costly function, such as a model's fit to calibration targets, using a surrogate to pick each run.".

column2: Simple exponential smoothing through a series with its sum of squared errors and next forecast
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Demand Forecasting. The module describes Simple exponential smoothing through a series with its sum of squared errors and next forecast as "Runs simple exponential smoothing through a whole series from a starting level, returning the one-step fitted values, their errors, the sum of squared errors (SSE) and the forecast for the next period. The inputs differ from the formula's: a series and a starting level instead of one observation and one forecast. Running it over a grid of alpha values and keeping the one with the lowest SSE reproduces the estimation the textbook describes."; HEO defines Demand Forecasting as "Demand forecasting projects future use of health services and medicines, and the staff needed, from past utilisation, population change and other drivers.".

column2: Net monetary benefit of two triage tests over a prevalence range and the break-even prevalence
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Diagnostic Accuracy. The module describes Net monetary benefit of two triage tests over a prevalence range and the break-even prevalence as "Compares two tests by net monetary benefit over a range of prevalences and returns the prevalence at which they tie, so that the preferred test can be read for any setting. The inputs differ from the formula's: two sets of accuracy and cost, and a vector of prevalences. With p_even the break-even prevalence, test A is preferred above it when G (Se_A minus Se_B) plus L (Sp_B minus Sp_A) is positive, as when A is the more sensitive and B the more specific test, and below it otherwise."; HEO defines Diagnostic Accuracy as "Diagnostic accuracy is how well a test agrees with a reference standard in detecting a target condition, usually reported as sensitivity and specificity.".

column2: Left-truncated Kaplan-Meier curve and restricted mean from entry, exit and event records
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Left Truncation. The module describes Left-truncated Kaplan-Meier curve and restricted mean from entry, exit and event records as "Builds the left-truncated Kaplan-Meier curve and its restricted mean from patient records, applying HE-FM-LTR-002 at every event time. The inputs differ from the formula's: whole vectors of entry times, exit times and event indicators instead of counts at one time."; HEO defines Left Truncation as "Left truncation (delayed entry) occurs when people join a survival analysis risk set after time zero and are observed only if still event free at entry.".

column2: Provider payment rules compared by chosen stay, net benefit and margin
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Contract Theory. The module describes Provider payment rules compared by chosen stay, net benefit and margin as "Compares payment rules, each a pair of fixed part and reimbursed share, by the stay the provider chooses and the resulting patient benefit, cost, payment and margin, so that a payer can see which rule gives the largest benefit net of cost and who keeps the surplus. The inputs differ from the formula's: vectors of rules and the parameters of a quadratic patient benefit B(q) = b_0 q minus b_1 q squared / 2, whose marginal benefit is b_0 minus b_1 q."; HEO defines Contract Theory as "Contract theory studies how contracts, such as provider payment rules, can align incentives when actions or information are hidden or cannot be verified.".

column2: Budget-neutral conversion factor and fee changes for a schedule of services
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Conversion Factor. The module describes Budget-neutral conversion factor and fee changes for a schedule of services as "Recomputes a whole schedule after a revaluation: the budget neutrality multiplier, the adjusted conversion factor, every service's fee before and after, its percentage change and the spending check. The inputs differ from the formula's: vectors of volumes and of old and new relative value units for any number of services, rather than two named services."; HEO defines Conversion Factor as "Conversion factor (CF) is the money amount per relative value unit that turns fee schedule relative values, such as Medicare RVUs, into payment amounts.".

column2: Validation table and flagged share to corrected prevalence, database PPV and flagged-cohort cost
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Criterion Validity. The module describes Validation table and flagged share to corrected prevalence, database PPV and flagged-cohort cost as "Runs the whole chain from a validation study to a corrected cost estimate: sensitivity, specificity and PPV from the validation two-by-two table, the Rogan-Gladen prevalence in the database from its flagged share, the PPV there, the flagged-cohort mean cost in each population, the inflation of the cohort size and the total cost of flagged patients against true cases. The inputs differ from the formula's: the four validation counts, the database's flagged share and size, and the two group costs."; HEO defines Criterion Validity as "Criterion validity is the degree to which a measure's scores agree with a gold standard for the same concept, assessed at the same time or later.".

column2: Gamma deviance residuals, unit deviances and model deviance for a set of patient costs
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Deviance Residual. The module describes Gamma deviance residuals, unit deviances and model deviance for a set of patient costs as "Computes the gamma deviance residuals for a whole set of patients, with the Pearson residuals, the unit deviances, the model deviance and the rank of each patient by the size of the deviance residual, so the worst-fitted patients can be listed in input order. The inputs differ from the formula's: a vector of positive costs and, optionally, a vector of fitted means; when the fitted means are omitted the intercept-only fit, the sample mean, is used."; HEO defines Deviance Residual as "A deviance residual is a signed measure of how poorly a generalised linear or survival model fits each patient; in a GLM its squares sum to the deviance.".

column2: Exponential survival fit with martingale and deviance residuals for every patient
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Deviance Residual. The module describes Exponential survival fit with martingale and deviance residuals for every patient as "Fits a constant hazard to patient-level survival times by maximum likelihood, then returns each patient's fitted cumulative hazard, martingale residual and deviance residual, the sum of the martingale residuals and the deviance of the exponential model, in input order. The inputs differ from the formula's: vectors of observed times and event indicators in place of a given cumulative hazard."; HEO defines Deviance Residual as "A deviance residual is a signed measure of how poorly a generalised linear or survival model fits each patient; in a GLM its squares sum to the deviance.".

column2: Distribution-based yardsticks and reliable change classification for a cohort of paired scores
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Distribution-Based MID. The module describes Distribution-based yardsticks and reliable change classification for a cohort of paired scores as "Computes the five yardsticks of the article from a sample's baseline standard deviation and reliability, then classifies every patient's change as a reliable gain, a reliable loss or neither and returns the share in each class. The inputs differ from the formulas': vectors of paired scores for a cohort, the baseline standard deviation and the reliability, with the 1.96 multiplier as an option."; HEO defines Distribution-Based MID as "A distribution-based MID is a minimal important difference estimated from score spread or instrument reliability, such as half a standard deviation.".

column2: Combined utility, QALY gain and cost per QALY under three combination rules for any number of conditions
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Disutility. The module describes Combined utility, QALY gain and cost per QALY under three combination rules for any number of conditions as "Combines any number of single-condition utilities on a shared baseline under the three TSD 12 rules, and returns for each rule the combined utility, the utility without the last condition, the QALY gain from avoiding the last condition over a stated duration and the cost per QALY gained. The inputs differ from the formula's: a vector of single-condition utilities of any length, a duration and a cost per case avoided. TSD 12 and the article give the rules for two conditions; applying the same rule to more conditions (sum of decrements, product of ratios, lowest value) is the convention stated here; TSD 12 section 3.2.1 notes that very little research has explored the accuracy of the methods for more than two simultaneous conditions."; HEO defines Disutility as "Disutility is the loss of utility caused by a health state, adverse event or treatment, measured from a stated baseline and used to reduce QALYs.".

column2: Dose ladder with Emax responses, shared and whole-vial course costs and incremental cost per extra responder
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Dose Response. The module describes Dose ladder with Emax responses, shared and whole-vial course costs and incremental cost per extra responder as "Evaluates a ladder of doses: the sigmoid Emax response and extra responders over placebo at each dose, the course cost with vial sharing (cost in proportion to dose) and with whole single-use vials, the average cost per extra responder, and the incremental cost per extra responder along the cost-effectiveness frontier, with dominated doses left without a ratio. The inputs differ from the formula's: a vector of doses in any order, the vial size and price and the number of administrations per course."; HEO defines Dose Response as "Dose response is the relationship between the amount of a drug or exposure and the size or probability of its effect, used in dose selection and HTA.".

column2: Discounted cost per QALY of several programmes' yearly streams under a list of cost and health rate pairs
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Differential Discounting. The module describes Discounted cost per QALY of several programmes' yearly streams under a list of cost and health rate pairs as "Discounts each programme's yearly cost and QALY streams under every pair of rates in a list, returns the discounted totals and ratios, and marks the programme with the lowest ratio under each pair. The inputs differ from the formula's: whole streams by year for any number of programmes, starting at year 0, and a table of rate pairs, in place of two cost instalments and one QALY gain."; HEO defines Differential Discounting as "Differential discounting applies a lower annual discount rate to future health effects, such as QALYs, than to future costs in an economic evaluation.".

column2: Dirichlet row from transition counts and a prior with beta-marginal intervals, correlations and a sampled row
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Dirichlet Distribution. The module describes Dirichlet row from transition counts and a prior with beta-marginal intervals, correlations and a sampled row as "Fits a Dirichlet row from a vector of transition counts and a prior, returns every component's mean, standard deviation and central interval from its beta marginal with the full correlation matrix, and, given uniform numbers, returns one sampled row from normalised gamma quantiles. Beta quantiles and gamma quantiles have no closed form, so this procedure cannot run in the site calculator; Excel BETA.INV and GAMMA.INV, R qbeta and qgamma and Python scipy.stats return them. The inputs differ from the formulas': a count vector of any length, a prior, a coverage level and optional uniform numbers."; HEO defines Dirichlet Distribution as "The Dirichlet distribution is a multivariate distribution for proportions that sum to one, used for uncertain transition probabilities from a model state.".

column2: ROC threshold for a minimal important change from patients' change scores and anchor classification
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Minimal Clinically Important Difference. The module describes ROC threshold for a minimal important change from patients' change scores and anchor classification as "Computes sensitivity, specificity, the misclassification sum and the Youden index at every candidate cut-off from patients' change scores and their anchor classification, and returns the ROC threshold, the candidate with the smallest misclassification sum (the lowest such candidate when two tie). The inputs differ from the formula's: a change score and an improved flag for every patient and a list of candidate cut-offs, in place of the counts for one cut-off."; HEO defines Minimal Clinically Important Difference as "The minimal clinically important difference (MCID) is the smallest change in an outcome score that patients perceive as important, beneficial or harmful.".

column2: N-th root of a transition matrix of any size by eigendecomposition with validity and reproduction checks
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Transition Matrix. The module describes N-th root of a transition matrix of any size by eigendecomposition with validity and reproduction checks as "Takes the n-th root of a transition matrix of any size by eigendecomposition, P^(1/n) = V D^(1/n) V^-1, and checks the result: whether it is real, whether every entry is non-negative, whether each row sums to one, and how closely its n-th power reproduces the original matrix. It handles structures with recovery or several intermediate states, for which no closed form like HE-FM-TMAT-001 is at hand. The inputs differ from the formula's: a whole matrix and any whole number n."; HEO defines Transition Matrix as "A transition matrix is the table of probabilities of moving between, or staying in, health states in one cycle of a Markov model, with rows summing to one.".

column2: Yearly incidence-based and prevalence-based YLDs from a history of incident cases
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Years Lived with Disability. The module describes Yearly incidence-based and prevalence-based YLDs from a history of incident cases as "Turns a history of yearly incident cases into the incidence-based and prevalence-based YLD counts for every year that has at least L years of history behind it, for a condition of fixed duration L. The inputs differ from the formulas': a whole series of yearly incidence, in place of one or two incidence levels, so any pattern of rises and falls can be followed, with an optional continuous discount rate for the incidence-based count."; HEO defines Years Lived with Disability as "Years lived with disability (YLDs) measure non-fatal health loss, usually as prevalence times disability weight; adding years of life lost gives the DALY.".

column2: Expanded tunnel transition matrix from death probabilities by cycle since entry, with its cohort trace
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Tunnel State. The module describes Expanded tunnel transition matrix from death probabilities by cycle since entry, with its cohort trace as "Builds the expanded transition matrix for a model with one origin state, one tunnelled clinical state and death, from the death probability in each cycle since entry, and runs the cohort trace with the update HE-FM-MM-001. It returns the matrix, the trace and, for each cycle, the average death probability of the tunnelled state (HE-FM-TUN-003). The inputs differ from the formula's symbols: HE-FM-TUN-001 takes occupancies and continuation probabilities one cycle at a time, whereas the function takes a vector of death probabilities by duration and an entry probability and fills the zero-diagonal tunnel rows itself, as Algorithm 1 of the tutorial by Alarid-Escudero and colleagues does by iterating through the tunnel states."; HEO defines Tunnel State as "A tunnel state is one of a fixed sequence of one-cycle temporary states in a Markov model, letting risks, costs or utilities vary with time in a state.".

column2: Partitioned survival occupancy, crossing check, life years and QALYs from PFS and OS curves on a time grid
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Partitioned Survival Model. The module describes Partitioned survival occupancy, crossing check, life years and QALYs from PFS and OS curves on a time grid as "Takes PFS and OS as a spreadsheet or a fitted model usually holds them, as survival values on a grid of times from model entry, and returns the state shares at each time, a count of grid times at which PFS lies above OS, and discounted life years and QALYs per person. It applies HE-FM-PSM-001 at each grid time, takes the areas between grid times by the trapezoid rule, discounts each interval at its midpoint and values the areas as in HE-FM-PSM-003. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables: the formula works at one time t, while the function works on whole curves, a grid and a discount rate, and it declines to value crossed curves rather than patching them."; HEO defines Partitioned Survival Model as "A partitioned survival model is a cancer economic model that uses PFS and OS curves to split a cohort into progression-free, progressed and dead states.".

column2: Expected discounted rewards of a time-homogeneous absorbing Markov chain by matrix inversion
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Markov Chain. The module describes Expected discounted rewards of a time-homogeneous absorbing Markov chain by matrix inversion as "Returns the expected total reward per person of a time-homogeneous absorbing Markov chain from a starting distribution across the transient states and one reward per cycle for each transient state, using the discounted fundamental matrix of HE-FM-MKCH-001 in place of a cohort run. A reward of 1 in every transient state gives discounted life expectancy and utilities give quality-adjusted life expectancy. It applies Sonnenberg and Beck's half-cycle subtraction on request and checks that Q is substochastic and that the discounted series converges. The inputs differ from the formula's: a starting distribution, a reward vector and a half-cycle option."; HEO defines Markov Chain as "A Markov chain is a random process moving between states in which the next state depends only on the current state. It underlies Markov cohort models.".

column2: Discounted life years and QALYs from a mixture cure model by numerical integration
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cure Rate Model. The module describes Discounted life years and QALYs from a mixture cure model by numerical integration as "Takes the inputs a cure model analysis usually holds, a cure fraction, a background hazard, a Weibull curve for the excess survival of the uncured, utilities by cure status, an annual discount rate and a horizon, and returns discounted QALYs by summing the mixture cure curve HE-FM-CRM-001, weighted by utility and the continuous discount factor, over a fine time grid with the midpoint rule. Othus and colleagues computed the mean survival of uncured patients, the integral of S_B(t) times S_E(t), by numerical integration. The inputs therefore differ from the closed forms HE-FM-CRM-003 and HE-FM-CRM-004: the excess hazard need not be constant, and the function builds the areas E_B and E_U itself. With both utilities set to 1 and d to 0 it returns T_bar."; HEO defines Cure Rate Model as "A cure rate model is a survival model that estimates the cure fraction and survival of uncured patients, used in HTA to extrapolate long-term survival.".

column2: Expected event probability and deterministic bias from the mean and standard deviation of an uncertain hazard
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Value. The module describes Expected event probability and deterministic bias from the mean and standard deviation of an uncertain hazard as "Takes the summary a source usually reports for an uncertain constant hazard, its mean and standard deviation, with a horizon, a cost per event and a cohort size, and returns the expected event probability and the bias of a run at the mean hazard. It fits the gamma shape and scale by the method of moments, applies HE-FM-EV-003 for the expected probability and HE-FM-TP-001 for the deterministic one, and adds the second-order approximation HE-FM-EV-002 as a check. The inputs differ from the formula's variables: the formula needs the gamma shape and scale, and the function derives them from the mean and standard deviation."; HEO defines Expected Value as "Expected value is the probability-weighted mean of an uncertain outcome, such as a cost or QALY total, across all its possible values.".

column2: Total years of life lost for a cause from deaths by age group and a named standard life table
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Years of Life Lost. The module describes Total years of life lost for a cause from deaths by age group and a named standard life table as "Takes the deaths from one cause by age group and the name of a standard life table, looks up the standard remaining life expectancy for each age group in that table, and returns the cause's total YLLs and each age group's share of the total. The inputs differ from the formula's symbols: the deaths arrive as a set of age-group counts and the standard values are looked up rather than entered, so one set of deaths can be run under GBD 2010 and WHO GHE 2021 and the results compared."; HEO defines Years of Life Lost as "Years of life lost (YLL) measure premature mortality as deaths times standard remaining life expectancy at the age of death, the fatal part of the DALY.".

column2: Incremental cost-utility and utility-cost ratios with quadrant from arm-level costs and QALYs
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Incremental Cost-Utility Ratio. The module describes Incremental cost-utility and utility-cost ratios with quadrant from arm-level costs and QALYs as "Takes the expected cost and expected QALYs of each arm, or matched probabilistic draws of them, and returns both forms PHARMAC asks to be reported: the ICUR of HE-FM-CUA-001 and the IUCR of HE-FM-ICUR-001, with the quadrant of the cost-effectiveness plane. Draws are averaged before any ratio is formed. The inputs differ from the formula's variables: the function builds Delta_C and Delta_Q from arm-level values, and it returns a missing value for a ratio whose denominator is zero."; HEO defines Incremental Cost-Utility Ratio as "The incremental cost-utility ratio (ICUR) is the ICER of a cost-utility analysis: extra cost over a comparator divided by extra QALYs gained.".

column2: Standard, Wagstaff and Erreygers concentration indices from group values, shares and scale bounds
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Concentration Index. The module describes Standard, Wagstaff and Erreygers concentration indices from group values, shares and scale bounds as "Takes the mean of a bounded health variable in each socioeconomic group, ordered from poorest to richest, the share of the population in each group and the bounds of the measurement scale, and returns the standard concentration index with its generalised Wagstaff and Erreygers corrections, plus the same three indices for the mirror variable. It builds each group's fractional rank as the cumulative share before the group plus half its own share, then the population-weighted mean and covariance, and then applies HE-FM-HINQ-005, HE-FM-CIX-001 in the generalised form of Erreygers and Van Ourti, and HE-FM-CIX-002. The inputs therefore differ from the formulas' variables, which take C and mu as given. Individual records can be entered one per row with their survey weights as the shares."; HEO defines Concentration Index as "The concentration index measures socioeconomic inequality in a health variable; a negative value means it is disproportionately held by the poor.".

column2: Attributable annual cost of prevalent cases from survey counts and a prevalence ratio
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Prevalence Ratio. The module describes Attributable annual cost of prevalent cases from survey counts and a prevalence ratio as "Takes the four counts of a cross-sectional survey and three facts about a local population, its size, its exposed share and an annual cost per prevalent case, and returns the attributable annual cost of prevalent cases. It chains three steps: the prevalence ratio HE-FM-PR-001 from the survey, the attributable fraction HE-FM-PR-003 with the local exposed share, and the top-down burden HE-FM-COI-002 applied to the local prevalent cases. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables: the survey supplies the ratio and the prevalences, and the local population supplies the cases and costs."; HEO defines Prevalence Ratio as "The prevalence ratio (PR) is the prevalence of a condition in an exposed group divided by that in an unexposed group, used to compare disease burden.".

column2: Probabilistic economically justifiable price at a stated probability of cost-effectiveness
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Economically Justifiable Price. The module describes Probabilistic economically justifiable price at a stated probability of cost-effectiveness as "Takes matched draws from a probabilistic sensitivity analysis, a threshold and a required probability of cost-effectiveness, and returns two prices per unit. EJP_mean is the price at which expected incremental net benefit is zero, the probabilistic EJP of the article. EJP_alpha is the highest price at which at least a share alpha of the draws is cost-effective at lambda, the stricter reading the article describes. Because each draw's net benefit is linear in price, draw i is cost-effective at a price P exactly when P is at or below its own EJP_i, so the probability of cost-effectiveness at P is the share of draw-level EJPs at or above P and the search over prices needs no further model runs. The inputs differ from the formula's variables: the function takes vectors of draws and a probability level and returns an order statistic as well as a closed-form value."; HEO defines Economically Justifiable Price as "The economically justifiable price (EJP) is the top price a manufacturer can defend on cost-effectiveness grounds at a given payer's threshold.".

column2: Incremental QALYs and ICER after LOCF from arm utility means and dropout fractions
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Last Observation Carried Forward. The module describes Incremental QALYs and ICER after LOCF from arm utility means and dropout fractions as "Takes the inputs a trial-based cost-effectiveness analysis holds, each arm's mean utility at baseline, 6 months and 12 months with complete follow-up, each arm's fraction of dropouts after the 6-month visit and the incremental cost, and returns the incremental QALYs and ICER with complete data and after LOCF. It applies HE-FM-LOCF-001 to each arm's 12-month mean, then the trapezoidal QALY formula HE-FM-QALY-002 with visits at 0, 0.5 and 1 year, where QALYs are 0.25 times the sum of the baseline mean, twice the 6-month mean and the 12-month mean, and then the ICER of HE-FM-ICER-001. Comparing the two ICERs shows how far the imputation alone moves the result."; HEO defines Last Observation Carried Forward as "Last observation carried forward (LOCF) fills missing trial follow-up values with each participant's last observed value, assuming no change after dropout.".

column2: Computational function for discounted QALYs and cost per QALY of a one-off treatment under a chosen timing convention
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Discounting. The module describes Computational function for discounted QALYs and cost per QALY of a one-off treatment under a chosen timing convention as "Takes the inputs a one-off treatment analysis usually holds, an incremental cost paid at the start, a yearly QALY gain, the number of years it lasts, an annual rate and a flag for counting each year at its start or its end, and returns the sum of the discount factors, the discounted QALYs, the discounted and undiscounted cost per QALY and the rise caused by discounting. It builds one factor for each year, so it also works at a zero rate where the closed form fails, and chains HE-FM-DISC-001 or HE-FM-DISC-002 with HE-FM-DISC-004. The inputs therefore differ from the formulas' variables, which assume one timing convention and a positive rate."; HEO defines Discounting as "Discounting converts future costs and health effects, such as QALYs, into present values so that options with different timings can be compared.".

column2: Computational function for annualised capital cost per unit of service from several capital inputs
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Annualisation. The module describes Computational function for annualised capital cost per unit of service from several capital inputs as "Takes the inputs a costing study usually holds, the price, resale value and useful life of each capital input, one discount rate and the annual volume of service, and returns the annualised capital cost per unit of service alongside the straight-line figure. It applies HE-FM-ANLS-001 to each input over its own life, sums the annual charges and divides by the volume. The Math / Code line shows two inputs, and the R and Python versions take any number."; HEO defines Annualisation as "Annualisation is the conversion of a capital outlay into an equal yearly cost over the asset's useful life, using an annuity factor and the discount rate.".

column2: Computational function for the yearly return on capital and price recovered in an annualised charge
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Annualisation. The module describes Computational function for the yearly return on capital and price recovered in an annualised charge as "Takes the price, rate and useful life of an input with no resale value and a year number t, and returns the balance of the price still tied up at the start of that year, the return on it at rate r and the part of the price recovered by that year's charge. It applies HE-FM-ANLS-002 to find E and then splits E as a loan repayment, which shows where the gap between the annualised and straight-line charges comes from."; HEO defines Annualisation as "Annualisation is the conversion of a capital outlay into an equal yearly cost over the asset's useful life, using an annuity factor and the discount rate.".

column2: Computational function for a baseline-risk adjusted odds ratio, events avoided and ICER from a centred meta-regression
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Meta-Regression. The module describes Computational function for a baseline-risk adjusted odds ratio, events avoided and ICER from a centred meta-regression as "Takes the inputs a decision modeller holds, a baseline risk for the model population, the fitted coefficients of a centred meta-regression on baseline log-odds and the cost and QALY consequences of an event, and returns the adjusted odds ratio, the absolute effect and the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio. It converts the risk to log-odds, applies HE-FM-MREG-005, exponentiates the result and applies the odds ratio to the baseline odds, so each step uses the result of the one before. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables, which need the covariate already on the log-odds scale."; HEO defines Meta-Regression as "Meta-regression is a precision-weighted regression of study effect estimates on study characteristics, explaining heterogeneity in meta-analyses for HTA.".

column2: Computational function for a yearly stream weighted by the simple hyperbola against constant-rate discounting
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Hyperbolic Discounting. The module describes Computational function for a yearly stream weighted by the simple hyperbola against constant-rate discounting as "Takes a level yearly amount, the number of periods and one parameter used both as the hyperbolic alpha and as the constant rate, and returns the sum of the simple hyperbolic weights, the sum of the constant-rate factors, the two weighted totals and their ratio. It builds one weight for each period, because the hyperbolic sum has no simple closed form, and so shows how much more weight the hyperbola gives to later periods than HE-FM-DISC-001 does at the same first-period rate. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables, which describe one delay."; HEO defines Hyperbolic Discounting as "Hyperbolic discounting is time preference in which the discount rate falls as delay grows, so plans made for later are often reversed when the time comes.".

column2: Computational function for a smaller-sooner against larger-later plan check with commitment thresholds under a chosen discount form
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Hyperbolic Discounting. The module describes Computational function for a smaller-sooner against larger-later plan check with commitment thresholds under a chosen discount form as "Takes the two amounts, a choice of discount form and its parameters, builds the weights at delays 0, 1 and 2, and returns the two margins of HE-FM-HYPD-005, whether the plan reverses, the penalty on the sooner outcome felt now that would tip today's choice, the reward paid with the later outcome that would do the same, and the first whole delay at which waiting is preferred. The penalty is minus M_0 and the reward minus M_0 divided by w_1, so their ratio is the timing premium 1/w_1 in step 4 of the article's example. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables, which take the weights as given."; HEO defines Hyperbolic Discounting as "Hyperbolic discounting is time preference in which the discount rate falls as delay grows, so plans made for later are often reversed when the time comes.".

column2: Computational function for per-person and population EVSI of a two-arm trial under normal incremental net benefit
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Value of Sample Information. The module describes Computational function for per-person and population EVSI of a two-arm trial under normal incremental net benefit as "Takes the inputs a trial planner usually holds, the prior mean and standard deviation of incremental net benefit from the probabilistic analysis, the per-patient standard deviation of net benefit in each arm, the number of patients per arm and the size and lifetime of the beneficiary population, and returns per-person EVSI, per-person EVPI under normality, the share of EVPI the trial captures and population EVSI. It chains HE-FM-EVSI-002 (preposterior variance), HE-FM-EVSI-003 (closed-form EVSI, applied also at the prior variance for EVPI) and HE-FM-EVSI-004 (population EVSI), so its inputs differ from the symbols of any one formula. The calculator version takes the two upper-tail probabilities Q_s and Q_0 as inputs because it has no normal distribution function, and the Excel, R and Python versions compute them. The same EVSI can be checked by the single-loop Monte Carlo scheme of the second ISPOR report, drawing a true incremental net benefit from the prior and a trial estimate around it, and averaging the amount by which the posterior mean falls on the other side of zero from the prior mean, the value of switching in those results."; HEO defines Expected Value of Sample Information as "Expected value of sample information (EVSI) is the expected net benefit gained by deciding after a specific proposed study reports instead of deciding now.".

column2: Computational function for weighted and unweighted population net health benefit across several groups
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Equity-Weighted Analysis. The module describes Computational function for weighted and unweighted population net health benefit across several groups as "Takes the number of patients, the equity weight, the incremental QALYs and the incremental cost per patient in each group, and one value of a QALY, and returns the programme's population QALY gain unweighted and weighted, its total incremental cost, the health displaced, the unweighted and weighted net health benefit and the unweighted and weighted ICER. It applies HE-FM-EQWA-001 to the group totals and HE-FM-EQWA-003 to the whole programme, and it is run once at GBP 25,000 and once at GBP 35,000 per QALY to give the four net health benefits PMG36 asks for. The Math / Code line shows two groups, and the R and Python versions take any number."; HEO defines Equity-Weighted Analysis as "Equity-weighted analysis is a cost-effectiveness analysis in which health gains for priority groups, such as the severely ill, are weighted more heavily.".

column2: Computational function for DALYs averted and cost per DALY averted from deaths, disability and duration in two scenarios
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Disability-Adjusted Life Year. The module describes Computational function for DALYs averted and cost per DALY averted from deaths, disability and duration in two scenarios as "Takes the size of a cohort, its deaths and the survivors' disability weight with and without a programme, the duration of the condition, the standard remaining life expectancy at the age of death, an optional continuous discount rate and the extra cost, and returns each scenario's DALYs, the DALYs averted, the share of them that comes from deaths prevented and the cost per DALY averted. It sets the survivors in each scenario to the cohort less its deaths, so the people saved by the programme are counted as living with the condition, and it chains HE-FM-DALY-002 or HE-FM-DALY-004 with HE-FM-DALY-003. The inputs therefore differ from the formulas' variables, which take survivors and DALY totals as given."; HEO defines Disability-Adjusted Life Year as "The disability-adjusted life year (DALY) measures health loss by adding years of life lost to premature death and years lived with disability.".

column2: Computational function for scoring an EQ-5D-3L profile under any constant and N3 coefficient set
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept EQ-5D-3L Value Set. The module describes Computational function for scoring an EQ-5D-3L profile under any constant and N3 coefficient set as "Takes an EQ-5D-3L profile, as a five-digit string such as 11223 or as five level inputs, and a coefficient set of the main-effects form, and returns the utility with the two indicators D and N3. It applies HE-FM-EQ3L-001 with level 2 and level 3 dummies built from the levels, so any value set tabulated with a constant, ten level dummies and N3 can be scored, and with the UK coefficients it reproduces HE-FM-EQ3L-002. The R and Python versions also score all 243 states."; HEO defines EQ-5D-3L Value Set as "EQ-5D-3L value sets are utility weights, elicited from a population's health state valuations, that score all 243 EQ-5D-3L states for QALY calculation.".

column2: Computational function for EVPI, error probability and population EVPI from a three-option table of draws
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Value of Perfect Information. The module describes Computational function for EVPI, error probability and population EVPI from a three-option table of draws as "Takes a table of net benefit for three options over five probabilistic draws, the size of each year's patient cohort, the number of years the decision stays relevant, the discount rate and the threshold, and returns per-person EVPI, the error probability and population EVPI in health and money units. It applies HE-FM-EVPI-001 across the draws and then scales the result by the discounted population as in HE-FM-VOI-002, with the first cohort undiscounted. The Math / Code line takes option A as the zero reference, and the R and Python versions take any number of draws and options."; HEO defines Expected Value of Perfect Information as "Expected value of perfect information (EVPI) is the expected gain from removing all uncertainty in a funding decision, the upper limit on research value.".

column2: Computational function for regression-based EVPPI and its EVPI bound from a probabilistic sample table
column10: Expected Value of Partial Perfect Information
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Value of Partial Perfect Information. The module describes Computational function for regression-based EVPPI and its EVPI bound from a probabilistic sample table as "Takes a probabilistic sample as an analyst holds it, a table of N runs with the sampled values of the parameters of interest and the net benefit of each of D options, fits a least squares regression of each option's net benefit less the baseline's on the chosen parameters, and returns the EVPPI from the fitted values, the EVPI from the raw net benefits and a flag that the estimate lies within its bounds. It chains HE-FM-EVPP-003 with HE-FM-VOI-001 for any number of options, so the inputs differ from the formula's variables, which start from fitted values for three options. A linear model in indicator, polynomial or product terms stands in here for the generalised additive model of Strong, Oakley and Brennan. The Math / Code line takes two options and four runs, with the fitted values from the regression entered as inputs, and the R and Python versions fit the regression for any number of runs and options."; HEO defines Expected Value of Partial Perfect Information as "Expected value of partial perfect information (EVPPI) is the expected gain in net benefit from knowing selected model parameters exactly before deciding.".

column2: Computational function for the efficient sample size over a grid of study designs by ENBS
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Expected Net Benefit of Sampling. The module describes Computational function for the efficient sample size over a grid of study designs by ENBS as "Takes the inputs for a grid of candidate designs, the sample size and per-person EVSI of each, the people facing the decision each year, the number of years, a discount rate, the study cost inputs and, for only in research, the number of people treated outside each design while it runs. For one design it returns the discount factor, the population EVSI, the expected study cost and the ENBS, and the code below repeats this over the grid to return the largest ENBS and the efficient sample size, or no design when none has a positive ENBS. It chains HE-FM-EVSI-004, HE-FM-ENBS-002 and HE-FM-ENBS-003, so its inputs differ from the formulas' variables. Per-person EVSI for each sample size comes from the methods on the EVSI page."; HEO defines Expected Net Benefit of Sampling as "Expected net benefit of sampling (ENBS) is a proposed study's population expected value of sample information minus its expected total cost.".

column2: Computational function for incremental net benefit on the money and health scales from per-arm trial summaries
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Net Benefit Approach. The module describes Computational function for incremental net benefit on the money and health scales from per-arm trial summaries as "Takes the per-arm summaries a trial report gives, the mean effect and cost in each arm, their standard deviations, the within-arm correlation and the arm size, together with a threshold, and returns incremental net benefit on the money and health scales with its standard error, interval and z statistic, plus the ICER. It first builds the variances and covariance of the two mean differences from the arm summaries, the inputs that HE-FM-AN-004 and HE-CF-AN-001 start from, then forms incremental net monetary benefit and divides by lambda to return the net health benefit of HE-FM-NBA-001, Stinnett and Mullahy's equation 7. The ICER is returned for reading with the quadrant rule of HE-FM-NBA-002, and the Excel, R and Python versions add the probability that net benefit is positive."; HEO defines Net Benefit Approach as "The net benefit approach is a cost-effectiveness decision framework that ranks options by net benefit at a stated threshold instead of by ratios.".

column2: Computational function for the cost-effectiveness frontier by removing dominated and extendedly dominated strategies
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness Frontier. The module describes Computational function for the cost-effectiveness frontier by removing dominated and extendedly dominated strategies as "Takes the names, expected costs and expected QALYs of any number of mutually exclusive strategies and returns the strategies on the cost-effectiveness frontier in cost order with their sequential ICERs, by the conventional elimination that Suen and Goldhaber-Fiebert summarise. It sorts by cost, removes dominated strategies, ties included, with the rule of HE-FM-DOM-002, computes the ratio of each strategy against the one before it, removes the first strategy whose ratio is higher than the next one, as in HE-FM-EXD-001, and recomputes until the ratios rise. The finished ratios are the slopes that HE-FM-CEF-001 reads. The inputs are lists of strategies, not the three named strategies of the formula. The Math / Code line shows one pass for four strategies already in cost order with no strict dominance, and the R and Python versions take any number and repeat the passes."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Frontier as "The cost-effectiveness frontier joins the strategies not ruled out by strict or extended dominance on a plot of expected cost against health effect.".

column2: Computational function for the one-pass net monetary benefit search for the cost-effectiveness frontier
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness Frontier. The module describes Computational function for the one-pass net monetary benefit search for the cost-effectiveness frontier as "Takes the names, expected costs and expected QALYs of any number of strategies and a largest value per QALY of interest, and returns the frontier strategies by the one-pass method of Suen and Goldhaber-Fiebert. It calculates net monetary benefit (HE-FM-NMB-001) for every strategy at every value in a grid made of zero, every positive pairwise ICER up to the largest value and that value itself, and keeps the strategies that come out on top somewhere in the grid, with no rounds of elimination. At one value it also returns the net monetary benefit each strategy gives up, L_k of HE-FM-CEF-002. The Math / Code line shows four strategies at one value, and the R and Python versions take any number of strategies and the whole grid."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Frontier as "The cost-effectiveness frontier joins the strategies not ruled out by strict or extended dominance on a plot of expected cost against health effect.".

column2: Computational function for health forgone by each option against the health-maximising option
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Equity-Efficiency Trade-off. The module describes Computational function for health forgone by each option against the health-maximising option as "Takes the population share of each group and the net health gain per person of each group under each of several options of equal cost, and returns each option's mean net gain, the highest mean gain and the health each option forgoes against it. This is the equity constraint analysis of HE-FM-EET-001 run over a set of options, so the health-maximising option is found by the procedure rather than named beforehand. The Math / Code line shows two groups and three options, and the R and Python versions take any number of groups and options."; HEO defines Equity-Efficiency Trade-off as "The equity-efficiency trade-off is the total health given up for a fairer distribution when the option that maximises health is not the fairest one.".

column2: Per-cycle exit probabilities by time since entry from a survival curve checked against one constant exit probability
