column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Markov Assumption. The module describes Per-cycle exit probabilities by time since entry from a survival curve checked against one constant exit probability as "Takes survival at the end of each of the first K cycles since entry to a state, from follow-up of people who entered it or from a model with tunnel states, and returns the exit probability in each cycle among those still in the state, the constant exit probability that a memoryless state fitted to survival at K cycles would use, the largest gap between the two and the mean stay of the fitted memoryless state. Each per-cycle value is h_d of HE-FM-MKA-002 taken from the data, the ratio of adjacent survival values as in HE-FM-CUMH-002, and the constant comes from the rescaling formula HE-FM-TP-003 with the K-cycle survival as the observed value. A memoryless state needs every per-cycle value equal to the constant; a large gap shows that time since entry carries information that one state discards, and the per-cycle values then become the duration-specific inputs of HE-CF-TUN-001. The check is descriptive. With patient-level data Williams and colleagues used a state-arrival extended Cox model with time in the previous state as a covariate to decide whether to accept the assumption. The inputs differ from the formula's symbols, which describe a stay already known to be geometric."; HEO defines Markov Assumption as "The Markov assumption is that the next transition in a state-transition model depends only on the current state and model time, not on earlier history.".

column2: Computational function for the critical inequality aversion at which two options give equal EDE health
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Distributional Cost-Effectiveness. The module describes Computational function for the critical inequality aversion at which two options give equal EDE health as "Takes the population share and the health per person of each social group under two options, such as a programme and its comparator from HE-FM-DCEA-001, and a bracket of inequality aversion values, and returns by bisection the Atkinson epsilon at which the two options give equal EDE health, the point where the change in EDE health of HE-FM-DCEA-002 changes sign. At each step it evaluates the share-weighted EDE of HE-CF-ATK-001 for both options at the midpoint of the bracket, keeps the half in which the difference changes sign and stops when the bracket is narrower than the tolerance, for any number of groups. The two-group closed approximation in the equity-efficiency trade-off package gives about 11.77 for the article's example, while solving the EDE comparison gives about 11.76, the value the article reports. The Math / Code line evaluates the difference for two groups at a given epsilon, the quantity bisection drives to zero, and the Excel, R and Python versions run the search."; HEO defines Distributional Cost-Effectiveness as "Distributional cost-effectiveness analysis (DCEA) is an economic evaluation showing who gains and loses health from a policy and its effect on inequality.".

column2: Computational function for a level yearly stream under the stepped Green Book schedule and the reduced schedule without pure time preference
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Time Preference. The module describes Computational function for a level yearly stream under the stepped Green Book schedule and the reduced schedule without pure time preference as "Takes a level yearly amount, a horizon of up to 125 years and two sets of three band rates, the standard schedule and the reduced schedule with pure time preference excluded, and returns the sum of the stepped factors of HE-FM-TPR-003 under each, the two present values and their difference. Paragraph 3.5 of the supplementary guidance reads the difference between the two results as an estimate of the wealth transfer attributable to pure social time preference. Each band's sum is geometric, so the calculator line adds three closed-form sums, and for a horizon of 30 years or less the standard sum is the annuity of HE-FM-DISC-001. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables, which describe one year."; HEO defines Time Preference as "Time preference is the preference for benefits sooner and costs later; in health economics it is one reason future costs and QALYs are discounted.".

column2: Computational function for ranking allocations by utilitarian, isoelastic and maximin health social welfare
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Social Welfare Function. The module describes Computational function for ranking allocations by utilitarian, isoelastic and maximin health social welfare as "Takes the health of each equal-sized group under each option and an inequality aversion parameter, and returns for every option the utilitarian total, the isoelastic welfare of HE-FM-SWF-001 (HE-FM-SWF-002 at epsilon of 1) and the maximin welfare of HE-FM-SWF-003, with the option ranked first under each. It repeats the article's three-step ranking for any number of options and groups, and it ranks the isoelastic values on a log scale so that very high epsilon values do not underflow. The Math / Code line shows three options and three groups at one epsilon other than 1, and the R and Python versions take any number. The values of epsilon at which two options swap rank belong to the Distributional Cost-Effectiveness package and are not computed here."; HEO defines Social Welfare Function as "A social welfare function (SWF) combines individual health or wellbeing into overall social welfare, setting how equality is weighed against the total.".

column2: Computational function for the ages at which the GBD age weight crosses a chosen level
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Age Weighting. The module describes Computational function for the ages at which the GBD age weight crosses a chosen level as "Takes the constants C and beta and a level, by default 1, and returns the two ages at which the weight equals that level, one on each side of the peak 1/beta, so the span of ages weighted above uniform can be read off. The crossing ages have no closed form in elementary functions, so the code finds them numerically by root search on each side of the peak. The calculator line checks a pair of ages by returning their weights. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables, which take one age."; HEO defines Age Weighting as "Age weighting values a year of healthy life by the age at which it is lived, as in the original GBD DALY, which gave years in young adulthood most weight.".

column2: Computational function for age-weighted discounted years lost per death or case with a numerical integral check
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Age Weighting. The module describes Computational function for age-weighted discounted years lost per death or case with a numerical integral check as "Takes the age at death or onset, the years lost or duration, the discount rate, the modulation constant, the age-weight constants and a disability weight, and returns the closed-form age-weighted discounted years (HE-FM-AGW-003, or HE-FM-AGW-002 when the rate is zero), the same quantity from a numerical integral of the weighted, discounted integrand over the span, their difference, the result times the disability weight for a case (HE-FM-AGW-004), and the ratio to the unweighted discounted years of HE-FM-YLL-003. The integral is a Simpson's rule sum over 1,000 panels in Excel and Python and adaptive quadrature in R, so a typing error in the closed form shows as a difference. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables."; HEO defines Age Weighting as "Age weighting values a year of healthy life by the age at which it is lived, as in the original GBD DALY, which gave years in young adulthood most weight.".

column2: Computational function for the stop or continue decision at one interim look of a two-arm trial
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Adaptive Value of Information. The module describes Computational function for the stop or continue decision at one interim look of a two-arm trial as "Takes the design-stage prior for incremental net monetary benefit, the pairs observed and their mean at the interim look, the remaining pairs, the sampling standard deviation per pair, the patients informed and the costs, and returns the interim posterior, the per-patient and population EVSI of the remaining pairs, the offline gain of HE-FM-AVOI-001 with no switching cost, the net gain with the participants' loss and the decision. It chains the normal update of HE-FM-BAD-001 in effective sample size form, the preposterior variance of HE-FM-EVSI-002 with n_t in place of n0, the closed-form EVSI of HE-FM-EVSI-003 at the interim mean, HE-FM-AVOI-001, and HE-FM-ENBS-001 with the cost of HE-FM-ENBS-002 for the remaining pairs (n equal to 2m, a variable cost of c/2 per participant, a share of one half on the arm expected to be inferior and the analysis cost C_a in place of the fixed cost), so its inputs differ from the symbols of any one formula. The calculator takes Q_z from 1-NORM.S.DIST(z,TRUE) because it has no normal distribution function. The Excel, R and Python versions compute it and also scan every remaining size up to the maximum, continuing if any one-stage plan has a positive net gain, the KG* rule of Chick and colleagues."; HEO defines Adaptive Value of Information as "Adaptive value of information applies VOI analysis to staged research, re-valuing further data at each interim look to decide whether to continue.".

column2: Seeded one-step agent simulation checked against the analytic infection probability
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Agent-Based Model. The module describes Seeded one-step agent simulation checked against the analytic infection probability as "Runs a small seeded agent simulation of one step and checks it against the analytic infection probability HE-FM-ABM-001. It takes a number of susceptible agents, a per-contact transmission probability, the number of infectious contacts per agent under a comparator and under a programme, and a base seed, and returns the simulated and analytic shares infected under each, the Monte Carlo standard error of the simulated share, a pass flag and the simulated infections averted per agent. Each agent i draws one uniform number per contact from its own stream, seeded with seed + i, and is infected when any draw is below p, so the simulation works contact by contact and never uses the formula itself. The programme removes each agent's last contact and keeps the draws for the others, so the two strategies share common random numbers."; HEO defines Agent-Based Model as "An agent-based model (ABM) simulates individuals as agents that follow rules and interact, so outcomes such as infections, costs and QALYs emerge.".

column2: Computational function for cycle-by-cycle background death probabilities from an age-banded life table
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Background Mortality. The module describes Computational function for cycle-by-cycle background death probabilities from an age-banded life table as "Takes a starting age, a cycle length, a number of cycles and a life table that gives an annual probability of death for each age band, and returns the background death probability p_bg for every cycle and the share of the cohort still alive when background causes alone act. For each cycle it finds the band that contains the attained age at the start of the cycle, starting age plus elapsed time, and rescales that band's annual probability to the cycle length with HE-FM-TP-003, so the probabilities rise as the cohort moves into older bands. The vector then feeds HE-FM-BGM-002 cycle by cycle. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables, which describe a single cycle."; HEO defines Background Mortality as "Background mortality is the death rate a model's patients would face without the disease, usually taken from general population life tables by age and sex.".

column2: Computational function for R_0 as the spectral radius of a next-generation matrix of any size
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Basic Reproduction Number. The module describes Computational function for R_0 as the spectral radius of a next-generation matrix of any size as "Takes a next-generation matrix K with n groups, or the matrices F and V of a compartmental model from which K is F times the inverse of V, and returns R_0 as the spectral radius of K together with the dominant eigenvector scaled to sum to 1, the share of cases in each group once the generations settle. R and Python call an eigenvalue routine. Excel has no eigenvalue function, so it uses power iteration with helper columns, applying K to a vector of cases generation by generation, the growth factor per generation that Diekmann, Heesterbeek and Roberts take as the characterisation of R_0. The calculator line shows the two-group case over three generations started from one case in each group, beside the closed form of HE-FM-BRN-005, and the inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables, which cover two groups only."; HEO defines Basic Reproduction Number as "The basic reproduction number (R0) is the average number of infections one typical case causes in a fully susceptible population, used in vaccine models.".

column2: Computational function for a foreign cost moved to a target price year and currency in either order
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Basket of Countries. The module describes Computational function for a foreign cost moved to a target price year and currency in either order as "Takes a cost in the source currency and its price year, price indices of the source and target countries, and the exchange rates of the costing year and the base year, and returns the cost in the target currency at base-year prices by the two orders that Turner and colleagues compare. Method 1 converts at the costing-year rate and then inflates with the target country's index. Method 2 inflates with the source country's index and then converts at the base-year rate, the order of the two stages of the CCEMG-EPPI-Centre Cost Converter. Each inflation step is the live price-year adjustment HE-FM-COST-002 and each conversion is HE-FM-BOC-001, or HE-FM-BOC-002 at purchasing power parity. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables, which describe one conversion."; HEO defines Basket of Countries as "The basket of countries is the set of foreign markets whose drug prices a regulator compares in external reference pricing to set a domestic price.".

column2: Computational function for a basket reference price and ceiling with countries that have no price
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Basket of Countries. The module describes Computational function for a basket reference price and ceiling with countries that have no price as "Takes the prices and exchange rates of any number of basket countries, a flag for whether each country has an observed price, a ceiling multiplier and a proposed domestic price, and returns the number of priced countries, their mean, median, lowest and highest converted price, the ceiling of HE-FM-BOC-004 and the margin of the proposed price over it. Countries without a price drop out of every aggregate, which is how the article's launch-sequencing case raises the ceiling. The calculator line covers five countries and the mean; the R and Python code take any number of countries and also return the median. The inputs therefore differ from the formula's variables, which assume five priced countries."; HEO defines Basket of Countries as "The basket of countries is the set of foreign markets whose drug prices a regulator compares in external reference pricing to set a domestic price.".

column2: Two risk strata run as separate cohorts against one averaged cohort, with life expectancy, QALY gains and ICERs
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cohort Model. The module describes Two risk strata run as separate cohorts against one averaged cohort, with life expectancy, QALY gains and ICERs as "Takes the share of a population in a low-risk stratum, the annual death probabilities of a low-risk and a high-risk stratum, a proportional cut in those probabilities from treatment, a utility per year alive and a one-off treatment cost, and returns the life expectancies of six cohort runs (each stratum and one averaged cohort, with and without treatment), the population QALY gain and ICER from the stratified runs, the same results from the averaged cohort, and the relative errors of the averaged cohort. It carries out the article's worked example. Each stratum gain is the difference of two values of the live L(q), HE-FM-ABS-001 less half a cycle, and equals e divided by (1 minus e) q because the half cycle cancels (derived here); the stratified QALY gain weights those gains with the shares of HE-FM-ATE-001, the ICERs follow HE-FM-ICER-001, and the life-expectancy shortfall is gap_L of HE-FM-COHM-001. The calculator line uses the closed form 1/q minus one half; the Excel, R and Python code instead run the Alive and Dead cohort trace numerically for a fixed number of cycles, so they also check the closed form, and the code takes any number of strata. The inputs differ from the formula's symbols, which describe one comparison at a time."; HEO defines Cohort Model as "A cohort model is a health economic decision model that estimates mean costs and outcomes for a patient group as a whole, without simulating individuals.".

column2: Computational function for an Euler run of a closed SIR model with and without vaccination counting infections averted statically and dynamically
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Compartmental Model. The module describes Computational function for an Euler run of a closed SIR model with and without vaccination counting infections averted statically and dynamically as "Runs a closed SIR model forward in Euler steps of HE-FM-CMPM-004 three times, without a programme, with a programme under a dynamic force of infection and with the same programme under the static force of infection taken from the no-programme run, and sums infections averted by each count over the horizon, as HE-FM-CMPM-005 does for one step. It also returns averted infection costs, optionally discounted with a continuous rate as in HE-FM-CONT-003. The calculator line writes out the article's two one-day steps term by term, and Excel, R and Python run any number of steps."; HEO defines Compartmental Model as "A compartmental model splits a population into compartments, such as susceptible, infectious and recovered, and uses equations for the flows between them.".

column2: Computational function for a Lowe CPI from weight-reference expenditure with price-updated weights for a three-item basket
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Consumer Price Index. The module describes Computational function for a Lowe CPI from weight-reference expenditure with price-updated weights for a three-item basket as "Takes the household expenditure on each item in the weight reference period b, the form in which the national accounts supply weights, with item prices in period b, in the base period 0 and at time t. It price-updates each expenditure to the base period, turns the updated amounts into weights and averages the price relatives with them, the steps of sections 3.3 and 3.5 of the ONS technical manual. The result equals the basket form of HE-FM-CPI-001 with quantities V_b / p_b, so the inputs differ from the formula's variables, which are quantities."; HEO defines Consumer Price Index as "The consumer price index (CPI) measures change in the prices households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, used to adjust costs for inflation.".

column2: Computational function for monthly D7BT values to financial-year CPI averages, their ratio and the average annual rate
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Consumer Price Index. The module describes Computational function for monthly D7BT values to financial-year CPI averages, their ratio and the average annual rate as "Takes twelve monthly index values for each of two financial years, April to March, and returns the two financial-year averages as arithmetic means of the twelve months, their ratio, which is the I_b / I_a input of HE-FM-COST-002, and the average annual rate of HE-FM-CPI-004 between them. Section 11.3 of the ONS technical manual defines the annual average as the arithmetic mean of the 12 monthly values and quarters in the same way; applying it to April to March is the article's step for costs priced in a financial year. The inputs are monthly values, so they differ from the formula's variables, which are two index values."; HEO defines Consumer Price Index as "The consumer price index (CPI) measures change in the prices households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, used to adjust costs for inflation.".

column2: Computational function for filling a fixed budget down a cost-effectiveness league table
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Cost-Effectiveness League Table. The module describes Computational function for filling a fixed budget down a cost-effectiveness league table as "Takes the names, incremental costs and incremental health gains of any number of independent programmes and a budget, sorts the programmes in ascending order of ICER and applies the funded share of HE-FM-CELT-001 row by row, or the whole-programme test of HE-FM-CELT-003 when programmes cannot be split. It returns each programme's ICER and share, the health bought, the spending, the budget left and the critical ratio of HE-FM-CELT-002. The inputs are lists of programmes, not the single row of the formula. The Math / Code line shows four divisible programmes already in ICER order, and the R and Python versions take any number of programmes and do the sorting."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness League Table as "A cost-effectiveness league table ranks health care interventions by cost per QALY or a similar ratio so decision makers can compare value for money.".

column2: Computational function for comparing the UK MVH and Zimbabwe EQ-5D-3L value sets state by state
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Country-Specific Value Set. The module describes Computational function for comparing the UK MVH and Zimbabwe EQ-5D-3L value sets state by state as "Scores one EQ-5D-3L profile under two national value sets of the constant and N3 form, the UK MVH tariff of HE-FM-EQ3L-002 and the Zimbabwe set of Jelsma and colleagues, and returns both utilities and their difference. The R and Python versions score all 243 states under both sets and count the ordered pairs of states for which the two sets disagree on the direction of the change, the cross-set reversal that HE-FM-CSVS-001 splits by term for one pair. Any other pair of constant and N3 sets can be compared by replacing the two coefficient dictionaries."; HEO defines Country-Specific Value Set as "A country-specific value set is a set of utility weights, elicited from one country's general public, that turns EQ-5D or similar responses into utilities.".

column2: Computational function for a PSA run with correlated log baseline rate and log hazard ratio through a constant-rate survival model
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis. The module describes Computational function for a PSA run with correlated log baseline rate and log hazard ratio through a constant-rate survival model as "Runs a complete probabilistic sensitivity analysis on a small fixed set of draws. For each draw it takes a pair of independent standard normal values, turns them into a correlated log baseline mortality rate and log hazard ratio with the Cholesky step HE-FM-PSA-001, runs a constant-rate survival model for both options with those same parameters, and stores the new option's incremental net health benefit. It then returns the expected incremental net health benefit (HE-FM-ENB-002), the probability that the new option is cost-effective (HE-FM-CEAC-001, with ties counted as not cost-effective), the two expected losses of HE-FM-PSA-002, the Monte Carlo standard error of the mean (the form of HE-FM-ANTV-002 with one observation per draw) and the number of draws for a target standard error (HE-FM-ABM-003). As in the article, mean survival under a constant mortality rate m is 1 / m years and each life-year is worth q QALYs without discounting, so a draw with log rate b0 and log hazard ratio b1 gives an incremental QALY gain of q times exp(minus b0 minus b1) less exp(minus b0). The Math / Code line writes out five draws; the R and Python versions draw any number."; HEO defines Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis as "Probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA) runs a decision model many times on jointly drawn inputs to estimate expected outcomes and decision uncertainty.".

column2: Computational function for annual patient time cost from service counts with the Yabroff time estimates
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Patient Time Cost. The module describes Computational function for annual patient time cost from service counts with the Yabroff time estimates as "Takes a patient's yearly counts of uses of each service category, the minutes each use takes, a flag for whether round-trip travel is added and an hourly value of time, and returns the annual patient hours and the annual patient time cost, the article's sum over K service types. It follows the service-based method of Yabroff and colleagues, in which the time estimate for a category already contains the waiting time where waiting applies, round-trip travel is added to the services, and each night in hospital counts as 16 waking hours. The inputs therefore differ from the single-type variables of HE-FM-PTC-001."; HEO defines Patient Time Cost as "Patient time cost is the value of the hours patients spend travelling to, waiting for and receiving health care, often valued at a wage rate.".

column2: Computational function for scoring an EQ-5D-5L profile under any 20-decrement value set
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept EQ-5D-5L Value Set. The module describes Computational function for scoring an EQ-5D-5L profile under any 20-decrement value set as "Takes an EQ-5D-5L profile, as a five-digit string such as 23245 or as five level inputs, and a five-level value set given as a constant and a table of 20 decrements, and returns the utility. It applies HE-FM-EQ5L-001 on each dimension and subtracts the five decrements, and the constant where the set has one, from 1, so with the England coefficients it reproduces HE-FM-EQ5L-002. The R and Python versions also score all 3,125 states, which is how the count of states below zero is checked."; HEO defines EQ-5D-5L Value Set as "EQ-5D-5L value set is a scoring algorithm, estimated from a general public valuation study, that gives each of the 3,125 EQ-5D-5L states a QALY utility.".

column2: Computational function for the outlay and least-cost inputs that hold the health stock on a target path
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Health Production Function. The module describes Computational function for the outlay and least-cost inputs that hold the health stock on a target path as "Takes the stock at the start of a period, the depreciation rate, the stock wanted at the start of the next period, the price of care, the wage, the time share and schooling, and returns the gross investment required, its least-cost outlay and the care and own time it buys. The required gross investment is the stock update HE-FM-DFH-001 solved for I and set to zero when the target is below the depreciated stock, since Grossman notes that health capital cannot be sold and gross investment cannot be negative; the outlay uses the unit cost of HE-FM-HPF-003 and the inputs the split of HE-FM-HPF-002. The R and Python code run the same steps over a path of periods from a starting stock, carrying each period's end stock into the next through HE-FM-DFH-001, the target when gross investment is needed and the depreciated stock otherwise, with depreciation that may rise with age, the pattern behind the article's comparison of a younger and an older person."; HEO defines Health Production Function as "A health production function shows how medical care, other market goods and own time produce health, with education raising efficiency (Grossman model).".

column2: Computational function for specific stop-loss expected cost, spread and premium by attachment point from a claims distribution and group size
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Attachment Point. The module describes Computational function for specific stop-loss expected cost, spread and premium by attachment point from a claims distribution and group size as "Takes the figures an employer or analyst usually holds when choosing a specific attachment point, a claims distribution for one member, the number of members, the coinsurance rate, any cap and a premium loading, and returns for each attachment point the expected number of members above it, the expected and standard deviation of total reimbursement, an illustrative premium and the ratio of spread to mean, the table of the article's worked example. It applies HE-FM-ATTP-001 for one member, then HE-FM-ASL-003 for the total over n independent members, and prices the layer at expected reimbursement times one plus the loading theta, the article's illustrative convention; HE-FM-ACTA-002 sets a proportional loading as a share of the gross premium instead. Its inputs differ from the symbols of HE-FM-ATTP-001 because it needs the group size and loading, and the Excel, R and Python versions loop over a grid of attachment points, which the calculator line takes one at a time."; HEO defines Attachment Point as "An attachment point is the claims level at which stop-loss insurance or health reinsurance starts to pay, per person (specific) or per group (aggregate).".

column2: Exact Hedges' correction factor by the log-gamma function with g and its variance
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Hedges' G. The module describes Exact Hedges' correction factor by the log-gamma function with g and its variance as "Computes the exact correction factor of Hedges, the ratio of gamma functions in his equation 6e, through the logarithm of the gamma function so that it does not overflow in large samples, and returns with it Hedges' g, the approximate factor of HE-FM-HEDG-001 and its error, the variance and standard error of g of HE-FM-HEDG-002 with the exact factor, and the exact variance of the corrected estimate from Hedges' Theorem 2 evaluated with g in place of delta. The site calculator has no gamma function, so the Math / Code line runs the approximate chain of HE-FM-HEDG-001 and HE-FM-HEDG-002, and the exact steps are in the Excel, R and Python code. The inputs are d from HE-FM-CD-001 and the two group sizes."; HEO defines Hedges' G as "A standardised effect size measure similar to Cohen's d but corrected for small sample size bias.".

column2: Computational function for delta-adjusted QALY gain, ICER and tipping-point shift over a grid for loss to follow-up
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Loss to Follow-Up. The module describes Computational function for delta-adjusted QALY gain, ICER and tipping-point shift over a grid for loss to follow-up as "Takes each arm's QALYs after imputation under missing at random, with a flag for the participants lost to follow-up, the incremental cost, the threshold, the shift ratio r and a grid of shifts, adds each shift to the imputed QALYs of those lost (r times the shift in usual care), and returns the delta-adjusted QALY gain, ICER and incremental net health benefit at every shift, with the tipping point found where the net health benefit changes sign by the interpolation of HE-FM-OWSA-002. This is the scan that Leurent and colleagues and Faria and colleagues describe, run on one completed dataset; with several imputed datasets the scan is run on each and the gains are averaged by Rubin's rules. The arm means follow HE-FM-LOCF-001 and HE-FM-LOCF-002 as read in HE-FN-LTFU-001, the ratio is HE-FM-ICER-001 and the net health benefit is HE-FM-CET-002. For an additive shift on QALYs alone the net health benefit is linear in the shift, so the grid returns the closed form of HE-FM-LTFU-001, which the Math / Code line computes from arm summaries. The grid is needed when the conclusion is judged on a quantity that is not linear in the shift, such as the probability of cost-effectiveness from bootstrap samples, or when several parameters are varied together."; HEO defines Loss to Follow-Up as "Loss to follow-up occurs when trial participants stop providing data before follow-up ends, so later outcomes, costs and QALYs can be missing.".

column2: Provider cost indices, direct standardisation check and reversed pairs from group tables
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Case-Mix Adjustment. The module describes Provider cost indices, direct standardisation check and reversed pairs from group tables as "Takes the national mean unit cost of each case group and, for each provider, its cases and its unit cost in each group, and returns each provider's actual cost, expected cost, crude cost per case, cost index and directly standardised cost per case on the pooled mix of all providers, with the number of provider pairs whose crude ranking the index reverses and the number the direct standardisation reverses. It carries out steps 1 to 4 of the article's worked example. With the weights of HE-FM-CWT-001 the expected cost and index follow HE-FM-CWT-003 multiplied by 100, the direct standardisation is the weighted sum of HE-FM-INEQ-001 with the pooled case shares as the standard, and each pair is classified with the reversal rule of HE-FM-CMAD-001. The calculator line writes out two providers and two groups; the Excel, R and Python code take any number of each, so the inputs differ from the formula's symbols."; HEO defines Case-Mix Adjustment as "Case-mix adjustment corrects comparisons of providers' costs or outcomes for differences in the patients they treat, so that like is compared with like.".

column2: Computational function for conditional covariances and the joint negative likelihood ratio of two tests from cross-classified counts
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Negative Likelihood Ratio. The module describes Computational function for conditional covariances and the joint negative likelihood ratio of two tests from cross-classified counts as "Takes the counts from a study in which every person had both tests and the reference standard and returns the single-test sensitivities and specificities, the conditional covariances C_pos and C_neg, the joint negative likelihood ratio LR_neg_12 of HE-FM-NLR-002 and the product LR_prod of the single-test ratios for comparison. The inputs are counts, not the formula's accuracy values. With the plug-in covariances the joint ratio equals the observed both-negative proportion among people with the condition divided by that among people without it (derived), so the procedure shows how much of that ratio the independence product misses."; HEO defines Negative Likelihood Ratio as "Negative Likelihood Ratio (LR-): (1 minus sensitivity) over specificity, the factor by which a negative test multiplies disease odds in decision models.".

column2: Copas selection parameters and implied unpublished studies from two assumed publication probabilities
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Copas Model. The module describes Copas selection parameters and implied unpublished studies from two assumed publication probabilities as "Takes the publication probabilities assumed for studies at two standard errors, the way the article sets each scenario, solves the selection equation of HE-FM-COPAS-001 at both for gamma_1 and gamma_0, and returns them with the implied number of unpublished studies of HE-FM-COPAS-002 for the published studies at those standard errors. With quantiles z_a = Phi^-1(P_a) and z_b = Phi^-1(P_b), gamma_1 = (z_a minus z_b) / (1 / s_a minus 1 / s_b) and gamma_0 = z_b minus gamma_1 / s_b. Huang and colleagues set the selection parameters of their simulation the same way, by solving two publication probability equations for studies of 20 and 500 patients in a selection equation written on the square root of the sample size; the closed form above, for the equation in 1 / s, is derived. The copas function of metasens chooses its grid of gamma_0 and gamma_1 to cover a range of publication probabilities for the study with the largest standard error, and repeating the calculation over pairs of probabilities builds the selection columns of the article's scenario table. The adjusted effect at each pair needs the conditional maximum likelihood fit of the copas software and is not computed here."; HEO defines Copas Model as "The Copas model is a selection model for publication bias in meta-analysis that re-estimates the pooled effect under assumed rates of non-publication.".

column2: HFMA net days in accounts receivable from three monthly net revenues and their calendar days
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Days in Accounts Receivable. The module describes HFMA net days in accounts receivable from three monthly net revenues and their calendar days as "Takes the net patient receivables at the end of a quarter, the net patient service revenue of each of its three months and the months themselves, and returns the calendar days of the quarter, its revenue, average daily net revenue and net days in accounts receivable. It counts the actual days of the three months, as HFMA MAP Key FM-1 requires, and then applies HE-FM-DAR-001, so its inputs are monthly ledger figures rather than the single R and D of the formula. The R and Python code take the last month reported and find the month lengths themselves, leap years included."; HEO defines Days in Accounts Receivable as "Days in accounts receivable (AR days) is a provider's net receivables divided by average daily net patient revenue, giving days of revenue still unpaid.".

column2: Computational function for HTMT ratios of every construct pair from an indicator correlation matrix
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Discriminant Validity. The module describes Computational function for HTMT ratios of every construct pair from an indicator correlation matrix as "Computes the heterotrait-monotrait ratio of Eq. 6 of Henseler, Ringle and Sarstedt for every pair of constructs from a full indicator correlation matrix with any number of indicators per construct, and flags the pairs above 0.85 and above 0.90. For each pair it divides the mean of the block of correlations between the two constructs' indicators by the geometric mean of the two within-construct means of the off-diagonal correlations; the two-indicator case is HE-FM-DISV-001. The site calculator has no matrices, so the Math / Code line writes the case of three indicators against two term by term, and the loops over pairs are in the Excel, R and Python code. The bootstrap test of the ratio against 1 that the authors also propose needs respondent-level data and is not implemented here."; HEO defines Discriminant Validity as "Discriminant validity is evidence that a health measure correlates less with measures of other constructs than with its own, as predicted in advance.".

column2: Computational function for the best package of whole programmes by enumerating every package within the budget
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Integer Programming. The module describes Computational function for the best package of whole programmes by enumerating every package within the budget as "Takes the names, budget costs and QALY gains of any number of independent programmes, a budget and the names of any programmes a rule requires to be funded, checks every one of the 2^n packages of whole programmes, and returns the best package that fits the budget and includes the required programmes, with its cost, its QALYs and the number of packages that qualify. Run once without and once with the required programmes, it gives the health forgone to the rule, the explicit cost of equity that Stinnett and Paltiel describe and the opportunity cost of an equity constraint that Epstein and colleagues estimate. The inputs are lists of programmes, not the scalar inputs of HE-FM-IPH-001. The Math / Code line shows four programmes with programme 4 required, and the R and Python versions take any number of programmes and any required set."; HEO defines Integer Programming as "Integer programming chooses which indivisible health programmes or medicines to fund to maximise health gain, such as QALYs, within a fixed budget.".

column2: Computational function for Erlang B refusals, beds for a refusal target and cost-minimising beds
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Capacity Planning. The module describes Computational function for Erlang B refusals, beds for a refusal target and cost-minimising beds as "Takes a ward's arrival rate per day, its mean stay, a refusal target and the yearly cost of a staffed bed and of a refused admission, and returns the Erlang loss probability, refusals a year and achieved occupancy for every number of beds up to a ceiling, the smallest number of beds that meets the refusal target and the number of beds that minimises the total cost of beds and refusals. It computes the loss probability of HE-FM-CAPP-001 for any number of beds by the Erlang B recursion B_0 = 1, B_k = a B_(k-1) / (k + a B_(k-1)), which avoids the large powers and factorials of the direct formula, and its target and cost inputs differ from the formula's symbols. The total cost of N beds is c_b N plus c_r times the refusals at N beds, and one more bed is worth adding while the refusals it avoids, times c_r, exceed c_b. Because each extra bed avoids fewer refusals than the one before, the first bed that fails this test marks the cost minimum (derived; it follows from the strict convexity of the loss function in the number of beds that Tuenter reports from Jagers and van Doorn, and a grid check of 75 cases found no exception). The calculator line writes the recursion out for six beds and returns the net saving of the sixth bed; the searches over N are in the Excel, R and Python code."; HEO defines Capacity Planning as "Capacity planning estimates the beds, staff, theatre time and equipment a health service needs to meet expected demand to a stated standard of access.".

column2: Computational function for MCDA totals, ranking and a health gain weight scan for three technologies
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept MCDA in HTA. The module describes Computational function for MCDA totals, ranking and a health gain weight scan for three technologies as "Takes the health gain of three technologies with the fixed range of that criterion, their scores on two further criteria and the swing points of the three criteria, and returns each technology's health gain score by HE-FM-MCDH-001, the weights and overall values by HE-FM-MCDH-002, and the highest overall value. Its inputs are raw performance on the first criterion rather than the partial values of HE-FM-MCDH-002. The R and Python code also rank the technologies, scan the health gain weight on a grid of 101 values, 0, 0.01 and so on up to 1, with the other two weights kept in the ratio of their points, and return, for each pair of technologies, the weight at which their overall values are equal. Each total is linear in that weight, so this weight takes the form of the switching weight w_s of HE-FM-WE-004, which that record computes only for the QALYs of two groups, here with the other-criteria blend in place of group A QALYs and the health gain score less that blend in place of group B QALYs (derived). It marks a change of ranking only when it is at least 0 and at most 1; a value below 0 or above 1 means the pair keeps the same order at every feasible weight, and a pair with equal slopes either never ties or, with equal totals, ties at every weight (derived). Equal overall values are reported as ties, with no rule to break them."; HEO defines MCDA in HTA as "MCDA in HTA uses multi-criteria decision analysis to appraise health technologies on explicit, often weighted, criteria such as health gain and severity.".

column2: Computational function for the second-best menu against shut-down and complete information with an outside option
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Mechanism Design. The module describes Computational function for the second-best menu against shut-down and complete information with an outside option as "Compares three policies for a purchaser buying from a supplier whose unit cost is theta_L with probability nu or theta_H otherwise, when both types have an outside option U_0 at least zero. Under complete information each type produces its first-best output and is paid its cost plus U_0. The second-best menu of HE-FM-MECH-002 pays the high-cost type its cost plus U_0 and the low-cost type its cost plus U_0 plus the rent (theta_H minus theta_L) q_H. Shutting out the high-cost type serves only the low-cost type at first-best output with no information rent. The purchaser takes the better of the two incentive-feasible policies, which is (2.32) of Laffont and Martimort, and the gap to the complete-information payoff measures what the hidden cost costs the purchaser (derived). The second-best output does not depend on U_0, so a large outside option makes shut-down optimal even when (2.28) has a positive solution."; HEO defines Mechanism Design as "Mechanism design uses game theory to set rules, such as auctions, tenders or matching schemes, under which self-interested choices serve a chosen goal.".

column2: Computational function for every equilibrium of a 2 x 2 game with the outcome probabilities and expected welfare of mixed play
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Nash Equilibrium. The module describes Computational function for every equilibrium of a 2 x 2 game with the outcome probabilities and expected welfare of mixed play as "Lists every equilibrium of a two-player game with two strategies each and values the outcome of mixed play, the procedure Slantchev sets out for finding all Nash equilibria, checking first for pure-strategy solutions and then for mixed ones. The pure cells come from HE-FM-NASH-001 and the completely mixed equilibrium from HE-FM-NASH-002. Under independent mixing each cell's probability is the product of the two players' probabilities, the pathway probability of HE-FM-CHN-002, and the expected payoffs and the expected value of an outcome measure W over the four cells are probability-weighted sums, the form of HE-FM-CHN-001. At the mixed equilibrium each player's expected payoff can be read from its first strategy alone, because both of its strategies pay the same (derived from the indifference condition). The probabilities, payoffs and E_W apply only when interior is 1."; HEO defines Nash Equilibrium as "A Nash equilibrium is a set of strategies, one per player, from which no player, such as a payer, provider or patient, gains by changing strategy alone.".

column2: Computational function for one tender under both pricing rules and a seeded check of the uniform-cost closed forms
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Auction Theory. The module describes Computational function for one tender under both pricing rules and a seeded check of the uniform-cost closed forms as "Runs one tender under both pricing rules and checks the closed forms of HE-FM-AUCT-001 and HE-FM-AUCT-002 by simulating many tenders with a fixed seed. In one tender the second-price rule pays the winner the second-lowest cost, since every supplier bids its cost, and the first-price rule pays the lowest equilibrium bid. The lowest of the bids is the min form used for observed prices in HE-FM-BOC-003, and the scalar line writes the second-lowest of three costs as the median of three. The simulation draws N uniform costs per tender, sorts them, and averages the lowest cost, the second-lowest cost and the winning first-price bid, which converge to E_c1, E_p and E_b."; HEO defines Auction Theory as "Auction theory in health economics studies how bidding rules in tenders set the price and supply of medicines, vaccines and medical equipment.".

column2: Computational function for two-step floating catchment area scores, mean and spread for any number of sites
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Geographic Accessibility of Healthcare. The module describes Computational function for two-step floating catchment area scores, mean and spread for any number of sites as "Takes the GPs or other capacity of any number of provider locations, the populations of any number of residential locations, the matrix of travel times between them and a threshold, and returns each provider's supply ratio, each location's 2SFCA score, the population-weighted mean of the scores and their population-weighted variance, scaled to a stated number of people. It applies HE-FM-ACCS-001 to every provider and location at once, with SUMPRODUCT over a travel-time block in Excel and matrix operations in R, so its inputs are a matrix and two lists rather than the formula's named scalars. The mean is the check that the scores conserve total supply, and the variance, the population-weighted second moment that HE-VR-HINQ-007 takes over ranks, here taken over scores, is Wang 2012's equation 4, the inequality objective of Wang and Tang, divided by the total population (derived). The calculator line repeats the chain for the article's two practices and three neighbourhoods and adds the mean and variance; any other size is in the Excel, R and Python code."; HEO defines Geographic Accessibility of Healthcare as "Accessibility is the dimension of health care access concerned with how easily people can reach services, given location, travel time, distance and cost.".

column2: Computational function for gravity accessibility scores, mean and spread for any number of sites
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Geographic Accessibility of Healthcare. The module describes Computational function for gravity accessibility scores, mean and spread for any number of sites as "Takes the capacities of any number of provider locations, the populations of any number of residential locations, the matrix of travel times between them and a friction coefficient, and returns each provider's demand potential, each location's gravity score and the population-weighted mean and variance of the scores, scaled to a stated number of people. It applies HE-FM-ACCS-002 to every provider and location at once, so its inputs are a matrix and two lists rather than the formula's named scalars; the mean and variance are as in HE-CF-ACCS-001. The calculator line repeats the chain for the article's two practices and three neighbourhoods; any other size is in the Excel, R and Python code."; HEO defines Geographic Accessibility of Healthcare as "Accessibility is the dimension of health care access concerned with how easily people can reach services, given location, travel time, distance and cost.".

column2: Computational function for Sullivan active life expectancy with its standard error over any number of age bands
column24: The module lists this computational function on the formulae page of the HEO concept Active Life Expectancy. The module describes Computational function for Sullivan active life expectancy with its standard error over any number of age bands as "Takes a period life table's survivors at the starting age and person-years by age band, the dependency prevalence measured in each band and the number of survey respondents behind each prevalence, and returns active life expectancy, life expectancy, expected dependent years, the active share, the standard error of active life expectancy and a normal 95% interval, for any number of bands. The point estimate is HE-FM-ALE-001. The variance is the standard estimator Imai and Soneji print as their equation 13, the sum over bands of pi_i (1 minus pi_i) L_i squared over N_i, divided by l_x squared; each band's term takes the form of the squared standard error of HE-FM-BINOM-004, with survey respondents in place of that record's patients, times the squared weight L_i over l_x (derived), so the bands are treated as independent binomial samples and the survey respondents N_i are inputs the formula does not hold. For the 1999 United States population with an activities of daily living definition, Imai and Soneji report 14.31 years at 65 with a 95% interval of 14.24 to 14.37 when the death rates are treated as known. The calculator line writes three bands out term by term; the loops over bands are in the Excel, R and Python code."; HEO defines Active Life Expectancy as "Active life expectancy (ALE) is the average number of years a person of a given age can expect to live free of dependency in activities of daily living.".
